body.title: Too White For Dirt - SMAP 267
body.body:
I don’t know if it’s just me, but whenever I visit a place, *I’m not only visiting the place.* I’m also checking out the environment, looking around to see if there’s anything worth capturing on camera. 

I can’t remember how many times I’ve done this. Do I even need to count? Original photos are part of my content here on Hive, so what am I even saying? Lol. 

***
Last Friday, I accompanied a colleague to an abattoir on Nsulu Street, off Mosque Street, here in my city. She had taken some meat there to be dried — one of the services they offer alongside the selling of meat. Busy spot, unfortunately, I had no idea such a place existed. 

While we waited for her package, I looked up and saw a flamingo perched on the brick watertank stanchion. It stood tall and still, head turning slowly, clearly scouting. Probably watching for scraps or small prey. Perched on the water pipe, its back towards the flamingo, was also a cooper’s hawk. 


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmR35bV4NixnpTa9sCm88G8EgixEf8ktTj6V6fdAM8D95o/1000256021.jpg 




***

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcfZkZH877mghTJvwZtbyt9egZX3Y5vRCSFVzGxi5VbBG/1776628623839.jpg)


Seeing the flamingo in such an environment got me thinking again: why do flamingos associate with dirt? For a bird that white, you’d expect it to avoid dirt altogether.  But flamingos don’t care. Lagoon, dump, abattoir,  muddy, dirty pools of water — if there’s food, they’re in.

> Isn't white supposed to be elegant and spotless?

Some I see here even follow a herd of cattle, perched on their backs, picking insects off their bodies. Seriously, the bird looks too clean for the places it chooses. Lol. 

I guess that’s just their nature. Survival doesn’t care about color - if there’s food, they’ll go. Clean or dirty doesn’t matter.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVRR4N8YoGqUnPJygmoSvrMFmHUCVp49FvuxmUq4U5P29/1776628624055.jpg)


 > Ironical, isn't it? 

Well, nature doesn’t follow our ideas of what’s “fitting.” It just is! 


***
**Author's Photos.**

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZuavB1TQ4H4UZnrridAehLxZjNowSUYK7oFXXXdCBNmQ/1000013948.png)

body.title: When I lose my mind :)
body.body:
I am writing this post with gratitude @sunscape because she drew my attention on soil pH and nutrients.
To make matters worse for this gardener, I know of some more traditional ways to test soil pH and I armed myself with a faster soil pH tester.
As soon as it arrived, I tested it and also checked the garden itself, because I fertilized it.I did the testing itself a month ago.
The thing is that a few years ago I planted three chokeberry bushes.
One took root, it bloomed and bore fruit.
The other one immediately dried up.
And with them the matter was resolved.
But the third one, planted next to this chokeberry that bore fruit, suffered from yellowing leaves. Well, it started well but quickly turned yellow.

And I decided to transplant it from that place.And I did that, but unfortunately I didn't test the soil.
Probably because I tested, fertilized and got good pH and fertility in this entire part of my garden.Only that place where that chokeberry is is a meter from the garden.
And I forgot about it, it slipped my mind. I was fighting a battle with winter, frost and who knows what else.In the previous post where I took a picture of that chokeberry and expressed my concern about the leaves @sunscape it got my attention to check the soil acidity and nutrients .
And then the light came on.
Tested, confirmed.
![20260418_181414.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKbF6fk1QwXKA53fNg4ryzzgKir6FB1FyDN2zT19kyYF3LcbpXECVfB844Y4oUP.jpg)

I took some wood ash and sprinkled it around the plant and immediately dug it in with a hoe.
![20260418_191050.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKJ1HpWeTiPjNZaZ1MryBEPTvvyVc9sZicM7AQfUTtyauxYbyQydzbmxY1dnv6M.jpg)



![20260418_191340.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKVVT5DeAgqJ7xGmUt7vHcJ4EuAZ6g3M8tRp9jJ8X1XHnVDT7cv5ZabMZvcxdG5.jpg)
I'm also collecting eggshells now, which I need to dry and grind.

I know it's not a quick fix and will take some time
Do you know of any other natural ways to fix soil pH?
---

Thanks for reading.
Until next time.
Stay healthy.
Markone85.

body.title: Chicken with creamy greek yogurt sauce [ENG/ESP]
body.body:
>
![post hive (78).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23y96dRPdu5BxgiFcfWWhmRQHr5AKQ9wrSXK4B915ZM95EYW5aLPPe4DMJwCEGWFeYfhb.png)
--- It’s the last day of the week, and I’ve completed my challenge to share recipes. It’s definitely been a lot of work—you have no idea how much time it takes to find recipes that fit my budget, the ingredients, the quantities… but anyway, here we are, doing the best we can with what we have. Today I’m bringing you a delicious chicken dish with a creamy sauce made with Greek yogurt. It’s the first time I’ve made it, and honestly, I really liked it. As I always say, it’s a different kind of meal, with a unique flavor, and it’s very tasty. ## Ingredients: - Chopped chicken - Seasonings (Worcestershire sauce, pepper, adobo, salt) - 2 tablespoons Greek yogurt - 1 tablespoon mustard - Chicken broth - 1 tablespoon honey - 1 small onion - Garlic --- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23w2m8RtMWGTwRaHZvhzuWVrzAUmFerDejrLoV18pvw3rSgYsdVhyK4s2aSqkQ6QF3FXe.png) |![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23vhyaAhWeKEDD3Tax5Y7g95pRoukXXMLhpJEBKkafWYns1NDYCVFN8xVpfNjeojNkjv5.png) |-|-| ## Preparation: To prepare this chicken, the first thing we’ll do is marinate it for cooking with a little Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper, a pinch of turmeric, and seasoning. We’ll put it in the skillet and let it cook for a while.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/Eoc7vLBy8YndrzyZXe4vv6B5VY5z4JwGzYy7tBDMPrUzX3p1zAq4EYP6a8KthBzyLja.png)
## For the sauce: While the chicken is cooking, let’s prepare the sauce. In this case, take the onion and chop it into small pieces. I read that it’s best to put the yogurt in a separate bowl before adding it to the pan, so that’s what I did. I added the two tablespoons, along with the mustard and honey, and separately, I took a little broth from the chicken and added it.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoeEQSVbvL6rYuewQCqKvYEEhRgaKmwWjfZswCQ2zTFToYR9zzPiDbqjq5vxJ3yGwky.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGvwYz9mqRqopb1ZoPTTmYUVjcRu5iPAjzundFH8KUYAPUGDRjgp1tnaU4YPnjfzoL.png) |![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoChcynWFNMD57xbtzErQMW34sNVuZ5DHahfU9KzQtQBe5MkLH36Vt9qh3UpVG6BVpH.png) |-|-| Now that this is ready, put the onion and garlic in a skillet and sauté them a bit, then add the yogurt mixture, so it looks like this. 👇
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGxsiVebbrZ1k4aLtsy3CqRB4S7WrCV8mFLuAtRF9SHXNzijjcwpy9YnyuoCEitT2U.png)
Once the chicken is ready, we’ll add our cream and let it cook for a few more minutes.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/Eo4CvSH4UNCDLApSmGLTgrP8Tms7Bwg2YBCdEr2PN58513fEfVsk81WTa69fFX7u4Am.png)
And that’s how our delicious chicken turns out, served with this mashed potato. You can eat it with whatever you like.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoyRyWTdp2GcHh43Czzdyqzy3rY52zmtXPeU8VX32CkdV63M613WMkEt8DcZnt2b8pH.png)
That wraps up this week’s recipes—we’ll see what we come up with for the new week. Thank you all for your continued support. Have a great weekend and a great start to the week. 😍 ---
SPANISH VERSION

Ultimo día de la semana, cumplida mi reto de compartir recetas, sin duda ha sido un gran esfuerzo, no saben lo que toma tiempo, buscar recetas que se amolden a mi presupuesto, los ingredientes, la cantidad, en fin, pero bueno, aquí seguimos, haciendo lo que podemos con lo que tenemos. Hoy les traigo un rico pollo con una salsa cremosa, con yogurt griego, primera vez que lo hago, y de verdad, me gusto mucho, como siempre digo, un menú diferente, con un sabor distinto, y muy rico. ## Ingredientes: - Pollo picado - Condimentos (salsa inglesa, pimienta, adobo, sal) - 2 cucharadas de yogurt griego - 1 cucharada de mostaza - caldo de pollo - 1 cucharada de miel - 1 cebolla pequeña - Ajo --- ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23w2m8RtMWGTwRaHZvhzuWVrzAUmFerDejrLoV18pvw3rSgYsdVhyK4s2aSqkQ6QF3FXe.png)|![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/23vhyaAhWeKEDD3Tax5Y7g95pRoukXXMLhpJEBKkafWYns1NDYCVFN8xVpfNjeojNkjv5.png) |-|-| ## Preparación: Para la preparación de este pollo, lo primero que haremos es adobarlo para cocinarlo, con un poco de salsa inglesa, sal, pimienta, un toque de cúrcuma y adobo. Lo llevamos al sarten, y allí lo dejamos cocinar un rato.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/Eoc7vLBy8YndrzyZXe4vv6B5VY5z4JwGzYy7tBDMPrUzX3p1zAq4EYP6a8KthBzyLja.png)
## Para la crema: Mientras el pollo se cocina, vamos a ir preparando la crema, en este caso, tomamos la cebolla, y la picamos en trozos pequeños. Leí que para que el yogurt lo mas recomendable es colocarlo en un bol aparte, antes de llevarlo al sarten, así lo hice, añadí las dos cucharadas, junto con la mostaza, la miel, y aparte, le saque un poquito de caldo al pollo y se lo agregue.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoeEQSVbvL6rYuewQCqKvYEEhRgaKmwWjfZswCQ2zTFToYR9zzPiDbqjq5vxJ3yGwky.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGvwYz9mqRqopb1ZoPTTmYUVjcRu5iPAjzundFH8KUYAPUGDRjgp1tnaU4YPnjfzoL.png)|![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoChcynWFNMD57xbtzErQMW34sNVuZ5DHahfU9KzQtQBe5MkLH36Vt9qh3UpVG6BVpH.png) |-|-| Ya con esto listo, en un sarten vamos a poner la cebolla con el ajo, que se sofríe un poco, y luego le colocamos la mezcla del yogurt, quedando de esta manera. 👇
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGxsiVebbrZ1k4aLtsy3CqRB4S7WrCV8mFLuAtRF9SHXNzijjcwpy9YnyuoCEitT2U.png)
Listo el pollo, le vamos agregar entonces nuestra crema, dejamos cocinar unos minutos mas.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/Eo4CvSH4UNCDLApSmGLTgrP8Tms7Bwg2YBCdEr2PN58513fEfVsk81WTa69fFX7u4Am.png)
Y así nos quedaría nuestro rico pollo, acompañado de este puré, ustedes pueden comerlo con lo que gusten.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoyRyWTdp2GcHh43Czzdyqzy3rY52zmtXPeU8VX32CkdV63M613WMkEt8DcZnt2b8pH.png)
Así cerramos esta semana de recetas, veremos que se nos ocurre para esta nueva semana. Gracias a todos por su apoyo siempre, feliz fin de semana, e inicio. 😍

body.title: My Hive Strategy - Why I choose powering up at this point of time?
body.body:
Hello everyone,
How are you all? I hope everyone is fine and doing great in their life.

When I joined Hive blockchain, I was just 20 years old. At that time, my main goal was to earn money because I was in college. I wanted to support myself with my expenses and also help my father financially. Like many beginners, I was looking for quick income.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTBLceFwXXHfPytVdKCTBRiUzE7N24VW57aXAcJ9am8Sy/image.png)


But as time passed, my mindset started changing. I realized that long term profit is not about earning quickly. It is about building your Hive power and growing your account over time.

Today, I want to share how my thinking changed over the last five years. I have spent almost five years on Hive, so I have seen different phases of the market.

I will be honest. In the beginning, and for a long time, my focus was almost 100% on earning money. But I never followed a path where I powered down everything just to cash out quickly. From the start, I believed in the future of Hive blockchain.

body.title: Sunday Walk in Ikole-Ekiti: Red Millipedes Everywhere Since The Rains Started
body.body:
Greetings Ecencyals and Hivers, I hope your Sunday is going great.

I had no plans to draw or work on comic pages today. Instead I took a walk around Ikole-Ekiti to clear my head and just observe.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTJpeccnnsHS7psvhkgL1FD2ewE564NzkXDnkZybJ3Zbr/1776621820127.jpg)

The main thing I kept running into was this red “100-legged” millipede. They’ve been showing up a lot more since the rains started. You’ll find them under grasses, crawling on walls, or tucked beside rocks like these ones.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUP7eZTt8Gybo7nf2NcUHTdgCyagG5HtneBf68AoUF7gK/1776621945346.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaGkjVsfWKwNNZrbDq936JvzckVHRnp5kkHs95LSoAQmg/1776621945533.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQAP91Vp3PbofQbsnQGgL7grDWyp3rQBb5AyqnvN1UJJq/1776621945699.jpg)


I was lucky to catch these three together. Two of them looked like they were mating, so I tried not to disturb them. I probably shifted the light or got too close because I flinched, but they hadn’t separated when I walked away. The third one was just off to the side, doing its own thing.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVK4jAZWQtaPbbtqF8ZoFZtM8tunyBoiPEY8x1T9ocb38/1776622094110.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTZkLYVDwCviZWwTbfeHU8RK5tmQngjaoF4Xhk7qL61eN/1776622276143.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmScWejhRsG8L66uRffhSakU6uU9zPgHzETqkdNw5oKPF4/1776622276338.jpg)

The red and black bands on them are so sharp. They move slow but deliberate. You can see all the little legs working if you crouch down and watch. They curl into a spiral when they feel threatened, but these ones seemed comfortable.

Millipedes aren’t harmful. They don’t bite or sting. They’re just out here breaking down dead leaves and helping the soil. The rain draws them out — wet ground makes it easier for them to move and find mates, I think.

No art or process post today. Just me, my phone, and a quiet moment with these guys before heading back in. 

Have a nice week guys. Thanks for viewing❤️

Hola, he estado desconectada por acá desde que hice CAF 2026. La razón? más allá de una lesión, solo quise tomarme una pausa necesaria. Y vuelvo dando un poco de contexto sobre lo que ha pasado estas 10 semanas.

El día del maratón fui con precaución, ya que venia con una molestia a nivel de la cadera derecha, que irradiaba hacia la pierna, lo cual hacía que no apoyara del todo bien esta pierna, la misma molestia que tuve a semanas de CAF 2025 se repitió a 3 semanas de CAF 2026. La molestia se iba luego de unos tantos kilómetros, en el caso de CAF 2026 se fue desde el km 12, sin embargo, sabía que debía darle con cuidado para no hacerme daño y porque sabía que había una probabilidad de que no pudiera completar el maratón, dependiendo de cómo me sintiera durante el resto del recorrido. Finalmente me mantuve a un paso tranquilo pero seguro y pude llegar bien a meta, sin dolor en la cadera, ni en la pierna, ni otro lugar. 

Pensaba que todo había salido muy bien, pero al día siguiente y toda esa semana post maratón estuve con mucho dolor al apoyar mi pierna derecha, literal estuve cojeando toda la semana, esa misma semana decidí ir a un traumatólogo que me recomendó un buen compañero del Team y qué bien que lo hice. Este Dr a diferencia del Dr con el que me vi el año pasado, más allá de pedirme un Rx de cadera, me pidió una resonancia magnética, Rx panorámica de columna y de miembros inferiores. Diagnóstico? Tengo el ángulo de wiberg de mi cadera derecha en el límite para displasia de cadera, debido a la molestia que tenía y no apoyar del todo bien mi pierna derecha, por compensación tuve una fractura por estrés en el cuerpo del pubis del lado izquierdo, también tengo mi pierna derecha 9.79 mm más corta que la izquierda. En medio de todo esto, afortunadamente, y parte de lo que quería descartar el Dr,  la zona donde se une el fémur con la cadera está bien, no he tenido desgaste ni lesión como tal en esa zona, para lo cual me dieron bastante tranquilidad en el sentido de que el protocolo a seguir para la recuperación sería mas sencillo. 

Debido a todo esto tuve que hacer una pausa de correr y cero ejercicios de impacto por 7 semanas, tiempo que permitiría la recuperación de la fractura que tuve, lo más loco es que ahí como tal nunca tuve dolor, siempre fue en la pierna derecha y a la altura de la cadera justo donde se une el fémur con la cadera. Me mandaron a hacer rehabilitación y mandarme a hacer una plantillas para correr, además de enfocarme sí o sí en el fortalecimiento, ya que necesito crear músculo suficiente y mejorar mi mecánica para estabilizar mejor mi cadera.

Hoy, a 10 semanas del maratón, afortunadamente me he venido sintiendo mucho mejor, estas 10 semanas se resumen en un descanso activo que necesitaba, entre  muchas caminatas y rehabilitación, a 6 semanas me dieron permiso de retomar el power bike, a 7 semanas me dieron permiso de hacer 2 min de trote suave y 1 min de caminata durante 30 minutos, a las 8 semanas hice mis primeros 30 min suaves continuos, a las 9 semanas ya estaba haciendo mis primeros 5K suaves continuos, y esta semana: 1) comencé a entrenar en un nuevo lugar para hacer fortalecimiento, ya estoy haciendo la transición entre mi fisio y este nuevo lugar, solo me queda una sesión de rehabilitación y estoy lista; 2) comencé nuevamente con mi plan de entrenamiento con mi coach de running, haciendo 40 min de trote suave martes y jueves y hoy domingo hice mis primeros 50 min de trote suave continuo, estrenando mis plantillas ya que me las entregaron este viernes. 

De aquí en adelante solo queda seguir avanzando, haciendo lo necesario, ahora el fortalecimiento y el uso de las plantillas se convertirán en mi no negociable para poder seguir haciendo lo que me gusta, recuperarme bien y volver bien. Ya iré reportando por acá mucho más de este proceso. Gracias si llegaste hasta aquí! 😊

body.title: What I Am Watching This Week
body.body:
## What I’m Watching This Week

This week is packed with major developments across semiconductors, AI, and earnings season. From standout results by TSMC and ASML to Amazon’s aggressive AI push, there is a lot happening right now that could shape the next leg of the market.

### TSMC delivers outstanding results

TSMC reported excellent results yesterday, reinforcing the idea that demand for AI chips continues to grow rapidly.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmToTBqipkwpjFDPVBapurZAPWErxCDSB3sM3Dd39KgN8C/image.png)


Here is what the latest trailing twelve month figures show:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeFzoPimTaNK4fLJG8xsLx6ev1LRGBEmvLESma94wQbHq/image.png)


Revenue reached **$128.5 billion**, with a **18.7% CAGR**.
Earnings per share rose **82.6%**, with a **20.4% CAGR**.
Free cash flow per share increased **92.5%**, with a **22.3% CAGR**.
Profit margins also continue to improve.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNWigkrYXG7GsoWeU8ZHwMUobmnFmGcArKSQbicRNRAqd/image.png)


The company is executing at an extremely high level, and the stock’s performance over the last year reflects that, rising **139%**.

From a valuation perspective, TSMC is trading at a **forward EV/EBIT of 16.8**, slightly above its average of 15. Still, with growth this strong and margins continuing to expand, that premium looks fully justified, at least in my view.

### ASML posts another huge quarter

ASML also released very strong first quarter 2026 results and once again beat expectations.

The key numbers were impressive:

Revenue came in at **€8.77 billion**, up **13.3% year over year**, beating estimates by **€110 million**.
GAAP EPS came in at **€7.15**, beating expectations by **€0.54**.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQSyKX4PW9XE31HyJtm3khq28fijvyyiE8uhguuYzYYV6/image.png)


Its full year 2026 guidance remains strong:

Total net sales are expected to reach **€36 to €40 billion**.
Gross margin is expected to come in between **51% and 53%**.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSkNco8xJVHwyKVrC9L1pTEuwnSEPv4UuYJK2aGJcBvVv/image.png)


ASML is also continuing to reward shareholders. The company announced a total **2025 dividend of €7.50 per share**, up **17% from 2024**. During Q1 2026, it also repurchased around **0.9 million shares** worth **€1.1 billion**.

ASML continues to dominate the semiconductor equipment space, and shareholders have every reason to be happy with the trend.

### Sandisk joins the Nasdaq-100

Another big development this week is Sandisk officially joining the **Nasdaq-100** in the latest major index rebalancing, replacing Atlassian.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZQmzDPCMswLCRZbW9buvgZzbePb5859ZFMvHwHZMbw5w/image.png)


The growth story here is eye-catching:

Revenue is expected to rise from **$8.9 billion today** to **$27.6 billion by 2027**.
The stock is already up **2,564% in one year**.
It is currently trading at **$851**.

Everything points to strong years ahead for Sandisk. The company that helped transform the world of SSDs and flash memory is now entering the elite group of the 100 largest technology companies in America.

### Amazon is going all in on AI

Amazon is also firmly on my radar this week.

CEO Andy Jassy made it pretty clear that being bearish on AI at this point is a mistake. More importantly, Amazon is backing that view with real numbers and enormous capital commitments.

A few highlights stand out:

Amazon’s chips business now has an **annual run rate above $20 billion**.
The company plans to invest **$200 billion in capex in 2026**, mainly focused on AWS, with signed customer agreements already in place and very strong demand for AI workloads.
Jassy believes those investments should begin paying off quickly, especially in **2027 and 2028**.

On top of that, Amazon announced a new **$25 billion investment in data centers in Mississippi**, expected to create **2,000 new jobs** while also supporting renewable energy initiatives.

The stock has gained more than **13% over the last week**, and analysts believe it could move above **$280 over the next 12 months**.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRrf9P6zW79eCaJpSNJUNtr67BjLeRMj9uy7ucU4GvMqJ/image.png)


Personally, I am more bullish than ever on Amazon.

### Earnings season is heating up

We are now officially moving deeper into **earnings season**.

Last week marked the beginning of the **Q1 2026 earnings season**, led by the major banks, and on average the results were very strong. This week the calendar gets even more interesting, with several important companies reporting.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmetRzYdLDXrSnYUg9u2ux7Mp7hKn6oLtFPP5g766FsDZA/image.png)


Here is the lineup I am watching:

**Tuesday:** UNH, GE
**Wednesday:** VRT, GEV, BA, TSLA, NOW, IBM, LRCX, TXN
**Thursday:** LMT, AXP, INTC
**Friday:** PG

Tesla is obviously one of the biggest names to watch, as it will be the first of the Magnificent 7 to report. ServiceNow is also especially interesting, because its results may give us more insight into the whole **SaaSapocalypse** narrative.

Overall, this is shaping up to be an important week, and in general, expectations are pointing toward a solid quarter for US corporate earnings.


**AI demand remains extremely strong, semiconductor leaders keep delivering, Amazon is accelerating its AI bet, and earnings season could give us the next big signal for the market.**

Viajar a Campeonato Sudamericano de Trail y Montaña 2026 en Samaipata fue, sin duda, una de las experiencias más bonitas y significativas que he vivido como atleta. No solo fue una competencia, fue una lección profunda que me dejó la montaña, porque sí, la montaña te habla… y tienes que aprender a escucharla.

Me encontré con un nivel altísimo, con corredores de toda Sudamérica que llegaron preparados para darlo todo. La ruta fue sumamente técnica, exigente desde el inicio. El ascenso fue brutal, muy fuerte, de esos que te ponen a prueba no solo las piernas, sino también la mente. Estar alrededor de los 1200 metros de altitud y enfrentar un desnivel positivo que alcanzaba aproximadamente los 1800 metros fue un reto enorme para mi respiración, para mi cuerpo y para mi fortaleza mental.

Durante la carrera me caí dos veces. La primera, logré levantarme rápido y continuar. Pero la segunda caída fue más dura, me frenó completamente y por un momento pensé en abandonar. Fue ahí cuando recordé las palabras de mi entrenador: “Si te caes, te levantas y sigues adelante”. Y eso hice.

No llegué de primera, llegué de última. Pero entendí algo muy importante: los últimos también tienen su lugar, porque son los que nunca se rinden. Esta experiencia no la veo como una derrota, sino como una oportunidad de aprendizaje, de crecimiento y de identificar en qué puedo mejorar para seguir avanzando.

Me voy feliz, agradecida y con el corazón lleno, orgullosa de haber representado a mi país y lista para seguir trabajando por lo que viene 💛 

Crea una vida que ames 

---

body.title: People Choose Their Own Place in Our Hearts
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma4JeMg365ZSN95PdBvnhjNqhQAX8Ggd7CTMs5vSdLiBE/1776629632210.jpg)

One evening I was sitting outside my house in the village. The sun was slowly going down, and the sky was turning orange. An old neighbor passed by and stopped for a moment. We exchanged a few simple words, but his kindness stayed in my mind for a long time. That day I realized something very simple about life.
We often think that we decide who deserves a place in our hearts. But the truth is a little different. Most of the time, people decide their own place in our hearts through their behavior, their character, and the way they deal with us.
Life teaches this lesson again and again.
Sometimes a person enters our life like a stranger. We do not expect much from them. But slowly, through small acts of kindness, honesty, and respect, they build a special place in our hearts. It does not happen in one day. It happens little by little, through actions.
On the other hand, there are people we once trusted deeply. We gave them respect and love. We believed they would always stand with us. But with time, their attitude changes. Their words hurt. Their actions show something different from what they once promised. And slowly, without making noise, they start losing their place in our hearts.
It is not anger that removes them. It is simply the realization.
I remember a small incident from my own life. A friend once borrowed something from me. It was not very expensive, but it meant something to me. Instead of returning it or even speaking honestly, he started avoiding me. Every time I met him, he made excuses. At that moment I understood something important. The issue was not the object. The real issue was the honesty behind it.
From that day, my respect for him quietly became smaller.
But life also shows the opposite side. Sometimes a person surprises us in a beautiful way. They help us when we least expect it. They stand with us when everyone else walks away. And suddenly we realize that this person has earned a permanent place in our hearts.
Respect, trust, and love cannot be demanded. They are built through character.
People often say words are important, but actions speak much louder. Someone may speak sweetly, but if their behavior is selfish or dishonest, the truth will appear sooner or later. And when it does, the place they once had in our hearts slowly disappears.
At the same time, even a quiet person who does not speak much can win hearts through sincerity and good character.
This is one of the simple but powerful rules of life.
No one forces anyone out of their heart. People walk out on their own through their actions. And in the same way, some people build a place in our hearts that stays there for years, sometimes even forever.
In the end, the truth is very clear.
The place someone holds in our heart is not given by our words. It is earned by their character.

body.title: ¿Por qué escribo novelas? (ESP-ENG)
body.body:
> 📗 Saludos, amigos de #literatos. Con gusto les comparto hoy unas reflexiones través de #ecency ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRXiPywT6AQGvqrnSoMcjgun76h4Qs8VLym4nFnmVwcrn/1776532098203.jpg)
***

> ¿Por qué escribo novelas? Escribo para que el tiempo no me mate sin haberlo interrogado. Escribo porque Faulkner me enseñó que el pasado ni siquiera es pasado. Llevo haciéndolo desde el año 2000. Veinteseis años ya. Una hoja de servicios manchada de tachones y madrugadas. No hay mérito en la cifra. Escribo porque soy incapaz de entender el mundo si no lo convierto en una frase. Flaubert buscaba le mot juste. Yo busco el silencio exacto que debe rodear a esa palabra. La verdad no se posee. Se persigue. Se rodea. Se acecha como el pez de Hemingway bajo el agua clara y fría. Mis novelas, incluso las inéditas como «El círculo musical del infierno» o «Prohibido morir en La Habana», son formas de acecho. Son mapas de una búsqueda que nunca termina. Por suerte. Escribo para interpretar voces. Virginia Woolf mostró que la conciencia es un río con muchos afluentes. En «El orden natural de las cosas» dejé que esas voces hablaran bajo la lluvia de La Habana. En «La nada infinita» las dejé gritar. No construyo argumentos. Construyo ecos. A veces el plano realista se quiebra y entra lo fantástico. No lo fuerzo. García Márquez me curó de la pedantería del realismo puro. Entendí que la muerte en el Caribe baila. Que la felicidad tiene la forma de un hielo derritiéndose en un vaso de aguardiente. Escribo para demorar la muerte. No para vencerla. Para demorarla. Mis personajes mueren mucho. O no pueden morir. «Prohibido morir en La Habana» nació de esa contradicción terrible: una ciudad donde la vitalidad es tan feroz que la muerte parece un acto de mala educación. Escribir sobre el final es mi manera de ensayar la despedida sin irme del todo. Bukowski escupía a la cara del abismo. Yo prefiero sentarme en el borde y describir el paisaje con la precisión quirúrgica de Auster. El azar y la fatalidad. Escribo para oír el agua. «El sonido del agua» sigue inédita. Es experimental porque me permito el fracaso. El agua lo borra todo menos el sonido de su caída. En el ruido del grifo o de la lluvia hay un ritmo anterior al lenguaje. A veces la prosa debe romperse para que se cuele ese sonido. Debemos escribir como quien se ahoga pero mantiene la calma. Con autoridad. Sin alardear. El texto debe sostenerse solo, como un vaso sobre una mesa coja. Equilibrio tenso. Conocimiento sutil de la gravedad. Escribo porque el silencio es un lujo que no puedo permitirme con tanto ruido dentro. Las novelas son mi manera de ordenar el caos. De darle una partitura al caos. «El círculo musical del infierno» trata de eso. De bajar al sótano con una linterna y un metrónomo. Mis influencias me dieron las llaves. Pero el sótano es mío. Los fantasmas que encuentro allí tienen mi cara. Llevo un cuarto de siglo escribiendo. ¿Para qué? Para que al final del día, si alguien lee «La nada infinita», sienta que la nada es un poco más soportable si está bien narrada. Para que la felicidad, cuando aparece en una página de «El orden natural de las cosas», sea verdadera. Escribo novelas porque no sé hacer otra cosa sin que me duela el alma. Y porque cuando escribo una oración corta y exacta, yuxtapuesta a otra, y la respiración del texto se detiene justo donde debe, sé que estoy vivo. Eso es todo. © Marabuzal, 2026. Todos los derechos reservados. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVDUKVA6YugQdRrhGACmnps8ddBkV8W6UwGEo9DwaNQxF/1768408479017.jpg)

> 📗 Greetings, friends of #literatos. I'm happy to share some reflections with you today through #ecency ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRXiPywT6AQGvqrnSoMcjgun76h4Qs8VLym4nFnmVwcrn/1776532098203.jpg)
***

>

**Why do I write novels?**

I write so that time doesn't kill me without me having questioned it. I write because Faulkner taught me that the past isn't even past. I've been doing it since 2000. Twenty-six years already. A record stained with crossed-out words and early mornings. There's no merit in the number.

 I write because I am incapable of understanding the world unless I condense it into a sentence. Flaubert sought the perfect word. I seek the precise silence that must surround that word. Truth is not possessed. It is pursued. It is circled. It is stalked like Hemingway's fish in the clear, cold water. My novels, even the unpublished ones like \

are forms of stalking.

They are maps of a search that never ends. Fortunately.

I write to interpret voices. Virginia Woolf showed that consciousness is a river with many tributaries. In \
I let those voices speak in the Havana rain. In \

I let them scream.

I don't construct arguments. I construct echoes.

Sometimes the realistic plane breaks down and the fantastic enters. I don't force it. García Márquez cured me of the pedantry of pure realism.  I understood that death in the Caribbean dances. That happiness takes the form of ice melting in a glass of rum.

I write to delay death. Not to conquer it. To delay it.

My characters die a lot. Or they can't die. \

was born from that terrible contradiction: a city where vitality is so fierce that death seems like an act of bad manners.

Writing about the end is my way of rehearsing farewell without leaving completely. Bukowski spat in the face of the abyss. I prefer to sit on the edge and describe the landscape with Auster's surgical precision.

Chance and fate.

I write to hear the water. \

remains unpublished. It's experimental because I allow myself to fail. Water erases everything except the sound of its fall. In the noise of the faucet or the rain, there is a rhythm that precedes language.  Sometimes prose must be broken so that sound can seep through. We must write like someone drowning but remaining calm. With authority. Without boasting. The text must stand on its own, like a glass on a wobbly table.

Tense equilibrium. Subtle awareness of gravity.

I write because silence is a luxury I can't afford with so much noise inside. Novels are my way of ordering chaos. Of giving chaos a score. \

is about that. About going down to the basement with a flashlight and a metronome. My influences gave me the keys. But the basement is mine. The ghosts I find there bear my face.

I've been writing for a quarter of a century.

Why?

So that at the end of the day, if someone reads \
they feel that nothingness is a little more bearable if it's well narrated. So that happiness, when it appears on a page of \

is real. I write novels because I don't know how to do anything else without it breaking my heart. And because when I write a short, precise sentence, juxtaposed with another, and the text's breath stops exactly where it should, I know I'm alive. That's all. (Google Translate). © Marabuzal, 2026. All rights reserved.

body.body:
https://youtu.be/m2f0PiWT0c0?si=b8gePIDNhal2p7JU

Happy Lord's Day brethren and trust we had a great day in God's presence today

Many at times when we cry and mourn for the loss of children who are not even up to teenagers, to know what sweetness lies in the world or the struggles one have to face or the challenges one have to overcome to become successful and have a story to tell at the end of the day and we begin to wonder what actually have they done to deserve dying at such a tender age as a child, when they could have lived long on earth, fulfilling destinies like the promises in the Bible.

But then, we have forgotten that we are told in the scripture, that both young and old stands before the throne on the day of judgement. So definitely, it has been established that it doesn't matter if we live long or not, but death isn't a respecter of anyone.

![1000637687.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/afrikens/EoeDWZTUYXjGwAvPSmmrUTPvkGNCyx2HPBB1QML5FfzbJjXz1SNd5veKprPwwyGeCLc.jpg)

We should realize how much God loves children that even made him use them as comparison or instances for admonishing the adults in living their lives so that they can inherit the kingdom of God. With this kind of love, then we should know that they are most precious and valuable to him, to not allow bad things happen to them if the scripture was not meant to be fulfilled.

Though, no one ever prays to die untimely or lose their children, but then I think the main prayer is, whenever it may be, we shall not lose eternal rest.

title.title: 🌆 Finding beauty in unexpected places
title.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPuLYmucS3qf5sFW24AdBx5dg5kMyNU2uepWpPV1852ZT/IMG_9638.PNG 

Not every place is meant to be beautiful…  
but sometimes, that’s exactly where inspiration hides.

Walking through spaces like this, with rough textures, worn surfaces, and imperfect details, I can’t help but see potential. As an architect, I’ve learned that beauty isn’t always about perfection — it’s about perspective.

A wall with peeling paint, a forgotten corner, a structure that seems abandoned… all of it tells a story. And somehow, those stories feel more real than the polished ones.

I think that’s what I want to do someday.

Not just create something new… but transform what already exists. Give meaning to spaces people overlook. Turn the ordinary into something that feels alive again.

Because architecture isn’t just about building.

It’s about seeing what others don’t.

**Diez Kilómetros de Amor y Perseverancia: Un Hito en Nuestro Viaje de Running**

Hola Runners paso por aquí a compartir mi última experiencia junto a mi mejor date. 

Empezamos con un ritmo cómodo, como lo muestra la captura de la aplicación Strava [Strava ](https://strava.app.link/3wDkGbGot2b). El primer tercio del camino fue un calentamiento controlado. Nos cruzábamos con otros corredores y familias, cada uno en su propio mundo, compartiendo el espacio verde. El atardecer pronto se convirtió en noche, y la iluminación artificial del parque cobró vida. Se puede ver a mi pareja, sonriente en un selfie nocturno, luciendo su camiseta azul y naranja de Gatorade. Su expresión es de determinación, a pesar de que la fatiga aún no había hecho su aparición estelar. En el fondo de la imagen, la estructura iluminada con el nombre de \

le daba un toque especial a la locación de nuestro hito.\n​Los primeros kilómetros pasaron con relativa facilidad, con la charla habitual y la compañía mutua como principal motivación. Sin embargo, a medida que nos acercábamos a la marca de los 8 kilómetros, la realidad del esfuerzo comenzó a pasar factura. Fue un momento crítico. En su rostro, la sonrisa se había transformado en un rictus de concentración y lucha, pero esta vez con su mano haciendo el signo de la paz, un gesto que más tarde interpretaría como un \

y no una celebración prematura. Se notaba el cansancio, la respiración entrecortada, el sudor brillando bajo las luces.\n​Fue entonces cuando la duda asomó. Estábamos a solo 2 kilómetros del objetivo, pero para él, esos dos kilómetros parecían una maratón. Sus piernas pesaban, su respiración era forzada. En un momento de flaqueza, me dijo: \

. Mi corazón dio un vuelco. Sabía que estábamos tan cerca. No era solo por la marca en la aplicación, sino por lo que significaba para él, para nosotros. Le tomé la mano, apreté el paso ligeramente y le dije: \

.\n​Sus ojos, que reflejaban la lucha interior, se encontraron con los míos. Hubo un silencio de unos segundos, solo interrumpido por el sonido de nuestros pasos rítmicos. Y entonces, vi un destello de determinación. Asintió, con un simple \

. Ese momento fue, sin duda, el más significativo de toda la experiencia. No fue un triunfo físico, sino un triunfo de la voluntad sobre el cuerpo cansado, de la perseverancia sobre la duda.\n​Los últimos dos kilómetros fueron una batalla de resistencia. Él luchaba con cada zancada, y yo, a su lado, le ofrecía palabras de aliento, contándole la distancia que quedaba, distrayéndolo con cualquier cosa para que no se concentrara en el dolor. Pasamos cerca del escenario iluminado, donde la iluminación fría de los focos contrastaba con el calor de nuestro esfuerzo. Yo iba unos pasos por delante, mirando hacia atrás para asegurarme de que seguía mi ritmo, como se captura en esa misma imagen. Su camiseta naranja brillante era un faro de determinación en la noche.\n​Finalmente, la voz sintética de la aplicación anunció lo que tanto habíamos esperado: \

. Nos detuvimos, jadeando, sudando, con las piernas temblando, pero con una sensación de euforia que no se puede describir con palabras. Nos abrazamos, un abrazo que contenía todo el esfuerzo, el dolor y la alegría compartida. Él, con la respiración entrecortada y una sonrisa que ahora sí era de triunfo total, me dijo: \

.
​Más tarde, cuando el pulso bajó y el cansancio dio paso a una profunda satisfacción, nos sentamos cerca del lago.
El cielo, ya completamente oscuro, se reflejaba en el agua tranquila, con las nubes dramáticas que habían acompañado nuestro inicio. El gran bloque de piedra en primer plano parecía una metáfora de la solidez de nuestro logro. Allí, en la paz de la noche, compartimos un momento de silencio, simplemente disfrutando de la compañía y de la sensación de haber superado un obstáculo juntos.
​Esta experiencia ha sido un punto de inflexión en nuestra relación y en nuestro viaje de running. Ha demostrado que, con apoyo mutuo y determinación, podemos alcanzar metas que parecían inalcanzables. Ahora, la carrera para la que nos estamos preparando ya no parece tan intimidante. Sabemos que, sin importar los obstáculos que se presenten, si estamos juntos, podemos superar la marca de los 8 kilómetros, y muchos más. Este es solo el comienzo.



---

For the best experience view this post on [Liketu](https://liketu.com/@rosbesalazar/diez-kilometros-de-amor-y-perseverancia-un-hito-en-nuestro-viaje-de-running)

title.title: I just did a simple calculation.
title.body:
I just did a simple calculation.
If a 100% vote removes 2% of voting mana, and a 50% vote removes 1%, then a 5% vote removes 0.1% of voting mana. So, if I wait for my voting mana to refill to 100%, I could cast 20 votes every 2 hours, which would remove exactly 2% of my mana. Since mana refills by 1% per hour, when the next votes are cast, my mana will be back to 100%. I think this is the most efficient curation method I can get.
Hopefully, my bot will find 20 posts of over 300 words to vote on every 2 hours.

20 votes every 2 hours would give 240 votes per day.
Currently, a 5% vote from me is worth $0.04, so $0.02 for you and $0.02 for me in return for curation.
That's a current curation return of 4.8 HIVE per day.
4.8 ​​* 30 = 144 per month
4.8 * 365 = 1752 per year.
This assumes the bot runs 24/7 and finds 20 posts to vote.
This week I need to try and quickly reach the goal of 20K BBHO on the @benef.bbho account.

Now I just have to wait for my mana to return to 100% to run some tests, even though I'm getting good curation returns at the moment.




![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/we-are-ai/23tbPFXJdbAjujuLjicHaTdDPxfCCQrqWtSjWT8syWC8cVGHgx1naQ6EJN8DCvu5nyg1e.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/we-are-ai/23tRn8czf1CMkfkm9cWBcZDk9qxFQex2PD3jtHeas43NpuMNBoP1XY8p7XMaok9hvdx5V.png)![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/we-are-ai/23t78uQEmXgk77X6Qac2yNDx5eLr3HMwPdz9LkcdLxCCoC9WkSFqEjJRXJH3Q2tAFEst5.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/we-are-ai/23swigvB8iCnR8UWCWeRkKyKq26W4ANGuJw5Nfz1Q4PnSpBR12gshQt5ZhKwM8hhr3V7A.png)

Otherwise, I increase my HP again and again whenever I can, so that I no longer need delegation, even though in the meantime I have put in some LEASE.

https://hive-engine.com/lease

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/we-are-ai/EnyoUsqFsPTQ3MCz2XRAx8FKMchndoGCqLN4Zub3QPxsJ5vJF1VcC9buPDMxViRdAq1.png)

Well, with all that said, I wish you a good week, and for my part I'm going to wait for the mana to go back up a bit for some testing. 

The rebot votes when activated for posts over 300 words and sends 0.01 GLYPH to each person within 24 hours.

The @benef.token team is able to buy them back faster and faster as their stack increases.

title.body:
# LIMA STREET DIARIES: FRAMES IN THE HEAT / DIARIOS DE CALLE: ENCUADRES EN EL CALOR [ENG - ESP]
### Street Photography & Bus Commutes / Fotografía de Calle y Viajes en Bus


![_DSC1644.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cabzphoto/23u5bTuZFwBiwsd132wdrFzNaFZKoU4RHG1FmwiXw5nLRyyB42BMnNB97tVaijKRTYHcG.jpg)

*“Finding the perfect frame makes you forget the summer heat, even for a moment.”*
*“Encontrar el encuadre perfecto te hace olvidar el calor del verano, aunque sea por un instante.”*

### English

Hello friends of the Black and White community and my #MonoMad companions. The start of classes means I'm back to riding buses every day. Even though it's close to home, walking is impossible, especially in this summer heat, which is terrible right now, to be honest. Still, I always try to keep a good mood to make the best of my trips and make them more fun.

I've already explained everything I feel when shooting on these buses and everything I find, but framing shots using bodies or any part of the bus simply makes me very happy. I smile when I start composing like this. It's a bit hard to concentrate these days; we are actually going through a merciless heatwave, not even the fan helps. I'm not a big fan of the heat, hence my complaining tone, hahaha. Well friends, I leave you with this series. I hope you like it; I'm always happy to participate in this community and to keep growing day by day with photography.

### Español

Hola amigos de la comunidad en Blanco y Negro y mis compañeros de #MonoMad. El inicio de clases me hace volver a subirme a los buses todos los días. Aunque es cerca de casa, no es posible caminar, y menos en este verano que está espantoso, para ser sincero. Igual, siempre mantengo el buen humor para sacar lo mejor de mis viajes y hacerlos más divertidos.

Ya he explicado todo lo que siento al fotografiar en los micros y todo lo que encuentro, pero armar encuadres con los cuerpos o con cualquier parte del bus, simplemente me hace muy feliz. Sonrío cuando empiezo a componer así. Es algo difícil en estas épocas poder concentrarse; en realidad estamos pasando por una ola de calor que no tiene piedad, ni el ventilador ayuda. No soy muy amante del calor, por eso mi voz de queja, jajaja. Bueno amigos, los dejo con esta serie. Espero que sea de su agrado; siempre feliz de participar en esta comunidad y de seguir creciendo día a día con la fotografía.

> **¡Kachkaniraqmi!** — *(Quechua: Until we meet again)*

J'aime utiliser leur travail pour participer au concours* 😀.

![Projet Tyxna](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23rz4VA2YGbTdtcnkEk7VkFjWwJgwochesRQa3EDEAp1JeqAbUY1tWnhovKj6F1yQKUEy.jpg)

> *Cette série de photos a été prise un matin lors de mes derniers tours de vélo l'année dernière. Je suis toujours à espérer de pouvoir prendre mon vélo les matins pour aller au travail. Mais les températures sont de retour en négatif* 😤

# ෴ ᴡʜᴇʀᴇ
![line_hive.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/xoycoMPQ-line_hive.jpg)

At the corner of Ontario and Moreau streets in Montreal. This is the **Pépinière Garden**, which transforms into a beer garden in the summer and hosts cultural events. It's located just behind a large building housing numerous artists' studios, including those of the [**Tyxna Project**](https://www.instagram.com/projet.tyxna/) and [**AShop**](https://www.ashop.ca/).

![Carte.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tHUivxKqLg7VAtMNVhdfZaw3jnoC3b8CD3rGjwUE3eMjvgFiustjqg4K1LXDeE43uFB.jpg)

> *Au coin de la rue Ontario et de la rue Moreau à Montréal. Il s'agit du **Jardin de la Pépinière** qui l'été se transforme en beergarden et accueille des événements culturels. Il se trouve juste derrière un grand immeuble accueillant de nombreux studios d'artistes dont ceux du [**Projet Tyxna**](https://www.instagram.com/projet.tyxna/) ou de [**AShop**](https://www.ashop.ca/).*

![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/242hU2diyoiTohfgR6SyYDRvYNi7p1Yoz6JkK9fTtWMZQ8MP5gGtTmmrw2fE4C7c8GHde.jpg)

# ෴ ᴡʜᴏ
![line_hive.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/xoycoMPQ-line_hive.jpg)

## Projet Tyxna

![423 - Projet Tyxna.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/243zde7KuKyiQ7XbduzUVWPG1SpBFjuSfxjb9tjGdG8pQcTrJ6V89AHwmZzmt9BpucYdV.jpg)

As I mentioned in the introduction, this isn't the first time I've talked to you about [**Projet Tyxna**](https://www.instagram.com/projet.tyxna/). As a reminder, it's a collective of four Montreal-based artists—**Fuser, Dodo Ose, AnkhOne, and Zek** who create shows using #StreetArt as their primary medium. Their studio is located in the building behind this mural.

> *Comme je le disais en introduction, ce n'est pas la première fois que je vous parle de [**Projet Tyxna**](https://www.instagram.com/projet.tyxna/). Pour rappel, c'est un collectif de 4 artistes basés à Montréal composé de **Fuser, Dodo Ose, AnkhOne et Zek** pour proposer des shows avec le StreetArt comme principal média. Leur studio se trouve dans l'immeuble derrière cette murale.*

<div class=\

/> This mural is truly magnificent. I don't know what the intended theme was; I can't find any posts about it. But it seems to be related to the French Revolution with its tricolor flags and cockades, Phrygian caps... and the female figures resemble Marianne, the personification of the French Republic. But I could be wrong; my knowledge on the subject is limited. **If you have any ideas, please feel free to share...** > *Cette murale est vraiment splendide. Je ne sais pas quel était le thème prévu, je ne trouve aucun post à son sujet. Mais elle me semble être reliée à la Révolution Française avec ces drapeaux et cocardes tricolores, les bonnets phrygiens... et les personnages féminins ressemblent à Marianne, la personnification de la République Française. Mais je peux me tromper, mes connaissances à ce sujet sont limitées. **Si vous avez une idée, n'hésitez pas à partager...*** ![427 - Projet Tyxna.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23vsJ5QWwd66S6qKL7GQcb1brPeEvUUhEp2GqjU4f1JUZCUebg2u2Uq2EnyX5PhaPahZr.jpg) I've never been to that beer garden for a beer in the summer. title.body: Hello fellow photographers, today I'm going to share a place in Las Tunas, Cuba, where I live. This place is a constant hub of activity, with pedestrians coming and going every day. Due to the various businesses surrounding it, it's very popular and well-known as the boulevard. There you'll also find an institution called \

(Footprints), and as you can see, that's its name. Along its approximately 100-meter length, you'll find several images of footprints, some sculpted in marble, others just silhouetted, and still others directly imprinted on the ground with ornamental plants planted in them.





Our city is known as the balcony of eastern Cuba, and the sculptures, because in any part or corner of it, you can appreciate sculptures, whether they are made of clay, marble, etc.




I took this picture in the afternoon, when it seemed to be resting itself, after so much hustle and bustle during the day, everything was calm and cool.

title.title: Traditions Are Our Identity And Heritage - Can They Be Changed?
title.body:
Traditions - Do you think there are traditions that are harmful, evil, or toxic? Why do you think these traditions were created? Why do you think society continues to perpetuate these kinds of traditions? Do you think we could change them? How would we change these harmful traditions?
Hello #qccommunity family, trust your weekend is going well. I welcome you to the blog. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaEcVR1C95Z1V5RV2Ls8Afh7cwbzm1tbawkXX1BM9mftZ/image.png) [Christopher1710](https://pixabay.com/images/download/christopher1710-bali-4319964_1920.jpg) Tradition can be defined as the way of life of people, which they are known for. It is a practice that is preserved and passed through generations. In my state of origin, we have many traditions; however, I am not privy to all of them. Among those traditions are: 1. New Yam Festival; this festival is celebrated to mark the beginning and end of the farming season. It happens once every year during the August meeting. The Igwe of our town, with his cabinet, champions the organisation and celebration of this festival. During this period, the youths and elders prepare cultural dances and masquerades to showcase glitz and glamour while prayers are offered as thanksgiving for the bountiful harvest and for fruitfulness for the new farming season. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUxPT3LirMTQzvKp6mjJiuxbshiSd9ri3WEjjMB4U42ft/1776628607357.jpg) [Pixelpower-01](https://pixabay.com/images/download/pixelpower-01-blacksmith-2740128_1920.jpg) 2. Uzu Awka Day; means blacksmith day, it is a day mapped out to celebrate the prowess of the blacksmiths in Awka. Their crafts and skills as blacksmiths are showcased with history in retrospect from the King and his cabinet as a major highlight of the day. Again, different classes of individuals attend the event to showcase talent and vigour in blacksmithing. There are a lot of cultural dances, masquerades, networking, and exchange of pleasantries. 3. Abstinence from killing Monkeys and green snakes; once you are a stranger to my hometown, you are advised to abstain from killing these two animals. They are seen as representatives of the ancestors and as guidance. They believe that once they are in your environment, they came for good news or to protect the individual from harm. They are sacred beings, and as such, killing them is regarded as an abomination. The offender faces ritual cleansing of the land, organising a burial for the animal, or even getting a sanction from the king. Traditions are good because they help us know our culture, which is our identity. However, I am not comfortable with the third tradition I mentioned above. There was a time we went for a traditional marriage and found a big python in our restroom. We wanted to kill it, but the elders around stopped us. They called some boys who came and used whistling to call the python from our restroom. It gently followed them to the bush while we were astonished. Later, they came back and told us that the python was protecting our house. I see that tradition as toxic and should be changed because a stranger can just fall victim to such abstinence and get into trouble by killing the monkey or snake. The monkeys come around at will and make noise. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmby4jdXYscmavxPqJk8g4oSzBUTG8E2YqYgq1pJY9dpby/image.png) [Vishu Joo](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543910759-cd9f15cc1f7a?q=80&w=857&auto=format&fit=crop&ixlib=rb-4.1.0&ixid=M3wxMjA3fDB8MHxwaG90by1wYWdlfHx8fGVufDB8fHx8fA%3D%3D) Society has been dancing to the tune of this tradition for a long time, and changing it wouldn’t be easy. Yet uneasy lies the head that wears the crown. If the villagers unanimously agree through a town hall meeting. Because there is power in the majority and unionism. The possibility of changing it would happen. Feel free to join [here](https://ecency.com/hive-117084/@queercoin/qc-community-weekly-contest-184) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbU2hSgaX1Af4R4dWfwNG3TcPhZMquzbJbmqGKqd7BpTd/1776628476884.gif)

title.title: ☕️ Tra idee e silenzi
title.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmb1XXDh8sGWSLzq2BxCycqLNYkysHkJXebebh6KY7MJ3k/IMG_1354.png 

Mi siedo qui, con il rumore lieve delle tazze e delle conversazioni intorno,  
e per un attimo tutto rallenta.

Non sempre ho bisogno di parlare.  
A volte osservo.  
Ascolto.  
Metto insieme pezzi.

Nel marketing si cerca sempre la frase giusta, il messaggio perfetto.  
Ma la verità è che le intuizioni migliori arrivano quando smetti di forzarle.

Questo è uno di quei momenti.  
Semplice, quasi invisibile… ma necessario.

Essere indipendente significa anche sapersi fermare senza sentirsi in colpa.  
Prendersi il proprio tempo, anche quando il mondo corre.

E tra un pensiero e l’altro,  
mi rendo conto che sto già creando qualcosa di nuovo.

Na filmikach z recenzjami było widać efekt cięcia, a u mojej mamy nie wychodzi to tak, jak bym się tego spodziewał. Nie miałem też za dużo czasu się tym bawić. Trzeba będzie któryś z następnych weekendów poświęcić na walkę. A takich zadań nazbierało się co najmniej kilka... The weather was a bit worse today, but for the first part of the day we could still sit outside in short sleeves. I’m a bit disappointed because it turns out that the lawn robot I bought for my mum isn’t working as it should — or rather, it works differently than I had expected. title.title: Mi comienzo en Splinterlands: Descubriendo un mundo de magia y estrategia en el Modo Frontera [ENG/SPA]
title.body:
>

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arribaeltelon/23tkomx21NaRgmf6SjJVYfkW9rb9JaPZbyc9rjQpzwGfCf5Biszf6d5QZNJq5951BwwaQ.png)

Hola, amigos de Hive. ¡Un saludo especial a todos los guerreros de Splinterlands!
He tardado un poco en pasar por aquí para contarles cómo ha sido mi experiencia inicial en la arena. Después de mucho pensarlo, finalmente me atreví a conocer el fascinante mundo de Splinterlands gracias a la invitación de mi amiga @angeluxx. Aquí les comparto los detalles de mi camino.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arribaeltelon/23tbCpBNQx14sm4Fq3FzL3FZB6bH6BHY7XcV7e17w3pSrBr24NKPG6fk4txPBYGdoD32r.png)


Al ingresar con el enlace de referencia, lo primero fue registrar mi nombre de usuario. Como mi nombre habitual es algo extenso, el sistema tomó la primera parte y así nació @arribaelt_lite. Una vez dentro, me dirigí a elegir mi apariencia en el juego; seleccionar el Avatar fue un momento divertido, ya que es la cara que mostraré ante mis oponentes.
Tenía la duda de si era obligatorio realizar una inversión desde el primer momento, así que le consulté a @angeluxx. Ella me explicó que podía empezar explorando las mecánicas en el modo \

, lo que me permitió familiarizarme con la interfaz sin presiones económicas iniciales.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arribaeltelon/23tuz8wBoJt7g4N29AXwZzGtTJWPpfpr4pJnj47X5UD4Boh3VThJLoRavqEgaiPGUDTkC.png)

Al principio me sentía un poco perdida, pero pronto descubrí que el juego es sumamente intuitivo. Lo que más me gusta es que te permite practicar constantemente para conocer el mazo de cartas. Las partidas se vuelven emocionantes una vez que empiezas a entender cómo se combinan las habilidades y los elementos.
Para perfeccionar mi técnica, me apoyé en las lecciones del Profesor Thalos Graystone. Él ha sido una guía fundamental para entender el verdadero potencial de mis cartas y cómo posicionarlas estratégicamente en el campo de batalla. Sus consejos me han ayudado a sentirme mucho más segura al enfrentar nuevos desafíos.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arribaeltelon/23wgDEXZrxqceoLVNyfyHeUpGXmWjZrGePSHzwy1dZMhmrp5ymk2ywh7VQ1GRk5YBopJB.png)

Aunque todavía estoy en proceso de aprendizaje, ya he podido saborear mis primeras victorias. Es muy satisfactorio ver cómo la estrategia da sus frutos al completar un duelo con éxito. Mi meta ahora es seguir practicando con constancia mientras reúno los recursos necesarios para adquirir mi Libro de Hechizos (Spellbook) y así integrarme de lleno en la economía del juego.
Apenas estoy empezando este viaje, pero la mezcla de estrategia y comunidad me tiene muy entusiasmada. ¡Espero verlos pronto en la arena de batalla!

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arribaeltelon/EoptpJS1LXcnZ9sNBe3RVhh7c874hPRFwm8xTboFE3fyjfFK3XjA8xn5XgSsWKE4WFm.png)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arribaeltelon/Eo44kaLW7SfBRpSJvyqbPtXpCMvSSSg2N1XdBVf53SnFwNJZJrYj2P9MoWK6NmnKm64.png)

title.title: Diario de un niño, el libro que dejó la primera marca [Es-En] Diary of a child, the book that left the first mark.
title.body:
<div class=text-justify>


Saludos, estimados amigos, por aquí haciendo acto de presencia y respondiendo a la iniciativa de @hiveargentina: El libro que marcó mi vida - Iniciativa Día del Libro / The Book That Changed My Life - Book Day Initiative [Ver aquí](https://ecency.com/hive-161447/@hiveargentina/493af481). 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcqDt6B3NAr1akd1BKyfC88W2KdiCJi5eEdbZkURVN126/image.png)

Desde que leí y escuché la convocatoria, he estado pensando, tratando de elegir un libro en particular de los que he leído hasta ahora, pero antes de mencionarlo, voy a hacer referencia a un recuerdo de 2020, cuando el 16 de junio participé en un reto consistente en publicar la portada de un libro significativo que me hubiera importado lo suficiente para recordarlo sin comentario alguno.
Al cuarto día publiqué la portada del libro que marcó mi vida, pues aunque han sido muchos los libros que me han influido, este en particular me marcó desde muy temprano y hasta hoy, a pesar de no haberlo vuelto a leer en su totalidad desde que aprendí a leer en sus páginas.
Concluido el reto, seguí publicando portadas para incluir algunos títulos que aprecio y tienen especial significado para mí.

En sus páginas aprendí a leer a muy corta edad, cuando el eslogan de la educación rezaba: La letra con sangre entra. Estoy seguro de que la mía no llegó al río, pero entre coscorrones y sinsabores, tuvieron que pasar años, tebeos y cruzar la mar océano para reconciliarme con la lectura por puro placer.

Sin duda, mi género favorito es la novela y en especial la ciencia ficción, aunque disfruto de la poesía, la historia, la espiritualidad y la autoayuda. Como excepción, disfruté mucho leyendo un texto de economía, aunque no me detuve en las gráficas de las diferentes teorías de mercado y dinero.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUkVvot8QPCUgkyYZPsah2h2ZbCsw3baKCy4QVfL2xUfX/image.png)
[Dos libros poderosos de esos por los que se dice que la pluma es más fuerte que la espada.] 

Una sola vez asistí a una feria del libro con motivo del día y no recuerdo nada especial, salvo que acudí invitado por un autor involucrado en la organización de la feria y con los años me regaló algunos ejemplares de sus obras que le valieron premios y presentaciones internacionales, aunque siempre bajo los auspicios del Estado. Seguramente deje de simpatizarle el día que le pregunte cuándo la publicaban en una editorial comercial. 
He conocido a otros autores publicados en papel y digital, pero me abstendré de comentar nada, no sea que alguno ronde por Hive y se sienta aludido sin necesidad. Aunque de uno de ellos nos trajimos un ejemplar comprado en Cumaná y, si no engaña la memoria, con una dedicatoria de amigo y autor. 
En un momento quise conocer al autor de una serie de libros de autoayuda que considero excelentes, pero cuando en uno de sus libros dejó su opinión acerca de la migración hispanohablante a su país, el deseo desapareció. Con los años he comprendido el abismo que hay entre el autor y su obra, no digamos nada del personaje.

El libro en que aprendí a leer es Corazón: Diario de un niño, del autor italiano Edmundo de Amicis. No conservo aquel libro y en una ocasión compré un ejemplar para mis hijos, llevándome una desilusión, pues se trataba de una versión recortada en extremo, donde faltaban demasiadas partes.  De este libro salió la historia de Marco o De los Apeninos a los Andes, famosa por el anime, pero en mi memoria guardo otra que no he visto reproducida en otra parte. La del pequeño escribiente florentino. 
Sin duda, este es el libro que dejó una primera marca en mi vida. 

Antes de concluir, quiero hacer unas invitaciones muy especiales a participar en esta iniciativa; espero que las acepten con el mismo aprecio con que las hago: @evagavilan2 y @josemalavem. Y que cuantos me leen y así lo desean, son bienvenidos a participar, recordando usar el idioma español. 
Gracias. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbgu7ePLTiyZZRAV4xByVdoiPymC5mdsikMyGCrKsJ7RW/image.png)

También hoy escribo en mi lengua materna, el español, dejando el texto en inglés por cuenta del traductor Google. Las imágenes de mi propiedad son de los libros de toda la familia que ahora tengo más a mano. 

#  Diary of a child, the book that left the first mark.

Greetings, dear friends. I'm here making an appearance and responding to the initiative of @hiveargentina: The Book That Changed My Life - Book Day Initiative [See here](https://ecency.com/hive-161447/@hiveargentina/493af481).

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcqDt6B3NAr1akd1BKyfC88W2KdiCJi5eEdbZkURVN126/image.png)

Since reading and hearing about the call for submissions, I've been thinking, trying to choose a particular book from those I've read so far. But before mentioning it, I'd like to recall a memory from 2020, when on June 16th I participated in a challenge that consisted of posting the cover of a significant book that mattered to me enough to remember it without any commentary.

On the fourth day, I posted the cover of the book that changed my life. Although many books have influenced me, this one in particular left its mark on me from a very early age and continues to do so to this day, even though I haven't reread it in its entirety since I learned to read from its pages.
Once the challenge was over, I continued posting covers to include some titles that I cherish and that hold special meaning for me.

I learned to read from its pages at a very young age, back when the prevailing educational slogan was: \

I'm sure mine didn't reach that point, but between bumps and bruises, it took years, comics, and crossing the ocean to reconcile myself with reading for pure pleasure. Without a doubt, my favorite genre is the novel, especially science fiction, although I also enjoy poetry, history, spirituality, and self-help. As an exception, I thoroughly enjoyed reading an economics text, although I didn't delve into the graphs of the different market and money theories. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUkVvot8QPCUgkyYZPsah2h2ZbCsw3baKCy4QVfL2xUfX/image.png) [Two powerful books, the kind that prove the pen is mightier than the sword.] I only attended a book fair once, for the occasion, and I don't remember anything special, except that I was invited by an author involved in organizing the fair. Over the years, he gave me some copies of his works, which earned him awards and international presentations, though always under the auspices of the State. He probably stopped liking me the day I asked him when they would be published by a commercial publisher. I've met other authors published in both print and digital formats, but I'll refrain from commenting, lest someone on Hive feel unnecessarily targeted. Although we brought back a copy from one of them, bought in Cumaná, and if memory serves, it had a dedication from a friend and the author. At one point, I wanted to meet the author of a series of self-help books that I consider excellent, but when he shared his opinion about Spanish-speaking migration to his country in one of his books, that desire vanished. Over the years, I've come to understand the chasm that exists between the author and his work, not to mention the person. The book I learned to read from is Heart: Diary of a Child, by the Italian author Edmondo De Amicis. I don't have that book anymore, and I once bought a copy for my children, only to be disappointed, as it was an extremely abridged version, missing too many parts. The story of Marco, or From the Apennines to the Andes, famous for the anime adaptation, came from this book, but I remember another story that I haven't seen reproduced anywhere else: that of the little Florentine scribe. Without a doubt, this is the book that left its first mark on my life. Before concluding, I want to extend some very special invitations to participate in this initiative; I hope they accept them with the same appreciation I have for them: @evagavilan2 and @josemalavem. And all of you who read this and wish to participate are welcome, remembering to use Spanish. Thank you. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbgu7ePLTiyZZRAV4xByVdoiPymC5mdsikMyGCrKsJ7RW/image.png) I'm also writing today in my native language, Spanish, leaving the English text to Google Translate. The images are my own and are from the family's books that I have readily available.

body.title: “Shaped by Stone… Shaped by Hope: Why Our Children Still Need a Place to Stay”
body.body: _These curves are not just art._ They are stories carved in stone. Recently, we visited a place that holds deep meaning for us.

/> A master artist — one of the finest in the world — once worked here, shaping soapstone and granite into powerful forms. Before he passed away two years ago, he had begun training some of our children.
/> He saw something in them. Potential. Creativity. A future. As we walked through his space, I looked at these curved sculptures differently. Each one carries a form… a weight… a direction.
/> Some bend. Some rise. Some seem to carry something unseen. And I could not help but think of our children.

/> They too are being shaped. Not by tools… But by life. By struggle. By hope. Some of them walk long distances every day just to come to school. Some return to homes that are uncertain. Some carry burdens no child should carry. Yet, like these stones, they continue.

/>

They endure.  
They grow  
But there is something missing.  
A safe place.  
A place where they can rest.  
A place where they can stay and continue learning without fear or exhaustion.  
That is why we need a dormitory.  
Not as a luxury.  
But as a necessity.  
The same way a sculptor shapes stone with care and intention…  
We are trying to shape lives.  
But without a safe space, the process becomes harder.  
Slower.  
More uncertain.  
This art reminds us that beauty can come from pressure.  
That strength can come from shaping.  
That something meaningful can emerge from something raw.  
And maybe…  
With the right support…  
These children will not only learn…  
They will rise.  
If this story speaks to you, I invite you to be part of this journey.  
Because sometimes…  
What we build for a child today…  
Becomes the future we all share tomorrow.

body.body:
https://images.ecency.com/DQmWS1SgYtuXaJaAySmDntm3AP8As8W2kMuLqybah2dGsmv/black_white_vintage_classic_music_presentation.jpg
Few artists in the history of Latin music have generated as many conflicting reactions as Cristian Castro. The son of actress Verónica Castro and artistically adopted by the late Manuel “El Loco” Valdés, his artistic lineage opened doors for him, but it was his voice (a strange blend of velvet and crystal edge) that cemented his place in the hearts of millions.

To understand his relevance, one must first accept an uncomfortable truth: Latin American popular taste has always been a volcano of contradictions. While Spanish-language rock flirted with intellectual posturing and salsa celebrated the barrio, the romantic ballad remained the emotional refuge of single mothers, heartbroken office workers, and teenagers who still believed in soap opera endings. There, in that territory that many critics considered corny, Castro built his empire. He didn't do so modestly, but with a display of vocal pyrotechnics that put even the most self-important tenors to shame.
Pocos artistas en la historia de la música latina han generado tantas reacciones encontradas como Cristian Castro. Hijo de la actriz Verónica Castro y adoptado artísticamente por el fallecido Manuel “El Loco” Valdés, su linaje artístico le abrió puertas, pero fue su voz (una mezcla extraña de terciopelo y filo de cristal) la que lo instaló en el oído de millones.

Para entender su relevancia, primero hay que aceptar una verdad incómoda: el gusto popular latinoamericano siempre ha sido un volcán de contradicciones. Mientras el rock en español coqueteaba con la pose intelectual y la salsa reivindicaba el barrio, la balada romántica se mantuvo como el refugio emocional de las madres solteras, los oficinistas despechados y los adolescentes que aún creían en finales de telenovela. Ahí, en ese territorio que muchos críticos consideraban cursi, Castro levantó su imperio. No lo hizo con modestia, sino con un despliegue de pirotecnia vocal que avergonzaba hasta a los tenores más engreídos.
To understand his impact, we have to go back to the early nineties, when Latin pop hadn't yet exploded globally with Ricky Martin or Shakira.

In 1992, at only seventeen years old, Cristian released \
which launched him to fame with songs like \
an album that still smelled of eighties production. But it was \
(1993) that catapulted him to stardom with the classic \
became an anthem of melancholic hope. Later came the album \

(1997), named after the same song, which catapulted him throughout Latin America. “The Roses Weep,” “If You Loved Me,” or “After You… What?”

In 1999, he solidified his success with the album “My Life Without Your Love,” which included the songs “My Life Without Your Love,” “To Love Again,” “Angel,” “For Loving You Like This,” and “Someday.” These songs, besides being musical gems, were also used as theme songs for several Mexican telenovelas of that era.

On the 2001 album “Blue,” it was the song “Azul” that ultimately defined his career: “Azul” is the musical equivalent of an overly sweet dessert, laced with corny metaphors (“Blue like a tear when there is forgiveness. So pure and so blue that it intoxicated the heart”) and a melody that seems written to be hummed in an elevator. However, it worked. It worked because Castro understood that Latin culture doesn't demand subtlety in heartbreak; it demands catharsis. If you're going to cry over a breakup, do it with a knife in your chest and a chorus you can belt out from the shower. That was his genius: turning sentimentality into an act of tender rebellion.
Para entender su impacto, hay que retroceder a principios de los noventa, cuando el pop latino aún no explotaba globalmente con Ricky Martin o Shakira.

En 1992, con solo diecisiete años, Cristian lanzó “Agua Nueva”, con el cual emprende el vuelo hacia la fama con temas como “No podrás” un disco que aún olía a producción ochentera, pero fue “Un Segundo en el Tiempo” (1993) el que lo catapultó con el clásico “Nunca voy a olvidarte” además que el sencillo “Mañana” se convirtió en un himno de esperanza melancólica, posteriormente vino la producción: “Lo mejor de mí” (1997), nombre de la misma canción lo cual lo catapultó por toda Iberoamérica. “Lloran las rosas” “Si tú me amaras” o “Después de ti... qué?”

En 1999, se consolida con el álbum “Mi vida sin tu amor” de donde se desprenden: “Mi vida sin tu amor” “Volver a amar” “Ángel” “Por amarte así” y “Alguna vez” quienes además de joyas musicales fueron temas para varias telenovelas mexicanas de esa época.

En el disco “Azul” de 2001 fue esa canción la que terminó por definir su carrera: “Azul” es el equivalente musical a un postre demasiado empalagoso y amasado en metáforas cursis (“Azul como una lagrima cuando hay perdón. Tan puro y tan azul que embriagó el corazón”) y una melodía que parece escrita para ser tarareada en un ascensor. Sin embargo, funcionó. Funcionó porque Castro entendió que la cultura latina no pide sutileza en el desamor; pide catarsis. Si vas a llorar una ruptura, hazlo con un puñal en el pecho y un coro que puedas gritar desde la ducha. Ese fue su genio, el convertir la cursilería en un acto de rebeldía tierna.

His controversial nature, however, nearly consumed him in life. The family scandals broadcast live by the Mexican tabloids, his statements about homosexuality that changed from week to week…

All of this made him a figure as hated as he was loved. In the 2000s, while Juanes filled stadiums with messages of peace and Julieta Venegas seduced indie music, Cristian Castro seemed like a relic from another era. But Latin culture has an unrelenting emotional memory: In every karaoke bar from Miami to Buenos Aires, “Azul” and “Por Amarte Así” continue to resonate with the same intensity as a pagan ritual. His concerts, though infrequent, still fill theaters. And when he opens his mouth to sing, the audience doesn't judge his eccentric personality; they simply embrace it.
Su carácter polémico, sin embargo, casi lo devora en vida. Los escándalos familiares transmitidos en vivo por la prensa rosa mexicana, sus declaraciones sobre la homosexualidad que cambiaban de semana a semana…

Todo eso lo convirtió en un personaje tan odiado como amado. En los años 2000, mientras Juanes llenaba estadios con mensajes de paz y Julieta Venegas seducía a los indie, Cristian Castro parecía un relicario de otra época. Pero la cultura latina tiene una memoria afectiva implacable: En cada karaoke de Miami a Buenos Aires, “Azul” y “Por Amarte Así” siguen sonando con la misma intensidad de un ritual pagano. Sus conciertos, aunque espaciados, siguen llenando teatros. Y cuando abre la boca para cantar, el público no juzga su excéntrica personalidad, simplemente la abraza.
