title.title: Drag Racing Streets Realistic Car Tuning Aur Intense Racing Experience
title.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1776619791546-c6e527db125034ae.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=inkbyte/97fb369d)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=inkbyte/97fb369d)


---

if you are a fan of racing games and especially drag racing then drag racing streets can be a great choice i tried this game personally and honestly initially i thought it would be a simple racing game but once the gameplay started the experience turned out to be quite realistic and engaging the strongest point of this game is its physics based system here you do not just have to race but you also get to tune your car gear ratios suspension and engine settings can all be manually adjusted which directly impacts the race performance

There are 150 plus cars available in the game which include jdm muscle and classic cars each car has the option to customize which makes the game even more interesting gameplay focuses on short distance races like 1 4 mile and 1 2 mile runs where your reaction time and perfect gear shifting are crucial i personally liked the manual clutch system because it makes the game feel more realistic.

The graphics are also quite decent and the cars are well designed weekly tournaments and online multiplayer races keep the game from getting boring and you are always engaged in some challenge or the other

On a negative note beginners may find this game a bit difficult because it takes time to understand the tuning system some users have also mentioned updates and performance issues but the overall rating is quite good overall if you want a realistic drag racing experience where both skill and tuning matter then this game is definitely worth a try it is not just about racing but also about strategy and mechanics which makes it different from other racing games.

---

title.title: Learning to Stay in Control, When Anger Takes Over
title.body:
<div class='text-justify'>

Early today, I stumbled upon a short movie clip and I watched how a single choice that would have been avoided, ruined a happy family. I watched how responding to anger forcefully and uncontrollable anger destroyed all that a man had struggled to build for years, destroyed in a few days.

He allowed a single decision he made out of uncontrollable anger, which led to the death of his son and wife. I felt distressed watching this video. All I could possibly say was, \

He would have walked out and focus on getting his family home. I couldn't help but blame the man for responding to his anger, even after his son called him repeatedly, but yet he chose to let his temper get the best of him. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmULfDGRt9qCiXktK1tSXYhedJSbD9U6Tst48jdcB96GMX/1776619907445.jpg) [PICTURESOURCE](https://unsplash.com/photos/closeup-of-a-black-hand-in-fist-VKC0CMAhDtc) Getting angry is inevitable and unavoidable, but we always have a choice on how to respond and control the situation. A single decision made due to anger can change the life of a person in a few seconds and that's why controlling how we respond to anger is necessary. Controlling temper could save us from regret and resentment towards ourselves. I know and understand that anger is a natural feeling amongst humans. I have been angry. There's no individual on earth that hasn't felt angry before and how it's responded to, could cause severe damage or save us. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcVQeit7erN5CTur8k22m8RBuUJhs8da66pLoPKi6FaxP/1776619920407.jpg) [PICTURESOURCE](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-man-with-his-head-in-his-hands-T9iLQrhESYE) I learnt from an article I read some time ago, that anger is a quick response, and the actions we take when we are angry aren't processed by the brain and that's why one of the ways to control anger is definitely by pausing before reacting and taking a break to think before responding. Personally, I take a walk, especially when I'm tempted to react impulsively. Practicing to pause and walk away will really prevent regret and many worse situations. A break like this will guide you into resolving a conflict peacefully and by having a simple negotiation. Take a deep breath and relax, and ask yourself questions about the situation, and you will realize that some actions aren't worth responding to, but rather ignoring, addressing in the future and even walking away from. Taking a deep breath and relaxing to consider the risk and danger your actions might lead you, people your actions might hurt or affect and these could save you from regrets, pain, bad situations and many more. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP1p4NvymkpViuETUVLB9tn2FoH5rMGtTBVU1WxsZiP27/1776619931675.jpg) [PICTURESOURCE](https://unsplash.com/photos/yellow-and-green-bird-on-brown-stick-W_irudglgK0) Uncontrollable anger/ temper is an attitude, habit and a trait that causes weak and dangerous decisions. Being silent doesn't make anyone weak, but instead gives a chance for the best decision and shows intelligence. This is just a thoughtful post and I hope it guides how we respond to anger and learn to walk away. Life is so unpredictable and responding to an emotion like anger could cause regret and everlasting pain. ### Thanks for reading ♥️ ### Vanilla 💗

Gm sktehive Family, have a great Sunday everyone!!

Today I'm sharing a short video I edited with some of my skateboarding adventures on my Sundays off. Sunny days with lots of skateboarding and fun with friends in the morning to invigorate the body and spirit for a new week that starts tomorrow, Monday.

Lately I've really enjoyed skating at the Ipiranga Museum because besides being very close to home, it's usually empty, but sometimes it can suddenly get crowded too. It's really cool because there's the option of doing street skating on the Portuguese marble blocks from Emperor Dom Pedro II's time. If it's too crowded, it's possible to skate on a track with a slightly different shape that's also hidden inside the museum, in a kind of forested area that doesn't get as much sun, which is also pretty cool.

One cool thing that always happens when I go there is that I always run into some friends from my school days when I lived in the south side with my mom, and I think it's really awesome to be able to meet childhood friends, and most of the time they're skateboarding too!! And in 2026, finding friends from '97/'98/'99 still active is really cool.

After that skateboarding session, the mission is to go back home and make lunch for my wife and daughter, and then watch a good movie with them because, after all, nothing is worthwhile if we can't spend some quality time with family to recharge our batteries!!

🛹♻️💚

Wishing everyone a great Sunday and a good week 🙌🏾

title.body: >Cuida tu cuerpo y tu mente

></center>

Con motivo del Día Mundial de la Salud, nuestra amiga @damarysvibra nos invita a hablar sobre lo que estamos haciendo para cuidar o mejorar nuestra salud. En un mundo caótico, lleno de desenfrenos, donde es fácil excederse, donde hay más contaminación y donde predominan los alimentos procesados, nuestro cuerpo es bombardeado diariamente por agentes nocivos, y es relevante saber qué estamos haciendo para defenderlo.  
Siempre he sido una persona saludable, gracias a Dios. Puedo contar las veces que he estado enferma, y cuando ha sucedido, ha sido debido a bajones mentales y emocionales. Es decir, sé que cuando estoy muy triste, mis defensas bajan tanto que me resfrío, algo que nunca ocurriría en situaciones normales, incluso si paso un día entero al lado de personas enfermas. Hay una conexión real entre mi espíritu y mi cuerpo, mi mente y lo que puedo sentir o sufrir, así que, sobre todo, cuido mi mente, trato de no tener \
y mantenerme alegre o tranquila a diario.\n\n

/> ¿Cómo lo hago? Por ejemplo, las condiciones en mi país pueden causarle un colapso mental a cualquiera, así que trato de no entrar en esa espiral de emociones fuertes y dañinas. En ese sentido, no me gusta ver las noticias, tampoco entro en discusiones inútiles, respiro profundo cuando hay falta de algún servicio público como electricidad, agua, gas, Internet. En el transporte público uso audífonos y escucho música. También escucho música mientras cocino, limpio u ordeno. La música es terapia para el alma. Me gusta salir, sola o acompañada, arreglarme, ir a la playa, tomar sol, caminar descalza. Y en los últimos años, he aprendido a no tomarme nada personal ni a pecho. Pero, como mujer de 50 años, tengo claro que debo empezar a cuidar aspectos que no cuidé antes, ya que mi cuerpo no es el mismo y ya no produzco ciertos elementos para estar al 100%. Por ello, tengo el hábito de beber agua con limón en ayunas para desintoxicar mi cuerpo. También tomo una dosis diaria de magnesio no solo para los huesos, sino también para mejorar el sueño. Además, consumo ácido fólico para mantener los niveles de hierro. Esas dos pastillas, magnesio y ácido fólico, han producido grandes y óptimos cambios en mi vida.

/> En cuanto a la comida, trato de comer saludable, en casa, sin aditivos químicos. Por ejemplo, le doy prioridad a las proteínas. Me gusta comer carne animal, así que como pollo, cerdo y res. No le tengo miedo a los carbohidratos, por lo que acompaño las carnes con arroz, pasta, pan o arepas. Como verduras y bebo mucha agua. No me gustan los refrescos ni los dulces, aunque ocasionalmente como un pedazo de postre sin culpa. Hay cosas que sé que hago y que no son saludables, como tomar café y cerveza, y no hacer ejercicio. Aunque soy una persona activa, y debido a mi trabajo a veces tengo que subir y bajar muchas escaleras a diario, admito que soy perezosa cuando se trata de hacer ejercicio. Esto es fatal para una persona de mi edad, que ya comienza a perder masa muscular y tener rigidez en las articulaciones. Por eso me he propuesto como meta este año inscribirme en un gimnasio o al menos empezar una rutina de ejercicios en casa que me ayude a mantenerme fuerte y ágil.

/> En algún lugar leí que hablamos de una persona saludable no solo cuando está físicamente bien, sino también mentalmente, y que la salud mental puede ser tan decisiva para la salud corporal, por ejemplo, que muchas enfermedades tienen su raíz en los sentimientos que acumulamos. Es inútil comer buena comida y consumirla con ira, tristeza o celos. Esa comida te va a hacer daño. Así que, así como comes, haz cosas que nutran positivamente tu espíritu: escribe, pinta, baila, duerme, haz el amor, abraza. Recuerda: la salud comienza en tu mente, y así como cuidas lo que consumes y va a tu estómago, también es fundamental lo que consume tu alma. No solo es verte bien, también es sentirte bien.
>La imagen principal fue creada en Canva las otras son de mi galería personal. El texto fue traducido con Deepl
>Gracias por vuestro apoyo, lectura y comentario, amigo. Hasta una próxima oportunidad

>Take care of your body and your mind On the occasion of World Health Day, our friend @damarysvibra invites us to talk about what we are doing to take care of or improve our health. In a chaotic world, full of frenzy, where it is easy to go overboard, where there is more pollution, and where processed food predominates, our body is bombarded daily by harmful agents, and it is relevant to know what we are doing to defend it. I have always been a healthy person, thank God. I can count the times I have been sick, and when it has happened, it has been due to mental and emotional \

That is to say, I know that when I am very sad, my defenses drop so much that I catch a cold, something that would never happen in normal situations, even if I spend an entire day next to sick people. There is a real connection between my spirit and my body, my mind and what I can feel or suffer, so above all, I take care of my mind, try not to have \

and stay cheerful daily.

How do I do it? For example, the conditions in my country can cause mental collapse to anyone, so I try not to enter that spiral of strong and harmful emotions. In that sense, I don't like watching the news, I also don't get into useless arguments, I take deep breaths when there is a lack of any public service such as electricity, water, gas, Internet. On public transportation I use headphones and listen to music. I also listen to music while cooking, cleaning, or tidying up. Music is therapy for the soul. I like to go out, alone or with company, dress up, go to the beach, sunbathe, walk barefoot. And in recent years, I don't take anything personally or to heart.

But, as a 50-year-old woman, I am clear that I must start taking care of aspects that I did not take care of before, since my body is not the same and I no longer produce certain elements to be at 100%. Therefore, I have a habit of drinking lemon water on an empty stomach to detoxify my body. I also take a daily dose of magnesium not only for the bones, but also to improve sleep. I also consume folic acid to maintain iron levels. Those two pills, magnesium and folic acid, have made great and optimal changes in my life.

Regarding food, I try to eat healthy at home, without chemical additives. For example, I prioritize proteins. I like to eat animal meat, so I eat chicken, pork, and beef. I am not afraid of carbohydrates, so I accompany the meats with rice, pasta, bread, or arepas. I eat vegetables and drink plenty of water. I do not like sodas or sweets, although occasionally I eat a piece of dessert without guilt.

There are things I know I do that are not healthy, like drinking coffee and beer, and not exercising. Although I am an active person, and because of my work I sometimes have to go up and down many stairs daily, I admit I am lazy when it comes to exercising. This is fatal for a person my age, who is already beginning to lose muscle mass and have joint stiffness. So I have set as a goal this year to enroll in a gym or at least start an exercise routine at home that helps me stay strong and agile.

Somewhere I read that we speak of a healthy person not only when they are physically well, but also mentally, and that mental health can be as decisive for bodily health, for example, as many diseases have their root in the feelings we accumulate. It is useless to eat good food and consume it with anger, sadness, or jealousy. That food is going to harm you. So, just as you eat, do things that positively nourish your spirit: write, paint, dance, sleep, make love, embrace. Remember: health begins in your mind, and just as you take care of what you consume and goes to your stomach, it is also fundamental what your soul consumes.

Not only is it about looking good, it’s also about feeling good.

title.body: 3/4 🧵 What makes this more interesting is the contrast with Jenner’s own public stance. Some powers and abilities are very important to understand because they help you at the time of selection and guide you which monster should be used in which battle.

Today I am comparing two monsters. One is named Kelan Gaines and the other is Delya. Both are good monsters and are very important in battles.

First I will talk about Kelan Gaines. Its mana cost is 8 which means you can easily play it in mid to high mana battles. In low mana battles it can create difficulties.

![Screenshot 2026-04-18 223311.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23z79Y8YmMNtPnKytB1e6XCe8HRN9kpqT42TCdXbBJnq9uv3P8oLbirx7vzbJjZQe6rXG.png)


![Screenshot 2026-04-18 223321.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23u5ZEBxJ17dmF8HavHbgjqi41eWCn3oa94TDshA98duka8h4t57NNAZ1DerVxrTtGoPv.png)


Its health is not very high but if you place a tank monster with it, it can survive for a long time. Remember that monsters with low health are actually support units and they should be placed in positions where they can survive longer in battle.

Another feature is its speed which is 5. This means it attacks fast and also helps its allied units attack more effectively. On the left side of the card you can see a purple “2” which shows its magic attack type. 

This is its special ability because it bypasses armor and directly hits the enemys health. It is very powerful against heavily armored enemies. The good thing is that it does not miss because of its speed.

If I talk about its price it is available in the market from $0.65 up to $74.

Now talking about the second monster Delya. This is also considered a dangerous monster. Its mana cost is 9. Again it is good for mid to high mana battles but selecting it in low mana battles would not be a good decision and this is also considered its weak point.

Its health is 6 which is better than the first monster. Its speed is also 5 which is very good. Its main feature is its ranged attack which you can see on the left side as “2”. This means if you place it in mid to backline position it will keep hitting the enemy from a distance.

![Screenshot 2026-04-18 223302.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23xozBezuBXTgw7sWdxKM6F4zMQkqejytm3Sg4LnwAsRwCvRDhRN9WjA1vCnF2FgGE9HX.png)

![Screenshot 2026-04-18 223254.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23uEvBi6KdvUhEA1oDx12FK6Zi3NvkSnxZsbCtGkeLN65adZH5zkkFNC6caknLLoVm7TB.png)

Its special ability is Double Strike which means it can attack twice in every round. This is very effective and useful in dealing more damage.

If I talk about its price it is quite an expensive monster. Its minimum price is about $57 and it can go up to $636.

Both monsters are very strong. If you add them to your team with good strategy and proper placement then they can help you win battles. Some of their abilities are similar so it is very important to understand them and select them properly in battles.


What do you people think about these monsters? Which monster do you like the most and what is the reason? Share you views in the comment section.


I hope you find this post useful and informative.. If you do, please remember to reblog it so that it reaches as many people as possible and that they can benefit the most from it. Also remember to upvote which will help me financially and grow my account.

title.body:
Crypto market pumped this week with updates on WW3. Bitcoin price broke up one of great resistance. Hive price was trying to reverse up from the bottom and It went up slowly. It touched one of great resistance. Hive price was in a descending channel and It touched the top level of this channel. Hive price could not break up the top line of this channel.

Here you can see daily chart of Hive price. Hive price tested 2 times to break up the top line of this descending channel. We may see reversing down after touching the top line of descending channel.


![e1.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chorock/23swftpiiootLj8e7HDATvf9e8n1BjX7ewHmb231LnxGmNX9AJN3yKLHfKsCugE1TdDHN.PNG)

Here you can see the indicators on daily chart of Hive price. There was great downtrend line on RSI Indicator. Hive price broke up this great downtrend line but reversed down again. It may be bullish trap. We have seen same breaking up on Bitcoin RSI Indicator. It may be a great bullish trap. 

There is uptrend line on MACD Indicator. If we see more daily red candles, this MACD Indicator will break down mini uptrend line.

Fisher Indicator is on the top and ready to reverse down.


![e2.PNG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chorock/23swiWiwWJrxzSMs6KKgf9jWmiPAU3LKGp9RK9kARiMeRZJcT493qt5Laagdt5WrULnLB.PNG)

We see the same scenario on Hive price as Bitcoin price chart. We have seen the updates on WW3. We will see the effects on crypto market. Crypto market may reverse down. If it happens, market maker will make great bullish trap.

We will see...

title.title: Coffee, not facultative - on running and returning
title.body: I just came back from a whirlwind trip through Ireland and the UK. With fewer sleep hours than I'd like but a looot of love and joy in my heart, I'm still reeling and somewhat refusing to leave the journey behind. So I thought I'd share with you one of the many fantastic stops of this past week.\n\n

> By happenstance (that is my brain, which is, by now, part Skyscanner), we started our adventure in rainy Birmingham, which we'd never seen before and which seemed fitting all in all, considering it's the birthplace of the one and only Ozzy Osbourne. I've got to say, the city didn't make the most fantastic impression on me, but it's not entirely the Brummies' fault. Weather was shit, we were dead tired, and in a constant to-and-fro, having chosen a hotel near the airport to suit the next day's morning flight. So Birmingham only had a short, few hours to make an impression on us. Naturally, I'd done my homework ahead of time, and the first stop in the city for exhausted travelers was caffeinated. A tiny little place called **Faculty Coffee**, in fact, which was nestled perfectly right across the street from Birmingham New Street. *(yes, of course I arrange train rides depending on good coffee... you don't?)*

> Faculty Coffee is hidden inside a gorgeous little passage (which I simply loved, and not just because of the sudden attack of rain). It felt like entering a secret. Which I suppose, in ways, was to set the tone for the entire journey ahead. From without, the place itself didn't amount to all that much. It certainly greeted you as unassuming - the sort of place you can easily wander past, unbothered. Still. I'd written it inside my palm, which meant we simply had to stop.
> I scanned the board, the way one does, but wasn't feeling too adventurous with the exhaustion and all (did I mention I hardly even glimpsed at the sweets? I was definitely off!).

> A simple filter (black only, apparently!) would do me just fine, and luckily for us, there was one last free table by the window into the passage, which beat hanging around inside the passage, waiting on the rain to quit.

> It also gave me a perfect vantage point for observing the crowds. And I do mean crowds (well, for this kind of small place, anyway). I love, whenever I go to this kind of coffee spot, to note the regulars, drifting in and out, the business of strangers' lives, the stopping for a takeaway cup that'll inevitably end up discarded on a beach somewhere, in the hope that it'll dissolve somehow faster than us.

> Weird, how humans be. But we're not on the Irish coast yet. But here, in this tiny little caffeinated nook of Birmingham. It grew on me, the way all these places inevitably will. With every hurried office-y person coming in. Every perfectly hipstery young family that refuses to quit specialty coffee outtings now they're three, which I must say I kinda like. You start looking at places in a different light, start seeing that they, also, are somebody's. That they're beloved by somebody, well-treaded, trusted.

> A place to return to again and again for someone. How amazing it is, to look at places (and people) in this light. Despite the modest decor, Faculty Coffee grew on me fast, and not just because of the refuge it provided. It became a place. A real, proper place, not just a stop in the rain. And I'm all for finding flickers of reality in this fleeting world we inhabit.

> On the plus side, the coffee itself was quite alright. My filter was exactly what I expect when I order a V60, which I guess isn't something to write home about, but very welcome (like all familiar things), nevertheless. It had a nutty, citrusy vibe to it, and I can definitely say I tasted blueberries somewhere in the mix (to be fair, I can say almost anything, can't I?). It was also well-roasted, but without leaving too strong an aftertaste, which I wasn't really in the mood for.

> It was, in simple words, the perfect coffee to propel us onward in our journey. I also tried the flat white that my mum ordered, but it only made me stick to the idea that these are usually best ordered in mediocre coffee places, where the coffee wouldn't be amazing, anyhow. It has this tendency of drowning out the aroma too much. I think life's for tasting the full, bitter thing, you know? And it lasted just enough for the rain to get a chance to stop, and allow us to sneak through droplets and encounter these beautiful places~

> Having seen all my heroes take photos on the Black Sabbath bench around the time of Back to the Beginning, a stop at this hallowed spot was simply a must. And I gotta say, the day brightened (at least in spirit), seeing how proud of Ozzy and Sabbath that entire city seems to be. A hidden place, a spot out of the rain, a whole lotta soul. Birmingham, you did alright.

title.body:
🌿 Active Sunday – seems calm, but actually quite intense! 💪 ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/1a4c613a-459e-4a5f-9591-9a21804524de.jpg) This afternoon started very innocently… with a short walk with my husband ❤️ A bit of talking, a bit of laughter, a bit of silence – exactly what you sometimes need the most. Then it was time for the garden 🌱 Yesterday’s shopping couldn’t wait! Flowers, herbs, shrubs – everything slowly started finding its place in the flower bed. Dirty hands, tired back, but that satisfaction… priceless 😍 ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/4b428bbd-ef24-4b3a-bc44-f6e8d00e4488.jpg) The weather started to get worse, it became colder and more grey… But I don’t stop that easily anymore 😎 I put on comfortable shoes and added a few more kilometers of walking. A bit of the city, a bit of greenery, a bit of time just for myself 🌳 ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/b6c50bd4-e346-4d80-bf72-f6a2f992a749.jpg) After coming back – a quick dinner 🍽️ And… instead of the couch — workout 💥 New dumbbells + TRX = fire 🔥 Short but intense. I can feel my body waking up after winter and wanting more and more! ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/647319ab-e290-4209-823a-8a7281562d0d.jpg) At the end, a little reset at the beautician 💅 Because balance is the key – something for the body, something for the mind, and something for the soul ✨ ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/58aeabb8-fce4-45cc-b031-e0863574e9d8.jpg) 👣 Today done: 13,482 steps 💪 + strength workout 🌿 + outdoor work And you know what? These are my favorite kind of days ❤️ Seemingly ordinary… but full of life. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/0fa48e2b-aa07-4acf-8463-48bb1b8b1251.jpg) #actifit #active #lifestyle #familytime #fitness #motivation #gardenlife #polishgirl #healthylife #movingforward ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/61d2b6b1-17a4-4e75-8de5-7b548701cdd8.jpg) 🌿 Active Sunday – niby spokojnie, a jednak konkretnie! 💪 Dzisiejsze popołudnie zaczęło się bardzo niewinnie… od krótkiego spaceru z moim mężem ❤️ Trochę rozmów, trochę śmiechu, trochę ciszy – czyli dokładnie to, czego czasem najbardziej potrzeba. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/2dce9fca-6b09-4312-9d4d-ef6fdc890683.jpg) Potem przyszedł czas na działkę 🌱 Wczorajsze zakupy nie mogły przecież czekać! Kwiaty, zioła, krzewy – wszystko zaczęło powoli znajdować swoje miejsce na rabacie. Brudne ręce, zmęczone plecy, ale ta satysfakcja… bezcenna 😍 ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/a2fb1c25-292b-43b5-86e6-a7c2f9a6df14.jpg) Pogoda zaczęła się psuć, zrobiło się chłodniej i bardziej szaro… Ale ja już się nie zatrzymuję tak łatwo 😎 Wskoczyłam w wygodne buty i dorzuciłam jeszcze kilka kilometrów spaceru. Trochę miasta, trochę zieleni, trochę czasu tylko dla siebie 🌳 ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/2f7469ee-a500-41c3-a586-6292a64874b3.jpg) Po powrocie szybka obiadokolacja 🍽️ I… zamiast kanapy — trening 💥 Nowe hantle + TRX = ogień 🔥 Krótko, ale konkretnie. Czuję, że ciało zaczyna się budzić po zimie i coraz bardziej chce więcej! ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/2136a7e3-66ea-41e0-ba64-07a549dedf04.jpg) Na koniec jeszcze mały reset u kosmetyczki 💅 Bo równowaga to podstawa – coś dla ciała, coś dla głowy i coś dla duszy ✨ 👣 Dziś zrobione: 13 482 kroków 💪 + trening siłowy 🌿 + praca na świeżym powietrzu ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/f92a26eb-3661-47af-a3b8-d80cd41ec040.jpg) I wiecie co? Takie dni lubię najbardziej ❤️ Niby zwyczajne… a jednak pełne życia. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/e4852eb5-c67e-4d93-9a84-b96e6885f06e.jpg) #actifit #active #lifestyle #familytime #fitness #motivation #gardenlife #polishgirl #healthylife #movingforward

title.title: ECHOES OF FAITH IN BESKID NISKI
title.body:
![Kopia – Beyond the route.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23x1QD5Xdu2r2wH2ArZkCjVVR133L2o6WHXaMc6BZd4QFWdPJV3YuoarrwKg47oSXb5Lv.jpg)


I’m back after a few days’ break. This break, however, was not caused by my laziness but by a short city break. I flew to Italy for a few days with my sister and a friend. However today’s post will not be about that. I’m going back to Poland and to my recent trip to Gładyszów in Beskid Niski. As I mentioned before, I will be gradually presenting the churches that I managed to see in that area. 
The first one I chose is the GREEK CATHOLIC CHURCH OF THE ASCENSION OF THE LORD IN GŁADYSZÓW. This church was located very close to my accommodation, but I photographed it only on the last day. As it usually happens, the closest places often turn out to be the farthest. 😁 But every cloud has a silver lining. I managed to catch slightly better light, as the weather during most of my stay there was rather cloudy.

>Wracam po kilkudniowej przerwie. Przerwa ta jednak nie była spowodowana moim lenistwem, a krótkim city breakiem. Poleciałam sobie z siostrą i z koleżanką do Włoch na kilka dni. Jednak dzisiejszy post nie będzie o tym. Wracam z powrotem do Polski i do mojego ostatniego wypadu do Gładyszowa w Beskidzie Niskim. Jak wcześniej zakomunikowałam, będę po kolei przedstawiała Wam cerkwie, które udało mi się zobaczyć w tamtych okolicach. 
Jako pierwsze wybrałam CERKIEW GRECKOKATOLICKA PW. WNIEBOWSTĄPIENIA PAŃSKIEGO W GŁADYSZOWIE. Cerkiew ta była zlokalizowana bardzo blisko mojego zakwaterowania, ale sfotografowałam ją dopiero w ostatnim dniu. Jak to zazwyczaj bywa, tam gdzie mamy najbliżej, to okazuje się, że mamy jednak najdalej. Ale nie ma tego złego, co by na dobre nie wyszło. Udało mi się bowiem złapać trochę lepszego światła, gdyż w zasadzie przez cały okres mojego pobytu tam pogoda była dosyć pochmurna.


![20260321_170803.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/243fnFfFmDfXoD1NXu9oiDrAeecQQTMLJB5ccbQpBuoNwzPKFUAg8JaHp1u3s19x9DiuQ.jpg)

![20260321_170817.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/244xu6esccFAFAFxoZKVFepVunN3GTVWazM4PMkazBsUgj1tSt2JXVXx26wTYqkryZkQL.jpg)

This church was one of the ones I liked the most. Unlike the others, it had very nice, vivid colors and its shape was also slightly different from the rest. It was more domed. Unfortunately, I wasn’t able to go inside, as almost all of these churches were closed due to it still being outside the tourist season. So I had no choice but to admire it from the outside.

>Cerkiew ta była jedną z tych cerkwi, która spodobała mi się najbardziej. W przeciwieństwie do innych kościołów ma ona bardzo fajne, żywe kolory a i też kształtem odbiegała nieco od pozostałych. Była bardziej kopulasta. Niestety do środka nie udało mi się wejść, gdyż jak praktycznie wszystkie te cerkwie były pozamykane ze względu na fakt, że było to jeszcze poza sezonem turystycznym. Nie pozostało mi zatem nic innego, jak podziwiać ją z zewnątrz.


![20260321_171101.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/243WP9mS7w6VB1wEMXWrNEtQ3Thxjr7G1j3qism674P4soHQuCm6YLTFr2BaLoYuSVaoa.jpg)

![20260321_171220.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/244A2JWfD6bn9gCMwGLEPRB4VWq3LTfLuaXnm4giiFY8AWR2LZVWt2dh3cZEgcGv4xYyq.jpg)

The church in Gładyszów was built in 1938. These are relatively recent years compared to most churches in this region. Perhaps this is why it differs slightly in appearance from the others. The style in which this church was built is the Lemko style. It is a characteristic style for Beskid Niski. Its most distinctive feature is its domed form.

>Cerkiew w Gładyszowie powstała w 1938 roku. Są to stosunkowo młode lata, jak na większość cerkwi w tym regionie. Być może właśnie dlatego odbiega nieco wyglądem od pozostałych cerkwi. Styl, w jakim została zbudowana ta cerkiew, to styl łemkowski. Jest to charakterystyczny styl dla Beskidu Niskiego. Największą cechą charakterystyczną to właśnie ta kopułowa forma.


![20260321_171014.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/EqBci3J19fyhCm69aQbQD3EseVKCSD3VmtnRJso9QjdfSR7Z2koS2gnWRGRZtFt6y1B.jpg)

![20260321_170850.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/2458HmUssg9Fk6FEpuvcgZ7Vid1AJEc7GMVdjS1hoYnBQBXNx3dKsRuku2SDUpRQPHLHd.jpg)


The domes are a symbol of heaven, and the towers are topped with helmet-shaped roofs. It may not be visible at first glance, but the structure is made of wood. Inside, there is a so-called iconostasis, which is a wall of icons separating the sanctuary from the rest of the church. It’s a pity I didn’t get to see it with my own eyes. The church in Gładyszów was for some time used as a Roman Catholic church before returning to its original function.

>Kopuły to symbol nieba, a wieże zakończone są hełmami. Może nie widać tego na pierwszy rzut oka, jednak mamy tutaj do czynienia z drewnianą konstrukcją. W środku znajduje się tak zwany ikonostas, czyli ściana z ikonami oddzielająca prezbiterium od reszty świątyni. Szkoda, że nie udało mi się tego zobaczyć na własne oczy. Cerkiew w Gładowszowie przez pewien czas była kościołem rzymskokatolickim, zanim wróciła do swojej pierwotnej funkcji.


![20260321_170926.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/244KLcJb9WRLoTyXzA5yyTffuiehnR18fson4pEzsi7eofTTsRXCdzYg98Ywz1rPJAneA.jpg)

![20260321_170909.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/243q4ks1A8siNh1dn2CafhS8GiegXqqmVjpVM3sA5YzhKuGdneMwrhz9iVdqBTACiv7Qj.jpg)

![20260321_170830.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/244xwkGn9poGkQT58Gz6MD2nF9F3tUsDn7u7PseaaosKBVPf3GtuhgD1fWNZg8rWgGZQ6.jpg)

If you ever find yourself nearby, be sure to visit this church. Perhaps you’ll have more luck and manage to go inside.

>Jeśli będziecie kiedyś w pobliżu, koniecznie zajrzyjcie do tej cerkwi. Być może będziecie mieli więcej szczęścia i uda wam się wejść do środka.

title.title: Analog Phone
title.body:
![3585.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQhxWTYtELFA4s3PESjj8bDRuqG9hZhRwtEFoJhsRxybA/3585.jpg)

There’s a very particular kind of nostalgia tied to analog phones—something almost tactile and intimate that modern devices just can’t replicate.

Think of the old rotary dial sets. The slow, deliberate act of dialing each number—waiting for the wheel to spin back with that soft whirr-click-click. You couldn’t rush it. Every call required patience, almost like you were committing to the conversation before it even began.

Conversations felt heavier in a good way. You stood in one place—often near a hallway table or mounted wall unit—fully present. No walking around endlessly, no switching apps. If you talked for an hour, you stood there for an hour, maybe leaning against a wall, tracing patterns on the floor with your foot.

Even the endings were different. No abrupt “seen” or disappearing chats.Analog calls weren’t just communication—they were events. Small, ordinary rituals that carried emotion in every ring, every pause, every goodbye.

Saw this timeless beauty yesterday in a shop and I was hooked by her. Appreciate the thought process of the brand. Indeed it has become a fossil. For my kiddo this analog phone feels like a relic from another world. 😊

title.title: PhotoFeed Contest - Landscape - Peaceful Polly Joke.
title.body:
Hey everyone!

Back to Cornwall for this post!
Polly Joke (pronounced Polly Yoke) is a small cove just south of the [very popular Fistral Beach](https://peakd.com/hive-186141/@bombaycrypto/photofeed-contest-landscape-fun-at-fistral). A river winds down to it from a fishery through the hills before trickling over the beach. The runoff can be seen in image three.

It was incredibly peaceful compared to the usual tourist trap beaches.

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.47.01.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23zbFSZRveVX73rHXJNPDKXT4YkrkXbWb6Shyhzuzxf8cixKFFmU34YGSoNZU1upbdX4j.jpg)

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.48.05.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/242D9ystGr8Kt7FeaVfgGdTGaBoWy7Yw9meqrxh7djiXwAigYRsV53EyBZauVtLSWZyH3.jpg)

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.47.44.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23yTYq3rkxYn1Y9aLXatGp7LCpiLJxVhxEbwJXo51U5Khc1gn7us8DEx3EAofVvcMhWVf.jpg)

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.47.23.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23zRrMcZVX5YxPxiTkZztjcK23BarKqgwnydiiTR1na2qjAGNqEsfFbvPWJ3NjRCnJavs.jpg)

The landscape here is stunning. Small caves had been carved out from the waves crashing into the rocks. Looking along the coastline towards Crantock Beach along the top of the cliffs is the path.

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.48.21.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23zbFSZsZMBAZayJEQroxpK1hBmG6KEsVkPyfMJueLKC1UUv2HNwQKgDMgAPvUB2sWUAQ.png)
![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.47.34.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23yJ5dU8zihXezyjByYxFNJ6DJCp257erQUmHs13177Bhq23tkq3fFQXv5QCzgWCJVqVz.png)

The seals chose a cove that is not accessible by foot, even at low tide. The coastal path runs around the top of the cliffs, some hikers can be seen if you look closely. Of course I had no intention to fly close to avoid stressing the animals.

_______________

Crantock beach is a wide sandy beach with a gentle decline into the sea which makes for shallow waters quite far out into the sea.

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.48.59.png](10)![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.48.54.png](9)![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.49.14.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23xVJsMVJkNhxtJGBMpsrS9k4Z1wZbhqtJwLML52DUsh6GfpbeBxtBukUMxSKXmrEJg4a.jpg)

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.50.24.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23zkg3KMrfLWaebXkjoGbVkcqkecjFsmWGAky3zLSNhip7qAkCvTGaL8tt7xH61QxTXW8.jpg)

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.49.57.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23vhwy8yW9MqGVXnmVx7NxR4HTjBc2XrgckW16ffhneLdQs4Kao2vxbH652ncmftM5Mmh.jpg)

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.49.45.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23x1BAqzh2Y3Fv3NQ7sByVMENZbsb71oknfzFC4t2t1V1rx4AvsbuYF7AvcooEdTejfhr.jpg)

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.49.38.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/23ydAJGavwoPjwQnhEfUULPrXunKEsKVN8G78Ly9Rjt4qhbTEsWnzMTxJiQkRinxyqkPB.jpg)

![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.49.22.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/EoEqvVPZCdDCgeX3uL2Ue2NzuTk8Yj3Tm8sgmP8xBLK3yLi8ZPGvyN2aY1YnxY3Hnpk.jpg)
![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.50.13.png](15)![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.49.06.png](12)![Screenshot 2025-09-27 at 14.49.30.png](7)

On that day, the surf appeared to be similar to what comes in at Fistral. Unlike Polly Joke, this beach naturally has lifeguards. 

![Screenshot 2026-04-19 at 17.55.33.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/242rpeu13jmZtS1uR7p6Hd1BapXVJj3cs1gV1Sm1xFW76DqhAVXYpBx5oKGCkBjQdCv4z.jpg)

![Screenshot 2026-04-19 at 17.54.59.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bombaycrypto/242NgpaUe8cZswLik16JA5VDQPoqkZ574UspCzPZYrq3kg7PJHLPiZknZZ8xrvrvZiTx1.jpg)

Conveniently there is a carpark in the middle of both of these beaches, close to a small village so it's as safe as can be and has people milling around.

These two beaches are two of the nicest in the county that I have visited so far and I highly recommend a visit!

Take care everyone!

title.body:
# Learn Zig Series (#23) - Iterators and Lazy Evaluation

![zig.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaHuB6qTWHaSpJHQ1S8FCCRmNQuUxTcPZdU4yKHsJ7vEP/zig-banner.png)

### What will I learn
- You will learn the Zig iterator convention: `next()` returning an optional `?T`;
- You will learn building custom iterators for your own data structures;
- You will learn the `while (iter.next()) |item|` consumption pattern;
- You will learn lazy evaluation: computing values only when they're actually needed;
- You will learn chaining iterator adapters: map, filter, take, skip;
- You will learn memory-efficient processing of large sequences with iterators;
- You will learn comparing Zig's approach to Python generators and Rust iterators.

### Requirements
- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- An installed Zig 0.14+ distribution (download from ziglang.org);
- The ambition to learn Zig programming.

### Difficulty
- Intermediate

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Zig Series`):
- [Zig Programming Tutorial - ep001 - Intro](https://hive.blog/programming/@scipio/zig-programming-tutoroial-ep001-intro)
- [Learn Zig Series (#2) - Hello Zig, Variables and Types](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-2-hello-zig-variables-and-types)
- [Learn Zig Series (#3) - Functions and Control Flow](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-3-functions-and-control-flow)
- [Learn Zig Series (#4) - Error Handling (Zig's Best Feature)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-4-error-handling-zigs-best-feature)
- [Learn Zig Series (#5) - Arrays, Slices, and Strings](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-5-arrays-slices-and-strings)
- [Learn Zig Series (#6) - Structs, Enums, and Tagged Unions](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-6-structs-enums-and-tagged-unions)
- [Learn Zig Series (#7) - Memory Management and Allocators](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-7-memory-management-and-allocators)
- [Learn Zig Series (#8) - Pointers and Memory Layout](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-8-pointers-and-memory-layout)
- [Learn Zig Series (#9) - Comptime (Zig's Superpower)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-9-comptime-zigs-superpower)
- [Learn Zig Series (#10) - Project Structure, Modules, and File I/O](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-10-project-structure-modules-and-file-io)
- [Learn Zig Series (#11) - Mini Project: Building a Step Sequencer](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-11-mini-project-building-a-step-sequencer)
- [Learn Zig Series (#12) - Testing and Test-Driven Development](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-12-testing-and-test-driven-development)
- [Learn Zig Series (#13) - Interfaces via Type Erasure](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-13-interfaces-via-type-erasure)
- [Learn Zig Series (#14) - Generics with Comptime Parameters](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-14-generics-with-comptime-parameters)
- [Learn Zig Series (#15) - The Build System (build.zig)](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-15-the-build-system-buildzig)
- [Learn Zig Series (#16) - Sentinel-Terminated Types and C Strings](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-16-sentinel-terminated-types-and-c-strings)
- [Learn Zig Series (#17) - Packed Structs and Bit Manipulation](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-17-packed-structs-and-bit-manipulation)
- [Learn Zig Series (#18) - Async Concepts and Event Loops](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-18-async-concepts-and-event-loops)
- [Learn Zig Series (#18b) - Addendum: Async Returns in Zig 0.16](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-18b-addendum-async-returns-in-zig-016)
- [Learn Zig Series (#19) - SIMD with @Vector](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-19-simd-with-vector)
- [Learn Zig Series (#20) - Working with JSON](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-20-working-with-json)
- [Learn Zig Series (#21) - Networking and TCP Sockets](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-21-networking-and-tcp-sockets)
- [Learn Zig Series (#22) - Hash Maps and Data Structures](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-22-hash-maps-and-data-structures)
- [Learn Zig Series (#23) - Iterators and Lazy Evaluation](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-23-iterators-and-lazy-evaluation) (this post)

# Learn Zig Series (#23) - Iterators and Lazy Evaluation

Welcome back! Last time we went on a tour of [hash maps and data structures](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-zig-series-22-hash-maps-and-data-structures) -- `AutoHashMap`, `StringHashMap`, `PriorityQueue`, `SegmentedList`, the whole collection. In the exercises I asked you to build a contact book, an LRU cache, and a frequency-sorted word tool. If you did those, you've already seen the `.iterator()` pattern on hash maps -- calling `.next()` in a while loop until it returns `null`. Today we zoom in on exactly that pattern: iterators, and the lazy evaluation philosophy behind them.

In Python, you'd reach for a generator. In Rust, the `Iterator` trait and `.map().filter().collect()` chains. Zig doesn't have a formal trait system and it doesn't have generators -- but it has something arguably more transparent: a simple convention. Any struct with a `pub fn next(*Self) ?T` method is an iterator. No interface to implement, no trait to derive, no runtime overhead. Just a method that returns an optional. When it returns `null`, you're done. That's it.

This simplicity is deceptive though. Once you internalize the pattern, you can build pipelines of lazy transformations that process data without ever materializing intermediate collections. And because Zig gives you full control over memory, your iterators can operate with zero allocations. We'll build all of this from scratch today. Here we go!

## Solutions to Episode 22 Exercises

**Exercise 1** -- Contact book with `StringHashMap`:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{ wc.word, wc.count });
    }
}
```

HashMap for O(1) counting, PriorityQueue for ordered extraction without needing a full sort. The max-heap trick is to reverse the comparison -- we compare `b.count` against `a.count` so higher counts come out first. Three data structures, each doing exactly what it's best at.

Right, on to iterators! ;-)

## The iterator convention: `next() ?T`

Zig's iterator pattern is dead simple. An iterator is any struct that has a `next` method returning an optional. When the sequence is exhausted, it returns `null`. No interfaces, no vtables, no trait bounds. Just a convention that everyone follows because it works.

You've already seen this pattern in the standard library. `std.mem.splitScalar` returns an iterator. `std.mem.tokenizeScalar` returns an iterator. Hash map `.iterator()` returns one. `std.mem.window` returns one. They all follow the same shape:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{});
}
```

Python has `range(0, 10)` built in. Zig doesn't -- but building your own takes about 20 lines. And because it's just a struct, you can see exactly what it does, how much memory it uses (12 bytes: three `i32` fields), and when it allocates (never).

Let's do something a bit more interesting -- an iterator over a linked list:

```zig
const std = @import(\

approach is exactly what Python generators do with `yield`. The difference is that Python generators are built on coroutine machinery (stack frames, suspension points, the `yield` keyword) while Zig iterators are just plain structs with a method. There's no magic, no special compiler support, no hidden allocations. You can inspect the struct in a debugger and see every byte of state ;-)

## Iterator adapters: map, filter, take, skip

The real fun starts when you build iterator **adapters** -- structs that wrap another iterator and transform its output. This is how you build processing pipelines without allocating intermediate collections. Each adapter is itself an iterator, so they chain together naturally.

Let's build the most common ones:

```zig
const std = @import(\

which I'll admit is not the prettiest thing. In Rust you'd write `(0..20).filter(|x| x % 2 == 0).map(|x| x * x).take(5)` with method chaining. In Zig we're using free functions and nesting. It's more verbose, but the mechanism is completey transparent. You can step through it in a debugger and see exactly which `next()` calls which other `next()`. No hidden trait dispatch, no closure captures, no iterator fusion compiler passes.

## Memory-efficient processing with iterators

One of the biggest practical advantages of lazy iterators is processing data that's too large to fit in memory. Instead of loading everything into an array, transforming it, and then consuming the result, you process one element at a time and keep only what you need.

Here's an example -- imagine processing log lines from a large file, counting only the lines that match a certain pattern:

```zig
const std = @import(\

)` -- file objects in Python are iterators that yield one line at a time. Zig's version is more explicit (you manage the buffer), but the principle is identical: process data as a stream, not as a blob.

## Composing iterators with your data structures

Let me show you a more practical example that ties iterators back to the data structures we covered last episode. Here's a simple in-memory database of records where we use iterators to query and transform results without building intermediate collections:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{@divTrunc(total_score, @as(i32, @intCast(count)))});
    }
}
```

This pattern -- a data structure that exposes one or more iterator methods -- is extremely common in real Zig code. The standard library itself is full of it: `std.mem.splitScalar`, `std.mem.tokenizeScalar`, `std.mem.window`, hash map `.iterator()`, `std.fs.Dir.iterate()` for directory entries, and many more. They all follow the exact same convention. Once you know the pattern, you can read any Zig API that returns an iterator without looking at documentation.

## Zig vs Python generators vs Rust iterators

Let me give you a quick comparison because I know a lot of you come from Python (we've spent 22 Python episodes together after all!) and some of you may be looking at Rust too.

**Python generators** use `yield` to suspend a function mid-execution:

```python
# Python: lazy range with generator
def my_range(start, end):
    i = start
    while i < end:
        yield i
        i += 1

for x in my_range(0, 5):
    print(x)
```

Python's approach is ergonomic -- `yield` turns any function into a lazy iterator automatically. But there's hidden machinery: the runtime creates a generator object with its own stack frame, suspension state, and reference counting. You can't see how much memory it uses without profiling.

**Rust iterators** use the `Iterator` trait with method chaining:

```rust
// Rust: lazy range with Iterator trait
(0..20)
    .filter(|x| x % 2 == 0)
    .map(|x| x * x)
    .take(5)
    .for_each(|x| println!(\

, .{val});
}
```

Zig's approach is the most transparent. The iterator is a struct you can inspect. The `next()` method is a function you can step through. There's no hidden state, no runtime overhead, no trait dispatch, no closure environment, no compiler magic. The cost is verbosity -- you write more code to build the same pipeline. But when you're debugging a performance issue at 3 AM, that transparency is worth its weight in gold (trust me on this one).

All three approaches achieve the same goal: lazy, memory-efficient data processing. The tradeoffs are ergonomics (Python > Rust > Zig), performance transparency (Zig > Rust > Python), and runtime overhead (Zig = Rust < Python by a large margin).

## Exercises

1. Build a `Countdown` iterator that yields numbers from a starting value down to 0 (inclusive). Then build a `Zip` iterator adapter that takes two iterators and yields pairs (as a two-element struct). Test by zipping a `Range(0, 5)` with a `Countdown(4)` and printing each pair like `(0, 4) (1, 3) (2, 2) (3, 1) (4, 0)`.

2. Build a `ChunkIterator` that takes a slice and a chunk size, and yields sub-slices of that size. The last chunk may be shorter if the slice length isn't evenly divisible. For example, chunking `\

`. Then use your chunker to process a byte array in fixed-size blocks, printing each block's length and contents.\n\n3. Build a `FlattenIterator` that takes an iterator of slices and yields individual elements from each slice in sequence. For example, if the inner iterator yields `\

`, the flatten iterator should yield `'h'`, `'e'`, `'l'`, `'l'`, `'o'`, `'w'`, `'o'`, `'r'`, ... and so on. Test it with an array of string slices.

## Dus, wat we geleerd hebben

- Zig's iterator convention is a struct with `pub fn next(*Self) ?T` -- nothing more. When it returns `null`, the sequece is done.
- The standard library uses this pattern everywhere: `splitScalar`, `tokenizeScalar`, hash map `.iterator()`, directory walking, and more.
- Building your own iterator is just defining a struct with the right method. Custom iterators for linked lists, databases, generators -- all follow the same shape.
- **Lazy evaluation** means computing values on demand. An infinite Fibonacci iterator uses 16 bytes of state and produces values forever, no allocation needed.
- Iterator **adapters** (map, filter, take, skip) wrap one iterator to transform another. They compose by nesting, and the entire pipeline runs with zero intermediate allocations.
- For memory-efficient processing, iterators let you handle data as a stream rather than loading it all into memory. Same principle as Python's `for line in file`.
- Compared to Python generators and Rust iterators, Zig's approach is the most explicit and transparent -- more verbose, but no hidden runtime cost.

This iterator foundation is going to matter a LOT going forward. When we start looking at formatting output and working with debug/log streams, you'll see iterators pop up everywhere in those APIs too. The convention is simple but it's the backbone of how Zig handles sequences of anything.

Bedankt en tot de volgende keer!

title.title: The difficulties of the creative process... A story about how to beat the monotony of everyday life
title.body:
>When I was in college, I remember asking one of my advanced literature professors something that stuck with me ever since. I said, “Professor, if we’re hired for our ability to write, for our art, then what’s really the purpose of our talent?” He looked straight at me and answered in a way I’ve never forgotten: “We write, mainly, for ourselves. It might bring money or satisfaction sometimes, but authenticity always comes first. Always.” I don’t remember a lot from those years, but that moment is burned into me.

*\n\n*

>Being on HIVE feels like stepping into a digital jungle. Talent is everywhere, just one click away. I’ll never get tired of saying it, this platform is full of people who are genuinely brilliant at what they do. And that creates its own kind of pressure. As writers, we all deal with that, myself included. But there’s also this other layer that no one really explains clearly, the whole system of support, curation, and votes. Sure, we all want recognition, something that pushes us forward, but it’s not always tied to merit or effort.

* ![20241117_165520.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chris-chris92/23uFKWsx7DJiBnha9cjDvbd8eS6NVz3bGAaP32paBNXhqaNDnDhWeay4YpFt2SNmubV35.jpg) *

>I’ve been here for almost two years, and I still don’t fully understand how that system works. What I do know is this: every time I sit down in my living room, laptop open, ready to write, I do it for myself. To leave something real behind. To express who I am, what I feel, what I think. Writing is where my humanity shows up first.

*\n\n*

>Before I even decide on a topic, or which community to post in, or what images to include, I ask myself one thing: is this worth sharing? Is there something here someone else might feel or connect with? Sometimes I get it right, sometimes I don’t. There’s no formula, no guarantees. And honestly, that’s part of the deal. I’m not someone who enjoys sitting in complaints. But I have noticed something, writing as a way to live, to eat, to survive, can get heavy.

* ![20241202_124013.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chris-chris92/23tvc1E2VUCVGwMVs23vrsukry9f5131LnHbSd1GC7pMRxdFbxq48Pzh8mdoTdfmXFpsq.jpg) ![20241105_113849.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chris-chris92/23vhuW1Tc4BiHoK2Uvk5YwANZXnaQi8SCHqtdLUndUJKjWvQ6erLaSahYXK18vh5L7m5i.jpg) ![20241105_112121.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chris-chris92/23wqgR3vWrw9fmnC6HfUBTVeojexaFwSCWyWnwCPGB7bNF7rmU2dZCDTJFYV9cGch4hx4.jpg) *

>Because passion is the intangible part of this whole thing. Sometimes you’re dealing with schedules, expectations, productivity targets, and that’s exactly the part I push against. A few weeks ago, I was going through a rough emotional phase, and ironically, those were the best posts I’ve written this year. I even shared one in the reflections community called Raindrops, and yeah, I genuinely recommend it.

*\n\n*

>Right now, I feel more stable. More balanced between what I think, what I feel, and what I want. Sometimes I forget I’m human too. That I’m allowed to stop, to breathe, to step away for a moment and reset. I wouldn’t call what I go through writer’s block, not exactly. It’s more like waves. There are moments where I feel completely driven to write, and others where that fire just isn’t there. My life is far from perfect. If I don’t write, I don’t eat. That’s a level of pressure not everyone really understands. Freelancing has its beautiful side, no doubt, but it also comes with a kind of vulnerability that’s hard to explain. You depend entirely on the present moment. And there isn’t always much empathy for that kind of life.

*\n\n*

>So I deal with the monotony the only way I know how, by turning it into something worth telling. By trying to do something meaningful with whatever I have in front of me. I am who I am. I do what I’ve always known I love. And more importantly, what I know sets me apart. Finding that space where passion, talent, and instinct meet is something we owe ourselves. It might fail sometimes, sure. But what it gives back, to your mind, your identity, your sense of self, that’s impossible to measure. Veni, vidi, vici.

* ![IMG_20241005_110352_771 (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chris-chris92/23vhRXV75ibUQnn1PzC7acZMhmGPYGjH5EphWivHDE8FikMDxcuX9QvXk9knx5hupoenq.jpg) ![IMG_20241005_110422_372.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/chris-chris92/23u5bYDemupXPrTaCvpLAmjUPxEBHhfH4mqJzsRX44csXGRwCX6cwEuToYVchmavfwntY.jpg) **

title.title: Never Alone: {Kisima Ingitchuna} [Let's Play] - 04
title.body:
* -- The Narrator

----


**Never Alone: Kisima Ingitchuna** is a puzzle platformer with co-op mechanics. The story is set in Alaska, following the girl *Nuna* and her fox companion in a journey to find the reason behind the non-stop blizzards hitting her village. Never Alone also comes with documentary-style clips about the lives of the Alaskan people.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcSDyrq1GVeM4GSxoS3FAy9BjRvW9kyFnGAzZQsYP6BQ9/NeverAlone_VeniceAI_lUm6dhT.webp 

This game is the definition of gaming as art. Folklore and platforming are interlaced together. The puzzles are challenging enough to require trial and error but easy enough to not require a guide. Never Alone can be finished in one setting if you know all the solutions. It required me about 3+ hours of interrupted gameplay to finish.

The best part for me is how *indie* it feels. From the emphasis on folklore to the small twists. Made me think, which parts are real beliefs of people living there, and which are purely fantastical? Despite the clunkiness of the game bugs, (which I encountered a few,) the main parts are all beautiful!

I got this game many years ago, and played the first level more than once. I'm glad I finally got to experience the full story. *would want to play again!* Now you get to see my experience:


----

title.title: KADR POKAŻE // POLSKIE KRAJOBRAZY I NATURA // POLISH LANDSCAPES AND NATURE // FOTO GALERIA #12
title.body: ## POLSKIE KRAJOBRAZY I NATURA FOTO GALERIA #12

> Na przełęczy Klekociny zastaliśmy słońce już w dość zaawansowanej fazie zachodu. Pięknego zachodu. Trochę żałuję, że nie zabrałem statywu lub filtra gradacyjnego. Ciężko było te zdjęcia obrobić przy tak mocno kontrastowych scenach. Mając statyw ze sobą, wykonałbym bracketing — trzy ekspozycje o różnej jasności, które następnie połączyłbym w Lightroomie, tworząc jeden obraz. Z takiego połączenia można wydobyć znacznie więcej szczegółów niż z pojedynczej klatki. Przy tych zdjęciach zdecydowałem się na skupienie na jasnych partiach, aby ich nie prześwietlić, tracąc przy tym sporo szczegółów w zacienionych miejscach.
### POLISH LANDSCAPES AND NATURE #12
At the Klekociny Pass, we found the sun already well into its sunset phase. A beautiful sunset. I regret a bit that I didn't bring a tripod or a graduated filter. It was difficult to process these photos in such high-contrast scenes. Had a tripod with me, I would have done a bracketing—three exposures of varying brightness, which I would then combine in Lightroom to create a single image. This combination can extract significantly more detail than a single frame. For these photos, I decided to focus on the highlights to avoid overexposing them and losing a lot of detail in the shadows.

title.title: Not My Regular Kinda Sunday.
title.body:
Hi guys 🤍


Today is not my usual kind of Sunday it didn’t go as planned.

I had an appointment with a client, and she couldn’t meet up at first. Honestly, I almost cancelled because I really value my time.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaxMeystTArgFDX8o6jVtdffZ2DhwN3LVcW9nWwdLxcM1/1776617691740.jpg)


 But she later called to apologize she had just arrived Aba from Lagos the night before for a wedding.

Well, I ended up doing her makeover, and before I knew it, my service time was already up. Since I had prepared for my weekend meeting, I just headed back home and joined via Zoom.

This week has been fruitful, engaging… and stressful. I didn’t even get my usual alone time, and I could feel it. But still, I’m grateful for so many things.

Even while feeling stressed and tired, I made out time to read something uplifting.


And then something clicked....

**I just realised that We don’t have to have everything together before we show kindness or give to others.**



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWm9aB9pXFdGVwuhUnQ9RQXgWafCarHAT4XREUgiPoJ2s/1776617557909.jpg)
>My clients before make-up 

It’s in the little things  small acts of kindness, small moments of sharing that matters a lot.
 they bring a kind of peace and joy that’s hard to explain.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYpVYJUD8dPhsTXxWhGy6DPRrX3TWqCACjhTEUmw1erCq/1776617596971.jpg)
>My client after makeup.

So yes, my Sunday didn’t go as planned, but it still turned out meaningful in its own way 🤍

As we step into a new week, let’s create opportunities to share what we have — our time, our presence, our finances… anything that can uplift someone.

How is your Sunday going? 😊

title.body:
Hello friends and hello PhotoFeed community, a nice day to everyone. Here I am writing a new blog this week, and after many weeks without doing so, I am participating in the Macro Photography category. I have regained a bit of searching and observation in the field, and I think this photo deserves to be shared with you. I hope you enjoy it. This will be my entry for: [📸 PhotoFeed Contest - Macro Photography Round 166](https://ecency.com/created/@photofeed/photofeed-contest-macro-photography-round-166).

> Hola amigos y hola comunidad de PhotoFeed, lindo día para todos. Aquí estoy escribiendo un nuevo blog esta semana, y después de muchas sin hacerlo, participando en la categoría de Macro Photography. He recuperado un poco la búsqueda y observación en el campo, y creo que esta foto merece ser compartida con ustedes. Espero la disfruten. Esta será mi entrada para: [📸 PhotoFeed Contest - Macro Photography Round 166](https://ecency.com/created/@photofeed/photofeed-contest-macro-photography-round-166).

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdnV4hsgx1SmfQYZwN9cmpcyqQ2siVKM9mu91PPEWGerx/20260414_165223_01.jpg)


The photo I share with you today is of a small spider that was resting on a green leaf, near it a small cocoon that served as its nest. After later identifying the spider, I found out that it is an orb-weaver spider from the family Araneidae. Araneids (Araneidae) are a family of araneomorph spiders composed of nearly 3,100 species divided into 169 genera, it is the third most diverse family, after Salticidae and Linyphiidae. Most build their webs in a circular spiral shape and remain in them with their heads facing down. So it is a very common species, but that does not make it less interesting, besides, I think it is very photogenic. Thank you very much for reading this little entry, and as always, I encourage you to share your opinions and tips for photography in the comments. Best wishes, all the success in the world, and see you next time. Bye bye!

> La foto que les comparto hoy es de una pequeña arañita que descansaba sobre una hoja verde, cerca de ella un pequeño capullo que le servía como nido. Una posterior identificación de la araña obtuve que se trataba de arañas de telas orbiculares, familia Araneidae. Los araneidos (Araneidae) son una familia de arañas araneomorfas compuesta por casi 3100 especies divididas en 169 géneros; es la tercera familia con mayor diversidad, después de Salticidae y Linyphiidae. La mayoría construyen sus telas en forma de espiral circular y se mantienen en ella con la cabeza hacia abajo. Así que es una especie muy común, pero esto no la hace menos interesante; además, creo que es muy fotogénica. Muchas gracias por leer esta pequeña entrada, y como siempre te animo a que me compartas tus opiniones y consejos para fotografía en los comentarios. Un gran saludo y todo el éxito del mundo, hasta la próxima. ¡Chau chau!

title.title: Concurso de la comunidad Ladies of Hive #285 \\ Ladies of Hive Community Contest #285
title.body:
Saludos apreciada comunidad de Hive, bienvenidos a mi participación en el Concurso de la comunidad @LadiesofHive #285: preguntas para esta semana a cargo de la dama @merit.ahama. 

>Greetings esteemed Hive community, welcome to my participation in the @LadiesofHive Community Contest #285: questions for this week by the lady @merit.ahama.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS4jwUEAFU6BtLdVHeTPxnLmEyvvsVyM12ZX8DRojzRi1/1776616947162.jpg)

1- ¿Cuál es un libro, vídeo de YouTube, película o lección de vida sobre el autodesarrollo que realmente le ha impactado? Podría tratarse de habilidades, dinero, propósito, relaciones, salud o crecimiento personal. Comparte lo que te enseñó y por qué lo recomendarías a otros.
Los 7 hábitos de los adolescentes altamente efectivos de Sean Covey, un libro que compre para mi hijo menor cuando estudiaba 4to año de bachillerato, fue exigido por uno de sus profesores, no estoy segura si lo leyeron e hicieron reflexionas sobre sus contenido. 
En los tiempos de pandemia lo tenía en la biblioteca y empecé a leerlo, realmente es un libro de crecimiento personal que me ha gustado mucho, un manual para la autoestima y el éxito, este libro avarca las situaciones más difíciles y decisivas de un adolescente, les da las herramientas necesarias para organizarse, tomar mejores decisiones para construir la vida que quiere vivir. 
Son siete lecciones que nos habla sobre la importancia de adquirir buenos hábitos, el pensar ganar, ganar, busca primero entender y luego ser entendido la importancia de tomar buenas decisiones, la necesidad de hacer equipo para lograr un buen equilibrio y como tienen en sus manos su propio destino. 

>1-.What is one book, YouTube video, movie, or life lesson on self-development that has truly impacted you? It could be about skills, money, purpose, relationships, health, or personal growth. Share what it taught you and why you would recommend it to others.
Sean Covey's *The 7 Habits of Highly Effective Teens*, a book I bought for my youngest son when he was in his junior year of high school, was required reading by one of his teachers. I'm not sure if they actually read it and reflected on its content. During the pandemic, I had it in my library and started reading it. It's truly a personal growth book that I really enjoyed, a guide to self-esteem and success. This book covers the most difficult and decisive situations a teenager faces, giving them the necessary tools to get organized, make better decisions, and build the life they want to live. It contains seven lessons that address the importance of acquiring good habits, the win-win mindset, seeking first to understand and then to be understood, the importance of making good decisions, the need to work as a team to achieve a good balance, and how they hold their own destiny in their hands.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZLQmz4mrm7esXaJ2nY1tMruugzu9WEKZqjFh51Sutvdp/1776617048406.jpg)

 >2- Right now in your life, what feels like your main reason for living?
How would you describe your purpose at this moment, and what keeps you moving forward each day?
I have many reasons to live, starting with the fact that I have a wonderful God who gave me life, filled me with blessings, and made me exist. For me, simply existing is a reason to live. I live for my family, the fundamental base of society, the ones who sustain me. They give me reasons to laugh, to be happy, and to want to get up every day with hope and gratitude. My reasons for living are endless and simple, like enjoying a delicious coffee, feeling connected to nature, having people to share a conversation with, an afternoon dancing with my granddaughter, talking with my siblings, helping someone in need, witnessing a sunset, being mesmerized by the sea, the arrival of night and admiring an illuminated sky, that smell of damp earth that reminds me of my essence, and many other things that make me believe life has meaning, and I have more than enough reasons to live it. I believe my purpose in life is to live, to live consciously, purposefully, in presence, in acceptance, with gratitude, with values, learning from every circumstance, from disappointments, from pain, from falls, always acting from understanding, compassion and not from anger; purposes evolve with us and do not always have to be tangible.

2- En este momento de tu vida, ¿cuál crees que es tu principal razón para vivir? ¿Cómo describirías tu propósito en este momento y qué te mantiene avanzando cada día?
Razones para vivir tengo muchas empezando porque tengo un Dios maravilloso que me dió la vida, me llenó de bendiciones, me hizo existir y existir  para mi ya es una razón para vivir, vivir por mi familia la base fundamental de la sociedad la que me sostiene, me dan motivos para reír,  para ser feliz y querer levantarme cada día con mucha esperanza y gratitud. 
Mis razones para vivir son infinitas y sencillas como disfrutar de un delicioso café, sentir el contacto con la naturaleza, tener personas con quien compartir una conversación, una tarde bailando con mi nieta, hablar con mis hermanos, ayudar a alguien que está en apuros, presenciar una puesta de sol, hipnotizarme ante la presencia del mar, la llegada de la noche y admirar un cielo iluminado, ese olor a tierra mojada que me recuerda mi esencia y otras muchas cosas más que me hacen creer que la vida tiene sentido y a mi me sobran motivos para en ella.
Creo que mi propósito en la vida es vivir, vivir con conciencia, con propósito, en presencia, en aceptación, con gratitud, con valores, aprendiendo de cada circunstancia de las decepciones, del dolor, de las caídas, de actuar siempre desde la comprensión, compasión y no desde del enojo, los propósitos evolucionan con nosotros y no siempre tienen que ser tangibles.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTC11QNFt6j1W4UhxpmNKDHcfQvT1gA7A8cqN61RTpgq8/1776617154673.jpg)

title.body:
![ChatGPT Image 16 apr 2026, 15_42_21 p3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zumzulik/23w2cS8ZkqsZZHKQUjLrymwT2HSHqT2fvmkUnhwebfnBQ2bf4tcBvHSAXfwyEigB35FhT.png)


###Questa immagine è stata generata da me grazie all’ ausilio dell’ Ai###
###This image was generated by me with the help of AI###


Ciao a tutti, io sono Omar, ma qui su **Hive** mi conoscete come zumzulik.

Questo è il primo capitolo di un racconto in tre parti. Prima di parlarvi di come gioco oggi senza vedere, voglio portarvi indietro nel tempo, a quando il mondo per me era fatto di luci, sfumature e dettagli che oggi posso solo immaginare.
La normalità della luce
In questa prima fase della mia vita, vedere era scontato. Ricordo la libertà di muovermi senza esitazioni e la bellezza di perdermi nei colori. Se chiudo gli occhi, il ricordo visivo più potente e prezioso che conservo è il viso di mia moglie. Lei è stata ed è tutto per me: amica, compagna, amante. Quel volto è l'immagine che tengo più stretta nel mio \

personale.
E poi c’erano i colori. Il rosso, in particolare, è sempre stato il mio preferito. Un colore vibrante, caldo, pieno di energia, che ancora oggi riesco a visualizzare perfettamente.

##Una vita in movimento e i primi mondi digitali##

La mia quotidianità era fatta di autonomia. Ricordo bene la sensazione di stare al volante: guidare per me non era solo spostarsi, era libertà pura. Sentire la strada e avere il controllo totale del mio spazio era qualcosa che davo per garantito.
Anche nelle mie passioni ero immerso nelle immagini. Amavo i giochi strategici, dove dovevo tenere d'occhio ogni angolo della mappa, e passavo ore su Minecraft. Costruire mondi, scegliere i materiali, vedere le proprie creazioni prendere forma blocco dopo blocco... era un'esperienza visiva totale. In quel momento, la tecnologia era \

un divertimento, non avrei mai immaginato che un giorno sarebbe diventata il mio ponte sensoriale per restare connesso al mondo.

##Un tesoro di immagini##

Raccontare questo periodo serve a farvi capire da dove sono partito. Quei ricordi sono le fondamenta su cui ho costruito la mia nuova realtà. La mia mente ha conservato ogni sfumatura, e sono proprio quelle immagini e quelle ore passate a costruire su Minecraft che oggi mi aiutano a dare una forma a ciò che sento o tocco.
Verso il cambiamento
Ma la luce, purtroppo, non è eterna. Nel prossimo post affronterò la parte più scura del mio percorso: il momento in cui i contorni hanno iniziato a farsi sfocati e la paura ha preso il posto della sicurezza. Vi racconterò il declino.

Grazie per essere qui a leggere la mia storia.

Il vostro
Omar/zumzulik

##Come promesso, complimenti a @pharesim74, ho visionato il sito **hivecomb.net** e voglio ringraziarti perl' ottimo lavoro di accessibilità che hai svolto. È semplicemente perfetto.##
Version traslate with AI

 My Life in Full Color#

Hi everyone, I’m Omar, known here on **Hive** as zumzulik.

This is the first chapter of a three-part story. Before I tell you about how I play games today without sight, I want to take you back in time—to when the world for me was made of lights, shades, and details that today I can only imagine.

##The Normality of Light##

In this first phase of my life, seeing was something I took for granted. I remember the freedom of moving without hesitation and the beauty of getting lost in colors. If I close my eyes, the most powerful and precious visual memory I hold onto is my wife's face. She has been, and is, everything to me: friend, partner, lover. Her face is the image I keep most closely guarded in my personal \

And then there were the colors. Red, in particular, has always been my favorite. A vibrant, warm color, full of energy, which I can still visualize perfectly today.

##A Life in Motion and the First Digital Worlds##

My daily life was built on autonomy. I clearly remember the feeling of being behind the wheel: driving for me wasn't just about moving from A to B, it was pure freedom. Feeling the road and having total control over my space was something I took for granted.
Even in my passions, I was immersed in images. I loved strategy games, where I had to keep an eye on every corner of the map, and I spent countless hours on Minecraft. Building worlds, choosing materials, seeing your creations take shape block by block... it was a total visual experience. At that time, technology was \

fun; I never imagined that one day it would become my sensory bridge to stay connected to the world.
A Treasure of Images
Sharing this period helps you understand where I started. Those memories are the foundations upon which I built my new reality. My mind has preserved every shade, and it is those very images and those hours spent building in Minecraft that help me today to give shape to what I feel or touch.
Towards the Change
But light, unfortunately, is not eternal. In my next post, I will face the darkest part of my journey: the moment when outlines began to blur and fear took the place of confidence. I will tell you about the decline.

Thank you for being here to read my story.

Your 
Omar/zumzulik

title.title: The Still Frequency\n
title.body:
The old man sat at the base of the tower when Kofi arrived.

  
There was no vehicle or bag I site. Just a wooden stool, a tin cup, and the nonchalant posture of an old man who had nowhere better to be at all. He was old in the way we would sing as kids, _“ ancient of days”_ to anyone we felt was too old. His face was filled with maps of deep lines, his hands enormous and scarred, his white kaftan so bright against the brown plateau something Koffi felt was odd for an old man.

  
Kofi, by contrast, looked exactly like a young technician that he was. Dressed in his dirty jeans and reeking of three days' unwashed odour. In his hands was his equipment worth more than his monthly salary; he had the look of a man who hadn't slept properly since the static started.  
\
Kofi said.  \nThe man looked up slowly. \
The man sipped from his cup. \
He nodded at the ground beside him. \

Kofi sat although he didn't fully understand why he was listening to a stranger.  
The plateau held a silence so complete it had texture, like it was listening to them. The winds ad chirpring insects added a calm background noise. No cars could be heard coming up from the valley roads below.  
\
he asked.  \nThe old man nodded and poured from his flask. \

Kofi opened his mouth. Closed it. “How could you tell that…”  
“Life is hitting you?” The old man laughed. “Have you looked at yourself in the mirror lately. Or don’t you have one?”  
Koffi looked away.  
“So when last?” The old man laughed again.  
Yet Koffi had no reply.  
\
the man said.  \nThe silence returned. This time, Kofi didn't fight it.  \n\
Koffi said. He hadn't planned to say it. “Hurts me till today.”  \n\
\nThe old man repeated the word like he was tasting it. \

Kofi laughed, “You already know.”

The sun was hiding now. The hills went fully dark. The tower's red warning light could be seen clearly now. Sitting there in the dirt beside a stranger koffi found something he had been searching for for years.  
Stillness. Actual stillness.  
Not the kind that comes with tiredness, but that chosen quietness of someone who had, at last, decided to take a break.  
\
he asked, standing finally.  \nThe old man considered this with great seriousness. \

Kofi picked up his equipment and walked up to the tower. He ran his diagnostics and filed his report. His discussion with the old man is still on his mind.

  
That night, he called his brother. Just to talk and maybe apologize after years of missing his wedding.

  
That night, he took a leave from work. He needed time to live a little from his usual routine of work and home to work lifestyle again. He also knew it was time to visit family and friends and make amends for his absence.
