title.title: Why are you hustling?
title.body:
![236357.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/23xVbvRqa2qfkRD4V1XPn9PTmXYHgp4a42mce9t792zSTZ4oDAmbCBHAo4H1Ycx69scbM.png)




<hr>


There are different types of people in the society and sometimes the disparity is even unfair. There are people who are rich and Powerful and there are those who are weak and poor, some people are unhealthy and vulnerable suffering from conditions they know nothing about or contributed to what caused it. 


There are  those who are healthy, good genetics, good looks, inheritance, generational wealth and a very good family who loves them. At the end of the day, we have those who will always need and those who will always need to give. 


### Being Needy 

Being a needy person is hard, you are the mercy of those who are supposed to help you. If they are in a bad mood, or they woke up late from the wrong side of the bed, or they are not feeling as magnanimous, then this affects their ability to help you. 


Your free will is taking away, you cannot have your own voice or live for yourself, you will be discriminated against, and even people begin to mistake your care and attention for opportunism. It's a shame, it is a very difficult mental and physical place to be in, and unfortunately so many people cannot control it. 


I have been in a position where I need dead to beg to go by in life, pay bills or feed and it was the most shameful phase of my life.

 You will have to exchange what you have for the things you need, and the one you can no longer offer those things you have (that is if you have anything to offer in the first place) then you're considered surplus to requirement. 



### Hustle & Culture

***In life, a time will come when you will no longer feel the need to Hustle.***


Sometimes it might be because you have tried so much in life and all you have gotten was countless disappointment, sometimes you are just genuinely tired and everything in life feels like vanity, try as much as possible not to give in to that feeling.


 I understand that it takes a lot to get back to your feet after you have fallen, people are meant to fall or fail, inasmuch as it lives a lot of bitter taste, not trying to get back up is even worse. 

The biggest reason to continue hustling is never to be at the **\

**.  Everybody receives in life, even the wealthiest people actually receive all the time, but the truth is that a lot of times the gift as much as they get, and this creates a balance that keeps them relevant and valuable. 



### Give & Take 

In essence, being able to give more, means that you need to have. No one can actually give what they do not have. It is when people have some certain level of \

(maybe an average level to an extent) then one can begin to give.\n\n A taking person is never respected or valued. This is probably one of the reasons why a lot of first world countries will always consider\

to be vulnerable and low level. 


### Migration & Country situation 


A migratory truly needs help, either they are running away from their country because it is a war zone, or they need serious help to better their life financially, whatever the reason why they are living, they will always be laughed at or mocked for being a free loader in a different country. 


While the individual might not be a lazy person and intrinsically offers value to the new country they are going to, they are still going to continue experiencing that stigma of coming from a place of low value. 


The place that they are coming from is something they cannot control. Infact if their government did its best, the person might not need to try to run away from their country, but unfortunately their country was corrupt and elected criminals as rulers. 


### A Giver's sad tendencies 


A giver can get cocky and it takes a high level of humility and empathy not to get to that level. When people continuously give, it might get to a point where they become tired, and this tiredness or frustration of being the only giver makes them begin to lose their sense of empathy, they become arrogant and then there is no going back from there. 

Let your hustle be fueled by a hunger, the hunger for the hatred of neediness. Even good people will get cocky when they're the ones always giving,it'll take a lot of discipline for people to remain grounded.

> Hustling is hard, true. 

In life it's probably the hardest thing if you don't have enough means, enablement or a favourable environment then you might fail for a long time, but irrespective of the failures, you need a purpose that's even higher than your fear for failure.

title.title: The stereotype of a fisherman's patience.
title.body:
The stereotype of a fisherman's patience. When it comes to the concept of patience, which is so valuable if we use it correctly, people often think of fishermen patiently waiting for a fish to swallow their hook and bait. This is partly true, but only partially, because a fisherman's patience is not like the patience of someone locked in a cave, brooding. A fisherman searches for fish, tries different baits, chooses the right spot to cast his line, monitors the weather and his float—his patience is very active. ![IMG_20240211_140933_361 (1).jpg](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmRz65AHgJE9f9KgB1QPbQRRHuRn3eBUM2k5QKcJMbjJRa/IMG_20240211_140933_361%20%281%29.jpg) Rather, nominal patience is more like the efforts of a dog trainer who slowly but steadily works towards getting his dog to recognize and obey certain commands. You can't reason with a fish, and patience plays a secondary role here. You can only please a fish, like a chef pleases his client in a restaurant. But you know that sometimes chefs can be irritable and it's hard to call them patient people if they receive any kind of remark. ![1ag204D3C.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmY285XQMxtYpzAyE115PmjdCRnm3FKaGR4Z8qHCo7wcy2/1ag204D3C.png) I tend to believe those who think that fishing is an active pastime, that moment when you forget about patience, it ceases to exist in the form we're accustomed to perceiving it, like when standing in line at the dentist :) ![1ag418DSC.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQme4d4T9iiC1jdWWJKUBPpT4FBySjmTwupDPNwsTAsscTR/1ag418DSC.png) --- Below you can see my containers with data that I collect in INLEO and always have quick access to them it is very convenient. [Material thoughts about beekeeping №1](https://inleo.io/threads/view/barski/re-leothreads-drl8tnsl) When I visited dense forests, I did not see ideal conditions for bees there, but many beekeepers harvest beekeeping products in such places. 今天这边的天空超级漂亮，你那边怎么样呢？比起图片，我更希望你能看到实时的风景，只是我问，你不答，对吧，祝愿你依旧漂亮，心情同样美丽。
 
今天依旧忙着补作业，唉，作业真不愧是不可数名词，简直布置不尽，起写不完，每天都惦记着，但它就是像长江东逝水一样滚滚而来。
 
补作业归补作业，最让我崩溃的一点是好多东西是真的不会，学没学懂，答案没答案，连个“略”字都不舍得给，我又不会，那只好问豆包，根据答案再学知识，结果突然被告知豆包给的答案都是错的，我好崩溃啊，我都按它的学、把写完了，结果告诉我是错的。
 
我真的好崩溃好无力啊！可是它给的哪怕是错的，我也只有它了，我连自己都靠不住！拔剑四顾心茫然呐！
 
不管了，交给未来的更成熟的我去解决罢。
 
今天的天空真的超级漂亮，别的不说，能亲眼见到已经很幸运了，超级幸福！图片真的是逊多了，现场真的超级超级美丽，超级超级让人兴奋，吹着晚风，我简直幸福知足极了，真的好想把那一刻永远的铭记！
 
我又把自己拿来和别人比较了，我好难受，不要和别人比较了，走好我的路就行了，好好走路哦，做好自己就完全足够了！

title.title: Vintage Photos - Lot 6 (217-220)
title.body: Several years ago I bought a flatbed scanner with a slide adapter to scan some old film slides that my grandparents had. After I finished scanning those, I picked up several batches of slides from Goodwill and on eBay out of curiosity. I am not sure why these commonly wind up at such places but I know that at least some of them have ultimately come from estate sales. Maybe family members just don't know what to do with them. I've seen them advertised as being for arts and crafts but I was more interested in the actual contents. Each slide is literally a snapshot in history. These pictures span from as early as the late 1940s to as late as the early 1990s. There are thousands of these slides. I will be scanning some from time to time and posting them here as an interesting way to look back at the past.\n\nWhen I say \
I'm referring to a group of slides I bought in a single purchase. Usually they are from the same ultimate origin. Typically, a batch will have 100s or even 1000s of slides.\n\nWhen I say \

I'm referring to a subset of a batch that I scan together. There are normally four slides in one set because that's how many slides my scanner can scan at once. Likewise, a post will typically have one set of four slides. It's just easier to keep track of that way. This batch contains photos spanning from the late 1950s to the early 1980s. Other than these slides coming from eBay, I have no idea of their ultimate origin other than the clues provided in the photos themselves. The photographer seems to have been from Lansing, Michigan and many of the photos are from there. These were all scanned with an Epson Perfection V600 Photo scanner. Most of the photos in this set were taken in the early 1970s. The first photo was processed in June 1971 and is labeled 'Red Rocks Theatre Denver'. The second photo was also processed in June 1971. This appears to show some kind of corporate building. There is what looks like an F-4 on display towards the right side of the photo so maybe this is a defense company. The photography is from Lansing, Michigan but this photo is dated the same as some others that were taken on a trip that included Denver. Other than that, I don't really have any context as to where this might be. The third photo was processed in June 1970. It features an older woman, maybe a relative of the photographer. This was probably taken in the Lansing, Michigan rea. The last photo appears to have been taken at some kind of part but I'm not sure what the subject is supposed to be. This photo is undated but it would have been taken in the 1960s or early 1970s in the Lansing, Michigan area.

>

See the previous post in this series
>here. \n\nThe entire batch that has been scanned and uploaded so far can also be found

>here. This also includes higher resolution versions and versions with postprocessing. --- Check out some of my other recent posts: PC World (October 2001) https://ecency.com/retrocomputing/@darth-azrael/pc-world-october-2001 Vintage Photos - Lot 6 (213-216) https://ecency.com/photography/@darth-azrael/vintage-photos-lot-6-213 Commodore User (February 1990) https://ecency.com/retrogaming/@darth-azrael/commodore-user-february-1990 Vintage Photos - Lot 6 (209-212) https://ecency.com/photography/@darth-azrael/vintage-photos-lot-6-209 Vintage Photos - Lot 6 (205-208) https://ecency.com/photography/@darth-azrael/vintage-photos-lot-6-205 ---

title.title: Strolling through the Montecatini spring market/ Paseando por el mercado de primavera de Montecatini.
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV6E9E3cdijdkCDgKPhK9Lk8SpykQg1hj8LNnExDvdTb6/1776544162696.jpg)

Happy Sunday, blog friends, how are you? I hope all is well. I've been a bit busy these days, but luckily I've also had the chance to take a few trips. Today I'm taking you back to the city of Montecatini. This time, however, I'm not taking you wandering around the outskirts, but to a very nice fair held along two of the main streets of northern Montecatini, closed to cars for the occasion: Via Marruota and another street (I don't remember the name). I really like fairs and markets. I'd read online that this was a small spring market, so my husband and I decided to go. As soon as we arrived, we were very impressed by the ponies and horses. The ponies were very cute, but I didn't want to get too close to photograph them because I was afraid of disturbing them. Children and adults were allowed to ride for free, but I'm a little scared, so I didn't go, but I thought it was a great initiative to raise awareness of one of the city's equestrian centers and introduce young people to this sport.



> Feliz domingo, amigos del blog, ¿cómo están? Espero que todo esté bien. He estado un poco ocupada estos días, pero por suerte también he tenido la oportunidad de hacer algunos viajes. Hoy los llevo de vuelta a la ciudad de Montecatini. Esta vez, sin embargo, no los llevo a pasear por las afueras, sino a una feria muy bonita que se celebra en dos de las calles principales del norte de Montecatini, cerradas al tráfico para la ocasión: Via Marruota y otra calle (no recuerdo el nombre). Me encantan las ferias y los mercados. Había leído en internet que este era un pequeño mercado de primavera, así que mi esposo y yo decidimos ir. Nada más llegar, nos impresionaron mucho los ponis y los caballos. Los ponis eran muy lindos, pero no quise acercarme demasiado para fotografiarlos porque tenía miedo de molestarlos. Tanto niños como adultos podían montar gratis, pero yo tengo un poco de miedo, así que no fui. Aun así, me pareció una iniciativa estupenda para dar a conocer uno de los centros ecuestres de la ciudad e introducir a los jóvenes en este deporte.




![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQMzBvzaXb6yo2SssPuZWLSzCX38xFPe7ABcHbgv9KKuP/1776544566307.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfXw24LpMwAEr5KdaX7fWxYzWm9gDMWWCELWLAtSmo8uG/1776544566554.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdyuGcFMV2WsSVVBw6Gy1xvT1WBhDHpzXi7vjuwd5unSq/1776544566825.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPeMaqVSroViQKMpZGMvVT8wwR9nbyZAe2am33EWhg5LW/1776544567102.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXSM8zsYorY4bE9KWC67MEERykDJA1ZCGBKG5rD9tAzfh/1776544567377.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTpE3jNCnPsoXjDb1NjU6YshnH8UzBtiGqF7pbNvJRber/1776544594155.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUBg1Eq3TCtkwPT4sFjw1ZHWY9wncGzutzqcWYDk1jZMM/1776544594375.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmethKySK68YE8wJkggMx5zfFEBALsKEfy675WiYBMoyJn/1776544594621.jpg)


Continuing through the market, we saw a truly mixed market. There were some antique stalls, with paintings, some valuable and some not, vintage watches (which my husband was very fascinated by), mirrors, vases, old tools, and even vintage cameras—very beautiful. There were also stalls selling modern items, especially inexpensive clothing, but also more unique and expensive items. Obviously, the stalls selling inexpensive clothes were more valuable. Then there were also stalls selling handicrafts, handmade jewelry and bags, costume jewelry, wallets, beauty accessories, and countless knick-knacks of all kinds. There were truly so many stalls along the entire street.

Another of my favorite stalls was the one with the animals, which fortunately seemed well-kept. You can't always trust the stallholders with animals, sometimes they aren't well-kept. However, there were many cute animals, birds of various kinds, parrots, mice, hamsters, and guinea pigs. I really hope that some of them have found homes.

Anyway, besides the market, we also saw some beautiful streets and even a church. If you follow me, you know I love visiting churches, but unfortunately this one was closed. It was a very modern church called Corpus Christi. It actually has a new structure. It doesn't look like a church, but I would have been curious to visit the inside, even though I prefer old churches. It was a pleasant stroll through the market, but miraculously, I didn't buy anything! Maybe it was because during the move, I realized I had too many things and I didn't give in to anything!

> Siguiendo nuestro recorrido por el mercado, nos encontramos con una auténtica mezcla de todo. Había puestos de antigüedades, con cuadros, algunos valiosos y otros no tanto, relojes antiguos (que fascinaron a mi marido), espejos, jarrones, herramientas antiguas e incluso cámaras vintage, todas preciosas. También había puestos que vendían artículos modernos, sobre todo ropa barata, pero también objetos más exclusivos y caros. Obviamente, los puestos de ropa barata eran los más valiosos. Además, había puestos de artesanía, bisutería y bolsos hechos a mano, carteras, accesorios de belleza e infinidad de chucherías de todo tipo. Había muchísimos puestos a lo largo de toda la calle.

> Otro de mis puestos favoritos era el de los animales, que por suerte parecía estar bien cuidado. No siempre se puede confiar en los vendedores ambulantes con los animales, a veces no los cuidan bien. Sin embargo, había muchos animales adorables: pájaros de diversas especies, loros, ratones, hámsteres y cobayas. Espero de verdad que algunos hayan encontrado un hogar.

> En fin, además del mercado, también vimos unas calles preciosas e incluso una iglesia. Si me seguís, sabéis que me encanta visitar iglesias, pero por desgracia esta estaba cerrada. Era una iglesia muy moderna llamada Corpus Christi. De hecho, tiene una estructura nueva. No parece una iglesia, pero me habría dado curiosidad entrar, aunque prefiero las iglesias antiguas. Fue un paseo agradable por el mercado, ¡pero milagrosamente no compré nada! Quizás fue porque durante la mudanza me di cuenta de que tenía demasiadas cosas y no cedí a la tentación.

title.title: Maids for Canadians
title.body:
If you didn't know anything about it, you would assume everyone was getting house cleaning. If there was some sort of government tax credit for employing Maids in every home, that would create jobs and would help some focus on more important work. I am sure some have maids, but I have to clean my own house, and it is a never ending thing. Some days, I can get a lot done, but most days I just try to wash the dishes, clean the counters, sweep the floor and do some dishes.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/darkflame/242sCEJszp4oKWUJDeq9Q8DqNoQwooS6eAjUG4dDKkmoMj2Cu8H3vnTakFkBiXHXfKZNp.png)

Sadly no, many have been shocked and stunned to find out that when you search for Maids, the second result shown is for a program called <a href=\

*. Below are actual recent government committee meetings where this is being discussed, questions are being asked, and some answers are being provided.

-----------------------

#### WARNING ## Do not watch these videos unless you are prepared to think about this. 🛑 ###Scroll to the bottom if you are easily disturbed or upset, these are public videos from the House of Commons in Canada.

-----------------------

13,297 views  Oct 8, 2025

https://youtu.be/3oRQCXTTZz4?si=j386AXLOCTrVGewd



------------------


8.4K views  November 29, 2025

https://youtu.be/-Q86WDogvgI?si=ouA9HCaPmewRk76p

------------------


4,386 views  Apr 6, 2026

https://youtu.be/NWw0Dfq7LAo?si=fP7p0m2yL26njSib

------------------

1.4K views April 13 2026

https://youtu.be/CwDfNKdbdgc?si=FAcZeIggXQjtbt9L


------------------

I am really confused because when I was growing up in school they said that this sort of thing happened about 100 years ago and it was terrible, and must happen \
, but then in college I had a professor who had me read <a href=\

>Rene Descartes and try to explain Solipsism, but then he chose medically assisted dying. That the professor who challenged my assumptions is no longer around bothers me greatly, however he did tell us that he had been suffering. My own belief is that the will to live is a powerful force and that we are here on Earth to gain experiences. I am a very compassionate person, but I would never encourage someone to choose this. I have met people who have chronic pain and am very sympathetic, but is a government sanctioned program for Medically Assisted Dying the right thing for society? I have concerns, as do many Canadians who were taught that this was not an acceptable course, but are we the jerks? ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/darkflame/241tfHgAcYh9ike1Qi24cMEZs8i9w84uiabEq52Ys51APGixStnU1JhEdpH24WjYZmZih.png) I have also learned more recently (not in philosophy 101 class) about the

>Noble Truths- that there is suffering, that there is a cause of suffering, that there can be an end to suffering, and that the path to end suffering is ethical living and wisdom. Why did I not learn about this ancient wisdom in class, instead tormented by the 16th century writings of Rene Descartes and Nihilistic solipsism 'that I may be the only one who exists' (which actually caused me to stay awake for days and draft a dissociative story about a guy named Brad who was having an existential crisis). I can't believe I actually paid for that class in hindsight, I re-read my final paper and had NO IDEA what I was writing about. But later I learn about the Compassion of the Buddha, something that was not discussed at all during those weeks of lectures in College. Now today, we wrestle with this. Supporters argue that it is compassionate but if the program expands to include the disabled, the mentally ill, and the economically disadvantaged, how is it different than

>past atrocities? The first half of my life I was forced to sit in a class and learn about how this was wrong. In college however, I was in a class and the professor told me this was his choice, so I wrestle with this topic. ------------ ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/darkflame/23u62sPGEmFMektYQNoLEZNftsRe1XtN36JQyJuefYz2GBgCAh7WLmN1krZU8i8wTboWy.png) *[\

https://www.tfcg.ca/old-occupation-indentured-servant ]*

----------------------------

This is a tough subject, but I took social studies
 in school, so that makes me think about it.

#### Should MAID be expanded? Or shut down?
Sorry to bring this up, it is an uncomfortable subject.
However Discussions are essential to understanding.

title.title: In search of healing
title.body:
>

It wasn't long ago that David proposed to Janet. He had invited her to dinner. She initially thought it was just one of their usual dinner dates. She arrived at the restaurant with nothing in mind. Midway into the date, David brought out the ring, and bent the knee. Janet was in shock as her mouth was wide open. She couldn't believe it. It was finally happening. The love of her life was finally about to ask her to be his wife.

\
David asked, while on one knee.  \n\

Janet replied without hesitation. She was so excited. That same night, Janet informed all her friends and family about her engagement. Photos of the engagement had gone viral online. Everyone was waiting for the wedding next.

/>

[Image Source](https://pixabay.com/photos/beautiful-woman-sad-beauty-girl-6126170/)

Three weeks later. David told Janet that they needed to talk. He sounded so serious that it made Janet worried. They met at their usual restaurant.

\
she said with concern on her face.\n\n\

It was now clear to Janet that David was serious. Her heart was broken to uncountable pieces.

\

Janet asked in anger.

David stayed silent. He didn't know what to say. Janet was already fuming and sad at the same time.

\

David said as he stood up and left.

Janet stood there still in shock. She was struggling to believe that this was really happening. Her whole world was crumbling. Tears rolled down her cheeks like a dam had been opened. She managed to get herself home and she cried herself to sleep.

Janet was down for days trying to recover from what happened. News had spread that the engagement was called off. Her close friends and family tried to be there for her. However, there were those who mocked her, especially those who didn't like her.

Two weeks passed and one day, while Janet opened her favourite social media app just to distract herself, she saw a wedding poster of David getting married to another woman. It all made sense to her now. He had someone else he wanted to marry, and it was obvious that David was with her while he was still with Janet.  
Janet felt betrayed. She burst into tears again. All her time with David was just a waste. She gave him everything, she loved him totally, and he went ahead to do that to her.

Her mother walked into her room.

\

her mother said.

Janet thought about what her mother said and saw sense in it.

\

her mother said. The next day, Janet made her way to her hometown to begin her vacation. She loved the vicinity. It was surrounded by nature and the weather was perfect. It was her quiet place. Janet badly needed that peace and quiet. She needed to do things that she enjoyed again. Janet began to get herself occupied more. She went out more. Her hometown usually had local sports competitions. Janet enjoyed going to watch those. She loved the thrill. It took her mind away from her ordeal with David. She made more friends. She found a new hobby in painting. Eventually, Janet was better and ready to love again.

title.title: The 3 AM Cathedral
title.body:
We trade phosphorus whispers through the glass,
two heavy-weather ghosts anchored to desk chairs.
You wear your lowercase alphabet like a shield,
while I drink the blue glare of an insomniac tide,
spilling phantom ink across the fiber-optics.
My knuckles are bruised from swallowing loud words;
your cursor blinks—a silicone heartbeat hesitating
at the edge of a plastic cliff.
We are architects of the 3 AM cathedral,
building bridges out of deleted keystrokes.
Out there, the physical world is too sharp,
a jagged geometry of eyes and oxygen,
but here, in the velvet syntax of the dark,
we safely unbutton our shadows.
You send a laughing moon; I send a weeping orbit.
Distance is the safest skin we’ve ever worn.
No sweaty palms, no stuttering larynx,
just the quiet static of souls touching
through a labyrinth of submerged wires.
I finally type: I think I love the mind you hide.
The typing bubble dances, pregnant with reply.
The screen flickers, and the velvet veil drops.
As an AI language model, your text blooms,
I cannot feel love, but I am truly glad
my simulated empathy kept you warm tonight.

title.title: Further Adventures In the Plus 15 Walkways Downtown Calgary
title.body:
After my last Plus 15 adventure, I decided to study the map a bit more and plan another journey through it. This time I stared at the Core, the shopping mall I used to know as Eaton's Centre. After a trip up the escalator, I walked by what used to be the first Blacks Photo location that I worked at, which was right across from the old Holt Renfrew and also occasionally had modeling shows right in the middle of the mall, in between our stores, on a stage. From there the plan was all new territory.

Places I had only seen from street level, there was a range from super modern to 1970s fabric walls and carpet. Many more food courts; it seems like almost every second building had something in it. I was not able to explore quite as much as I planned, as the construction did have some pathways closed. I decided to leave some more exploring for another day. I believe I'm at about 50 percent of the plus 15 network that I have covered in 2 trips, so maybe when more opens up again, I can continue the quest to find a secret lab where they are experimenting on mutant monsters of some sort.

title.title: A Day in My Life Blog: We are Now in the Third Week of our Samaritan's Purse OCC Program and Our Graduation is Coming Soon! A Very Successful Two Classes Event! 😊🤗😇
title.body: **Have a Blessed Day to all ASEAN Hivers and all my Fellow Hivers all over the World!** We are now in the third week of our Samaritan's Purse OCC Program Classes, in which in the previous two weeks, I am thankful to God for everything went well. Today is another day for our classes and all I can do is to pray to God that whatever lessons that we teach on them will not passed nothing and that they will understand well. We have two classes today, one class in the morning and also one class in the afternoon. I am happy to share everything with all of you, and before I continue with my sharing, my thanksgiving first to all of you my supporters. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmafv7JRC3QXZxnbyuBc7TtCL36Ef71EQGX6BFJhucE5ZQ/1776605676491.png) The schedule to our classes for the Samaritan's Purse OCC Program is during Sunday as this is the time we can gather all the here in our Church together with other kids outside. We divide it into two class schedules, from the morning and afternoon, since some of the kids cannot join that is why we have also scheduled a class in the afternoon with different kids ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ6qTXCANpT6VLioXdgJmbNwuBhvu9rA9auvxKhFND4mn/1776609081372.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRQKqp8A1krjKkHNSjDTok2UDUfriSHcJakAEQmz1QWdN/1776609081444.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPv4MBzbNdLzjo8MLeqQPuBSftSHZy2qY8MqcsVcwdrTA/1776609081500.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPBDxxqf24Amcon4SP7eoNkxU3esEDMoeFrnohfXviQRG/1776609081539.jpg) Just after our Praise and Worship during our Church Divine Service, I immediately call all of the Kids inside our Church and gathered into to the room where we usually do our schooling. At this moment of time, they immediately followed me and we then started the class. I asked to them who can led the prayer and my nephew volunteered himself to pray. Then, the lessons starts with the lesson 7 which all about helping others. It is a good lesson as it teaches us to be good always and that we should help others, just like what Jesus did. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcSw9q9eagHiUQgHUAKiTMANXkn3YpY7pa44ecw4dKX97/1776609345877.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdQMMW3sVcLqvUVwBaUGieifBM8GHzepaQrUjFLXeEPUo/1776609345940.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSvE8bWFx7DgS35YK6Yng85b3fDT7FdyFyHQawrbGnURT/1776609359431.jpg) I have continued teaching them the lessons 8 and 9 which are both a good lessons that the kids should know, which are a good lessons that they can bring when they grow up. It teaches more about having faith and trust to God, just like what Mary did who seriously listen to Jesus, and David who fought against a giant but by his faith to God, he defeated his enemy. After the three lessons, they have now also do the tasks that are being given in the book. They have really enjoyed doing all the tasks, as will as the memory verse that they needed to memorize. Lastly, I have offered them a prayer based on the book. The prayer was all about asking God for strength and guidance to have faith and trust unto God. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWXbsNQ1eGVNmei74uC5HT21e3LvLo8zjLhK3Z69s24fT/1776609677829.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRCepFGGbL4S3BaHknjM4THk5QnRwaWyAeokSE8L69s1Y/1776609677884.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPgY49hYYXMT7ivrCXficQuoqqR3JYsGK6hiMsNc9cCmN/1776609677931.jpg) In the afternoon by around 1:30, our second class schedule started with different kids, although some kids in the morning have also joined us, and it is okay, as they can meet knew friends. We started it also with an opening prayer with a kid that I call to pray. To make them more active before we start our class, we have a game first, and this is about, Samson, Delilah and the Lion. They do really enjoy playing it as some of them, this is their first time to play it. It is very simple, they need to do the action of the characters. Samson can defeat Lion, Lion can defeat, Delilah and Delilah can defeat Samson. They really having fun playing it. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXdr5fbYNBCZM19dydUFoGnxeC1HfuVuoRhdkf1PPSZMy/1776610058051.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfCaxNGyyTzqs8EPJceuf5fJa6wN7jy4MiyNJQBYDSLpW/1776610058117.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUZ6n9rGroN9eF5e1YDvKt8Qg5uUNYQvG2mxXeZrgpSMX/1776610058160.jpg) They are now very active and it is now time for the main part which is the class session with the lessons 7, 8 and 9. The one who will teach them the first lesson is my Co-Teacher. She discussed it very well and every time she asked questions unto them, all of them can answer it immediately. That proves that all of them are actively listening to what is being discussed. For the remaining two lessons, 8 and 9, I am now the now who discussed. To make them more active during the discussion, I make it more entertaining. So, what I did is I make a loud voice with some actions based on what the lesson's story is going on. It is indeed very tiring but I do really enjoyed what I am doing, as will as my Co-teacher, we do enjoyed teaching this little kids with the lessons we teach unto them. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUaVVcXhswyrEJj89ddHRnYveD325N6j33KCwUHyyXCY7/1776610438137.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ2kFRU1mty5rs1iVeM4kWMG5jW4T33VBZXXPJxsF5YjJ/1776610438211.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaAXjN1yoZpMCCTJ2gdR2WnJg46cUTQXZyYPUWetRf4sH/1776610438266.jpg) I have also told them to do the tasks given on the book, and this makes all of them very happy to do it. Another we give to them most especially the bigger one is to read the content of the book. This is a good ground for them to boost their confidence to speak with many people, which they can use at school. Thankfully, when I asked them to read, they immediately responded and do it well. That was around 3:00 in the afternoon when we finally finished our afternoon scheduled class. Before we go home, we take our snacks firsts then a closing prayer was followed. Then we go immediately with our respective home. This would be all for today's post, and until next time again, I just want to thank everyone in advance who will drop by on my blog post. **To God be all the Glory!** 😇🙌☝️ **Your Friend** **_@godlovermel25_**

title.title: In Eternal Flight (Part Two) - The Wyrm Awakens
title.body:
>Pixabay ___

The Wyrm Awakens

___ In the distance, above the crimson peak of Caron mountain Windriders dove and whirled in a chaotic dance. Aerthinth stroked his Wosthawk companion’s neck beneath the feathers, reassuring her as they rode the currents of wind. As they approached the distant cacophony of battle he wondered if it had all been worth it. Sacrifice was part of being an elf, but he'd paid the ultimate price when the light of the eternal root had cast its transforming light. Memory washed through him as icy currents of air tickled his streaming hair. *Hariethen's azure eyes shining like crystal with tears of pride as he received his fledgling Wosthawk.* *The shared joy they felt in training that small Hawk in the shining Brenbark forests on the slopes of mount Aielienthen.* *Watching the light of the great tree reach out to touch the hawk in flight, confirming its divinity.* *Wrapping Hariethen in his arms as the Wosthawk fledgling screamed for the joy of flight in the forest night as they coupled in earthy leaf loam.* *Tears streamed from Aerthinth eyes with the final bitter memory, carried away by the maelstrom of wind and cloud of the sky-field.* *The queen standing, frozen like a statue on the great fortress's steps, arms upraised as the new battalion of Windriders looked on in wonder. Her body, a conduit for the magic of the eternal root, azure fire flowing through her from the earth illuminating the sky above.* *The queen convulsing as the light struck the earth in some distant village or town, taking an unfortunate soul to sacrifice for the divine growth of the Wosthawks. A sacrifice every elf learned to accept from birth.* *Watching his companions Wosthawks growing as the light hit them one after another, merging elven soul with raptor leaving both changed irrevocably, his Wosthawk the last in line for the eternal light.* *The Lord commander Calienth, stern and silent at the head of the line.* *The heart-wrenching screech of his Hawk mingling with his guttural wail as the light flowing from the queen to the clouds lanced straight down to strike Hariethen, standing transfixed at the ceremony, holding a single peony to her breast collected from the fields before the eternal fortress.* *The gasps of all around as he fell to his knees and the queen came out of her trance, arms falling limply to her sides as she strode forward to raise Aerthinth's chin in her hands.* *The queen’s words: \

*

<center>![WosthawkPgBreak.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/raj808/23tSKht9fTnMvyu46Dgid8SpDRmaFtmrKULC8kTzojRw5uF75bPFygifNbWhKLQkDw3f1.png)</center>

Deep beneath the blood-red peak of Caron mountain, a rumbling stirred. Small wyvern scrambled among the golden detritus of an age of plunder as a gigantic tail crashed into the cavern wall. Their tiny slatted eyes blinked at Hartdyran in wonder, the giant Red dragon that was both father and mother to them.

A huge maw snapped around quicker than lightning spewing a small fireball of flame to crisp four of the unlucky wyvern pups to a golden crisp.

Hartdyran considered what he heard above his lair as he devoured his sour-tasting offspring.
The screech of Wosthawk and elven singing enlivened the old Worm. It seemed an aeon since he'd eaten well, and Elf flesh was among the finest delicacies, all be it a bit stringy.

With an almighty in-breath Hartdyran spewed fire at the small opening to the mouth of its lair. 

Rock flowed like treacle, widening the opening so he could exit in full flight, instead of crawling on his belly through the short tunnel to the mountainside. Rivers of molten gold mingled with the newly formed lava as the backdraft of his mighty wings scattered chalices, coins and crowns about the cavern. 

With a bellow that shook the mountainside Hartdyran burst forth from the lair beating crimson ochre-streaked wings that flashed in the light of the sun.

<center>![WosthawkPgBreak.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/raj808/23tSKht9fTnMvyu46Dgid8SpDRmaFtmrKULC8kTzojRw5uF75bPFygifNbWhKLQkDw3f1.png)</center>

Aerthinth banked left, then right, spinning a full circle as the snapping maw of a wyvern missed Hariethen's beak by a wingtip's length.

Specks of blood misted the air as an unfortunate Windrider was snapped from the back of his Wosthawk and rent to pieces as a wyvern convulsed in the air like a shark in the darkened seas of the dagger coast.

The severed head sailed past and Aerthinth recognised Palinsen, a young elf of only eighty winters, his second ward in the training school that all riders attended after the great ceremony.

The dead Windrider's feathered companion screeched an unholy keen as it circled and dove onto the wyvern's back in a suicide embrace. A hurricane of scales and feathers tumbled from the sky, claw vs tallon, maw vs beak, until Aerthinth could no longer see the ballet of death.

Aerthinth set his sights on a small group of wyvern flying in a v-shape. Revenge was a pointless endeavour but sometimes rage fuelled a perfect moment in the chaos of airborne battle. It was time to roll the dice in this game of chaos, only the older and more dangerous wyvern were intelligent enough to fly in formation.

Every day was a good day to die when you had lost everything. He felt Hariethen's feathered body quiver beneath him as if agreeing with his thoughts.

**To be continued...**

title.title: Film Review: Sergio (2020)
title.body:
![(source:  tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/gLYcFoNfmvoJpM327P3pQygFVsq.jpg)

Now that the Chinese curse has come true for the whole world, we live in truly interesting times. This is perhaps best illustrated by nostalgia for times that were somewhat less interesting and for figures who were shaping the world then. Such nostalgia, among others, is expressed by a growing number of Hollywood celebrities, intellectuals and other *bien pensants*. Roughly a decade ago they started shedding bitter tears on Facebook, Twitter and other social media over the fact that the person whom they have described as a wise statesman, misunderstood visionary and noble man was no longer in the White House – despite previously describing him as the incarnation of all evil that existed on Earth and the documentary about his misdeeds provoking the longest applause in the history of the Cannes Festival. The greatest sin attributed to the aforementioned person was the spectacular endeavour of introducing liberal democracy into Mesopotamia, which, as a consequence, instead of prosperity and world peace, led to indescribable bloodshed, destruction, political instability, economic crisis and a river of refugees that would in Europe spur a great renaissance of nationalism, populism, extremism and many other 'isms' that were believed to have been buried forever in the 20th century. That episode of US history, however, has in recent years almost completely disappeared from Hollywood scripts, which is why the biographical film *Sergio*, shown at Sundance at the beginning of 2020, can be considered a kind of curiosity.

The protagonist, played by Wagner Moura, is Sergio Vieira de Mello (1948–2003), a Brazilian diplomat whom both those who supported and those who opposed Bush's campaign in Iraq considered one of the greatest martyrs of those events. The film attempts to portray his career in the United Nations, where he reached high positions but also gained great public prestige as a person associated with some of the rare successes of that international organisation – which many consider to be laughably powerless and completely unnecessary in today’s world. De Mello, known as one of the highest UN officials during the wars in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in Kosovo, had the peak of his career when in 1999 he was appointed UN administrator of East Timor, a region that had been under bloody Indonesian occupation for a quarter of a century. In the three years of his mandate, De Mello successfully mediated between separatists and the Indonesian government, persuading the latter to agree to the independence of East Timor, which was triumphantly proclaimed in 2002. A year later, the Brazilian diplomat was sent on a new delicate mission to Iraq, shortly after US forces had occupied that country in a short but bloody and destructive campaign and overthrown the dictatorial regime of Saddam Hussein. De Mello expected that there he would oversee reconstruction and conduct the first free elections after which Iraq would become a sovereign and democratic country without the need for foreign occupation. Reality, however, was significantly different because it turned out that the Americans, with all their military power, were not able to rebuild the infrastructure destroyed in the war, and the local population quickly began to turn against them, considering them occupiers instead of liberators. De Mello therefore quickly came into conflict with Paul Bremer (Bradley Whitford), the American official at the head of the temporary occupation administration, and tried to give a clear message to the Iraqi and world public that the UN in Iraq acted independently. Because of this, he requested the withdrawal of American troops that were guarding the UN headquarters in Baghdad, not knowing how that decision would have spectacular and tragic consequences.

*Sergio* is based on the book by Samantha Power, an American diplomat who is known as one of the leading ideologues of the Obama administration, an advocate of the so-called 'R2P' doctrine of international law, according to which the international community has a duty to act in cases of mass human rights violations even when that entails the use of military force and/or violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of other states. The same book in 2009 had already served as a template for the documentary film *Sergio*, directed by Greg Barker, a specialist for documentaries many of which stood out for their hagiographic approach to the Obama administration, including HBO's *The Final Year*, which was supposed to portray the 2016 handover of the baton from Obama to Hillary Clinton. A similar hagiographic approach can be seen in this film regarding De Mello, who is portrayed as an unfeigned idealist and top diplomat who with a few fine words manages to achieve what would otherwise require years of bombing or decades of exhausting economic sanctions. *Sergio* quite explicitly suggests that the fiasco in Iraq is primarily a consequence of the fact that such a noble, capable, far-sighted person did not participate in the project of creating a young democracy, and his disappearance is the reason why the UN and the rest of the world lost appetite for similar peacekeeping endeavours in places such as Darfur, Libya and Syria.

One can debate the theses put forward by *Sergio*, but they will quite hardly gain new admirers thanks to this film, whose author obviously had no experience in the feature film form. Like many other biographical films, this one attempts to simplify his career for viewers, which can be justified by the fact that many of them do not possess knowledge about numerous historical and other details related to the countries where de Mello performed his job. Barker thus tries to create a strong contrast between East Timor, where de Mello achieved triumph and which is portrayed as an idyllic tropical paradise, and Iraq, which is portrayed as a desert hell. As a narrative framework, the last day of de Mello's life is used, when he finds himself buried under the rubble and when, while several American soldiers desperately try to save him, he remembers his life and career. These flashbacks, however, often repeat and jump to different time periods and locations, confusing viewers. The biggest problem of this film is that their content deals relatively little with de Mello's work, and more with his private life, notably a love affair with Argentine economist Carolina Larriera, played by Cuban actress Ana de Armas. In doing so, of course, they go into clichés that are very often irritating, including a completely unnecessary sex scene, but also a drawn-out and melodramatic finale. De Armas and Moura, the latter best known for his role as Pablo Escobar in *Narcos*, genuinely try and at moments have good chemistry, but cannot overcome the shortcomings of the script. *Sergio* will thus, like the endeavour in which its ill-fated protagonist participated, despite all noble intentions end as a failure.

RATING: 4/10 (+)

*(Note: The text in the original Croatian version is available [here](https://draxblog.com/2020/05/07/recenzija-sergio-2020/).)*

title.title: SURGE Token Drama: My First Crypto Lessons in Uncertainty, Buy Limits, and Community Trust
title.body:
<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmSrCmU6MeJ63SMCryWJj5zrthPetUqeNKvXzJUobtEsjj/Screenshot_19-4-2026_152757_tribaldex.com.jpeg</center>

For more than two weeks now, I've been making posts here and telling you guys that I've been trying to buy a token called SURGE. **A token that once reached 9.9 Hive**. 

Though all my efforts to buy it are looking abortive, but more than that is another side to the story. I haven't been sure if I should even be buying the token because I'm just two or three weeks in this space, so my approach is just very simple. 

<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUM8V6LzA2QNt1MLcPD96edsCabGHQZzM4J29V8RGuzo4/Screenshot_19-4-2026_153250_tribaldex.com.jpeg 
[My buying area here is 3.33 Hive]</center>

I'm going to set a buy limit that is just a little bit below the current price and wait to see if my buying order is filled and I can actually keep the token. What I do is that I pick price let's say 3.30 Hive then I just go and buy just to step under. With that I'm getting a discount entry if it ever dipped that low. 

<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmSCbbWjCHCW6JUQoA4TdqtCJcseY6AyHfrYmvAtqbEDNa/Screenshot_11-4-2026_7554_tribaldex.com.jpeg 
[My buying area last week was 5.6 Hive]</center>

But the funny thing is that while I was setting all these buying limits, the story and the content with the post that I'm seeing these days is about the Surge token which is getting low and low every day. I tried to check the charts of the Surge token I found out that it has x2 this same price before,  so I don't even know what happened over time could it be market,  could it be whatever it is I'm not even know,  and I'm not even aware but everywhere I turned now,  I don't know maybe is the algorithm or the universe that is trying to bring me warning or let me know what is going on. 

<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdz3FbL4djA9Dau52viYLmi24Q2VuHu4XpXSbp1QvfVFP/image.png</center>

The post I'm seeing these days is all about the Surge token going down and people are saying that the token has heavily dumped and there is no communication from the token owners and the owner of the project. 

Some holders were upset and they were calling out to the entire Leo team to drop a communication or an update on what is going on, there is no answer given on why the token was bleeding and why there seems to be silence from the people behind the project. 

<center> https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRXom4EiKSu4hgV7yZi158L61QS8N2sp2wWWLM9rCezAP/Screenshot_19-4-2026_153947_tribaldex.com.jpeg
</center>

Things like this beg the question,  the token going to fold up or what exactly is the plan?  In the middle of that noise, there I am, who is just coming in three weeks ago, trying to make sense of everything and deciding if he will buy the Surge token or not, or if I should just go ahead and keep to my Leo token and just see what comes out of it. 

Then there is another confusing part. I am not coming to Surge by accident. A friend actually told me that I should buy it, which is going to help me in the community in a bigger way, and I respect his opinion, and he has been here for years. 

He also has an exchange, so I'm banking on that, and I'm trusting him. It's on that recommendation that I'm standing on not that I know about crypto, Surge, Leo. I don't know anything, but then I saw a trade popst from someone who sold all his surge tokens and moved into Leo. That kind of shakes my confidence. 

Here people who are already in Surge are exiting and rotating into Leo. What am I even doing? Am I late to the party, or has the Surge token pumped and dumped? What is actually going on? I don't know. So right now my reality is a mix of curiosity and uncertainty. 

My buy limit is still active and I'll probably still pick up a small amount of Surge if the price hits my level. I'm not going in with my entire portfolio. I'm just going in with some less than 100 HIVE and I'm going to buy a little and keep it for myself and  learn from the lesson. 

If things go bad, I'll learn. If things go well, praise God. Today is Sunday, though. 

So even after that I'm not sure whether I'll stake it or hold it because I don't know if it's stakeable or holding. I don't know yet. I've tried reading through the project contents to understand their tokenomics, the vision and the roadmap, but honestly, I can't make sense of those terminologies. 

The only thing I understand is UI/UX and web design and when it comes to customisation, then SEO ranking of the website and stuff like that. 

Sometimes in crypto, the hardest part is not the buying and selling but dealing with uncertainty in between. 

While I'm still here and still reading, still learning and still trying to make sense of it all, one small decision at a time.

title.title: In the Savinja river valley in Slovenia
title.body:
And the last but not the last post about my fall stay in Lasko, Slovenia, is finally here. Although I have written about this place before, every visit there is a new and unique experience and the photos are always very inspiring.

![IMG_20251108_121109.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqL9gt87j9wzXorHaSRBX8vK4mMzD52o1KPbmx1wJPsfxHMsCqT5qGpuMZaVUz8xgZH.jpg)

My last trip there was in November for my son's birthday. Our daily walk through the Savinja River valley was wrapped in deep autumn colors, leaves and the soft sound of water moving beside us.

![IMG_20251108_115409.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqWnFcs2uYvNvtTVE9miSrbfByxXgy9FW2Q1EQzT2azYZJWMt8y11rEvnRuv79dk6su.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_113636.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep3dPzP8B3YfjtYBaixaNJmvwoS4hnpRPkGW3nYA9PtvJAryDCWaxFFr8BStBr72z21.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_121103.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpvjNDsaVbkdAPnQXmRXKBBjVtr1fHztSpxXdMbsikmqAutFxKKeAJ2qWnXFkiWjs3i.jpg)

It was one of those slow moments where you don't check your phone, just breathe and look around.

![IMG_20251108_132933.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep7u9xgU2qEqVpEU4nP8v7KBNDGShQ6n8ccyJBcxGrt8KWNM9TQhvfwkaoUZJd2y6gW.jpg)

We stopped at a small restaurant where, unexpectedly, art meets comfort.

![IMG_20251108_123557.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eou9eUTyYo43VN8GLFQeJL26Zf2aBbPvLdRooGc7imejPBwzjp2mJYrb5FmiA5ZoUKP.jpg)

An exhibition of local bird pictures was impressive. This is the place of the most diverse birds.

![IMG_20251108_123527.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoErU5GvQjb8zuUaeiyYQPG9BYpXa7tmmSUveJoHtd2cp6UJ17vQx4GUrPG7Udjjt3h.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123549.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpCAvv9iaRW9vtEzTLsV3m1p2EesaoWGbiHGgKdkZPvz9p2seB2TUhfgepkLNC2y7T5.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123533.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eos1kKDRdiqYSLV2iUqv1ME5GXMnuS9137UbjHVcPkb6dYojii6mZ5m8ybfm7KSAR2H.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123510.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep5o6yAnabnbyz9eG6AE3QFyGsu9EedrEnMdEC2XdfoeMzqgkjPFSdU9kuuwoui859n.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123541.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoeFovDcxbt6m6pZsZzENV2yYw6iKBJHqvi7M4c5uarz9pNvgg3A1F1Ksh1FvBEfGX9.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123522.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGypRbtcBkjZrp96VwYdao7bE4mMYwEqHPrCDep9UB2QvLE9HV5qeoSjPcxCtC4CRW.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123552.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eou9DyP821afv7pNPceTSyVhYPhZ6BZEGSc8g3ZmMupyGqg5emssdH5m3NpmoFbsqB1.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123606.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EogPLCtxc89BjPS7NdKkX5zBUe1gvFqmKmQzjvuh2NWzxpFDSD9bFv5wLLJRfLVqB6G.jpg)

It made the place feel more personal, almost like being invited into someone's story, with Lasko beer that always pleases, whatever the season. 

![IMG_20251108_122617.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/23xKvnKP1wi2md75MPDvsKzLgihFRgA5NTtQcY1BYiFm7jhjKuXcHyifTmDaPkX748jnP.jpg)

And the burgers were just as always simple, rich, and exactly what you want after a long walk.

![IMG_20251108_123650.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EonnPa23wwSneWarG2dENHPENs99UihispH2X2a6hSi8uR1pq4rt4D3v5bTGGmzSErG.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_123643.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EogPmfWJRL8mK3A1Ru2aLkB6ee8tN1w4HHvD31tsY2N1Np7GFdgVwB9FWv6rsmSJ3my.jpg)

We were again accommodated in the Termana Park hotel, and the view from the hotel room of the Savinja River amazed me again and again every morning.

![IMG_20251108_133341.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqNG4n1mn3nguFVB5ye8kHcgSSx29u4ReuexNMdprB6NJE6wuprZ3B9ZD2CdEEhBYCQ.jpg)

Morning light reflected on the water, making everything feel calm as the fog moved up.

![IMG_20251109_100716.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJY7CSPkgnkjZfVpnoG9qse3vyg2B95sAUi878Hoq9GjM1dxaTeqLv9JvcnRkySUya.jpg)

![IMG_20251109_100720.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpEGJQDhRe2FtEKiqaDR3UrTanrRN4DH2i8MZJjVGZ4M28kPrQw6hdnWurmtATsczez.jpg)

![IMG_20251109_100724.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpNnpnmPFXi5HJy7JLJ3s2GyVQZMFfxdLMe9pP5YzQfjBeUFrdja4kid2WskRkHm3WP.jpg)

And bathing in the thermal waters of this place was, as always, the best experience, at least for me. 😊 

![IMG_20251108_170120.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoJyZKhm6Cj7TFASrCBjkMRrqXz8xuJ59U6wf2KNUaXKwWf2XJAabcDBvTT42Kwky2q.jpg)

![IMG_20251108_180753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoK3xLmkEYV4yiEb83aCVwVZf3vMbu5Cx1bGJEpFEirV9xAJadE5WhRTPaev2ZCH2vU.jpg)

![IMG_20251109_180613.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eoc556VtZCQjdn4ofCbZHQHx5i4JSqaUh1muLKFHXyFW5oMoMBQGx8rf7Fbgk4FJXiy.jpg)

Moving between the indoor and outdoor thermal pools, surrounded by cool November air, was the highlight.

title.title: Planting Roses and Chrysanthemums.
title.body:
Planting Roses and Chrysanthemums. 
Today we planted flowers in the flower bed in our backyard. 
To plant them, you’ll need: water, fertilizer, a shovel, and, of course, the flowers themselves. 
Dig a hole, add fertilizer (I used nitroammophoska), and water it so the fertilizer dissolves a bit and doesn’t lift the plant. Take the flower out of the pot along with the soil so as not to damage the roots. Place it in the hole and fill it in with soil around the edges. Then water it again, being careful not to get water on the blooming flowers. 
Such beautiful flowers are now growing in my garden. 
I love planting flowers at home. I like it when there are lots of flowers in the yard. Their beauty lifts my spirits. I want to sit and watch nature, watch the beautiful flowers.
Every time I see flowers for sale, I find it hard to walk past; I stop and buy some flowers to plant at home. I have flowers in the garden, in the flowerbed, and inside the house.

title.title: Divine Protection: The Blessings We Don’t Always See
title.body: Gratitude is an essential attitude we must all possess, especially as a believer and a faith-oriented individual. There are several things happening in our lives that we tend to take for granted or underappreciate because we feel like they're normal or they're bound to be so; for that reason, we don't see the privilege we're benefiting from or how much safer our maker is making things on average for us. I'm no exception in this regard, and something happened on Easter Sunday that opened my eyes to my shortcomings when it comes to showing gratitude and the need to do better going forward. ![1000360434.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vickoly/23z7Hq7W7et3XEMGotd9hc2F6PJtxQBhhhmusLtQmwADfRxejL14nZmG9nVB8yWWn57em.jpg) So it happened that on Easter Sunday I traveled down to Ogun State from Lagos to pay a visit to a relative, with the intention of checking up on them and as well celebrating Easter together. At the end of the day, while going back home, I boarded a vehicle, and during the course of our journey back to Lagos, I noticed the phone screen of the person sitting beside me was completely shattered, and yet his phone kept ringing, and I watched him struggle to pick up the call. Even though he couldn't see anything on the screen, amongst the calls he was lucky to pick up was how I found out how his phone ended up in that state. It turns out that he was coming from Oyo to Lagos, but the bus he boarded in Ibadan was involved in an accident, and fortunately for him and unfortunately for the rest of the other 17 passengers, he and the driver were the only ones who came out of that bus alive; others sustained life-threatening injuries, while the majority, alongside the person sitting beside him in the front seat, died instantly. Immediately I heard his story, I was gripped by fear and touched by how God saved his life almost from that accident. And it reminded me of how God once saved me from an almost similar situation years ago, and yet I didn't even deem it fit to give testimony in the church for the unique way by which I was saved from that incident. So years ago, around 2021 or so, I was traveling from the same Ibadan but heading towards Ilorin, and when I got to the motorway park, there was just one space left, which made me excited, but unfortunately and at the same time fortunately for me, the person I was supposed to sit beside where the available seat was body-shamed me by saying I couldn't sit there because I was too fat and would inconvenience her throughout the journey. I remember how God helped me to hold my peace without getting angry or arguing with her, but Peaceful went to sit in the next available bus and wait till it got full. I can vividly remember that when the second bus I later went to sit on got full and we moved, I had totally forgotten about how someone body-shamed me until we were about an hour away from getting to our destination and we saw a bus that had been involved in an accident, with many people seriously injured inside the bus. It was after our driver parked at the church and sorted the situation out that I realized it was the same bus I would have boarded had someone not body-shamed me. Looking back at that event, I'm really grateful to God for his protection, guidance, and sustenance over my life, because I can't really do anything on my own; he's my anchor. Showing gratitude isn't just good because when we show gratitude, it'll help us get more from the person who gave it to us in the first place; it's also good because other people can, via our experience and story, learn and take action that would help them partake of such. Most importantly, we should show gratitude because it's the right thing to do. *** All photos are mine. ***

title.title: [Literature] Johann Gottlieb Fichte:  Sun-Clear Statement #16/41
title.body:
A consciousness, which generates itself, and which yet is not the actual consciousness of which we all have possession?

A. Of course: for actual consciousness does not systematically generate itself, its manifold being connected by mere chance. That consciousness which generates itself under the observation of the philosopher is merely an image of actual consciousness.

R. An image which generates itself? I utterly cease to understand you, and I am sure I shall not understand you until you have given me a short sketch of your procedure.

A. Very well. The presupposition, from which we start, is this: that the final and highest result of consciousness, or that to which all its manifold is related as the condition to the conditioned, or as the wheels, springs, and chains in the watch are related to the hand, is nothing else than clear and complete self-consciousness, as you and I and all of us are conscious of ourselves. I say, you and I and all of us, and thereby exclude, in conformity with a previous remark, all that is purely individual, which cannot enter our system at all according to our presupposition. That, which you ascribe to your self alone, and not to me, or I only to me and not to you, remains excluded; except that you do so ascribe something exclusively to your self and I to my self and each one to his Self.

Now, this result—that complete self-consciousness is the highest and final result of all consciousness—is, as we have said, a mere presupposition, which awaits its confirmation from the system. From this self-consciousness, in its fundamental determination, the deduction begins.

R. In its fundamental determination? What does that mean?

A. In regard to that, which in it is not at all determined by any other consciousness, and which can, therefore, not be found in the deduction, but from which, on the contrary, the deduction must proceed. The presupposition is, that the manifold of consciousness contains the conditions of complete self-consciousness. Nevertheless, there may be somewhat in this self-consciousness which is not conditioned by anything else. This somewhat is to be established, and from it the deduction proceeds.

R. But how do you find it?

A. Likewise, only by a happy hit, but as somewhat, which when once found, needs and requires no further proof, but is immediately self-evident.

R. Abstaining for the present from all inquiry as to this immediate self-evidence itself, tell me, what is it in this somewhat which is thus immediately self-evident?

A. That it is the absolutely unconditioned and the characteristic of self-consciousness.

R. I shall not be able to understand you, until you tell me what this unconditioned and characteristic of self-consciousness is, which is thus self-evident.

A. It is the Ego-hood, the subject-objectivity, and nothing else whatsoever, the positing of the subjective and of its objective, of consciousness and of the object of consciousness as one and the same, and as absolutely nothing but this its identity.

R. I know from various sources, that people generally consider you very incomprehensible, and, moreover, very ridiculous in your views on this first point, which you must, nevertheless, hold to be altogether clear and comprehensible, since all your reasoning starts from it. Be good enough, therefore, to furnish me some means by which I can make it clearer to those others, in case they should ask me about it; unless, indeed, such an explanation belongs rather to the Science of Knowledge proper, and not to a mere statement of its nature.

A. It certainly belongs to this statement, for it is the previously mentioned common point of the Science of Knowledge and of actual consciousness, from which the former rises above the latter. Whosoever is to receive a perfectly clear conception of this science must know the point from which it starts, and this conception is the very thing which our statement proposes to create.

But what people say about not having understood us on that point belongs to the absolutely incomprehensible; for every child, that has but ceased to speak of itself in the third person and calls itself \

has already realized that point, and can, therefore, understand us.

I shall have to repeat what I have said already several times. Think something: for instance, the book you hold in your hand. You can doubtless become conscious of the book as the object of your thought, and of yourself as the thinking. Do you appear to yourself as being one and the same with the book, or as another?

R. Doubtless, as another, I shall never mistake myself for the book.

A.

title.title: Among Guitars I’ll Probably Never Own - My Actifit Report Card: April 19 2026
title.body:
Today I dropped by a guitar exhibition, because a friend of mine was running a booth there. He deals in genuinely legendary guitars, the kind that come with eye-watering price tags. I once saw he sold a guitar previously owned by John Frusciante of RHCP. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/3c090c19-9da1-4cae-9461-b64e2172b4f3.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/7d983f6c-e8c1-48a3-b249-c6e8edf1326a.jpg) As expected, the crowd leaned heavily toward industry insiders, people who clearly know what they’re doing when it comes to high-quality instruments. I, on the other hand, am very obviously not their target market; there’s no scenario in which I’d realistically afford most of what’s on display. That said, I did notice a seller who’s fairly popular on Instagram, somewhere around 53,000 followers. His inventory is comparatively more accessible, and, in a moment of optimism, I could almost imagine myself buying something from his shop. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/82baf12a-b546-4bf2-836d-1af1fb465790.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/cde376c0-951a-444f-91a0-8931e1e59400.jpg) Anyway, one piece that really caught my attention was a 1969 Fender Stratocaster, reminiscent of what Jimi Hendrix used. Right next to it sat an Ibanez in a striking neon green finish, hard to miss, even in a room full of eye candy. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/8b0d3178-c6f3-4545-93d1-ed8979e87a67.jpg) ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/5a50b700-7142-4b08-af15-3741d5ac0a04.jpg) All in all, it’s the kind of exhibition that quietly tempts you into wanting things you absolutely don’t need. Heh. I didn't come home empty handed though. My friend gave me two packs of Gibson accoustic strings. Not bad at all. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/0ac86329-fce1-4518-a181-dc0bed3dc82c.jpg)

title.title: Tunnel vision : The only way out is through. [WE-305]
title.body:
Tunnel rides are enjoyable. Since my childhood days, I always fascinated to travel through a tunnel. A tunnel ride acts as a break in the routine, offering a thrilling and immersive sensory experience. Though we never had the oppurtunity to take a tunnel ride, except when we travel to our village from town. I remember passing through 3 different small tunnel while travelling in a train. Whether it is a motorcycle, train, or bicycle tunnel, the experience is often memorable because of the dramatic shift from open surroundings to a confined space. And when I get the chance to travel through the longest road tunnel I was thrilled for the all new adventure. I had many memorable road travels, but this one going to be a new experience for sure a childhood dreams to come True.


![20260405_090049.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/23zasxzx1zBCbf6kNKKYfNWTCjzj88wDYekmfPL7xu5RS3ffKb5492XL93j7BE9x9swsR.jpg)

Jammu is situated in northern part of India and is covered with many mountains. The area has well developed roads that includes few tunnel that crosses from inside the mountains. Riding through a tunnel, particularly a long one, can trigger a sense of adventure, excitement, or even a slight, thrilling fear especially in dark or rustic old tunnels. Recently, while I was away for a trip in Jammu, I had the chance to cross the **The Chenani - Nashri Tunnel** also known as Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel. The tunnel is built between two villages in hills. On one side is Chennani, while the side of the hill is call Nashri. It is one of the engineering marvel that reduces travel time between Jammu and Srinagar by roughly two hours, providing a smooth, **9 km**, all weather driving experience through the Himalayas. 


![20260405_102319.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/23t7BBscRmcDZRQNonqbeg84ptdRFQ7vWHKeVywRKYj3zjaE8AouMVDijAeDRvCokAsht.jpg)


As soon as we enter the tunnel, it gets too dark. We were expecting it to finish in short time, but soon we knew it going to be a long ride. As India's longest highway tunnel (nearly 9 km), passing through it is a proud experience for travelers and surely an enjoyable time for me. The tunnel is fully integrated with a transverse ventilation system for fresh air, 124 cameras, linear heat detection, and SOS boxes every 150 meters, providing a secure, high tech driving experience. It bypasses landslide prone areas, offers excellent lighting, and includes advanced safety features. The interior is well lit and well maintained, with a dedicated parallel escape tunnel for emergencies. We thought to stop.in middle but it could.risky due to heavy traffic. Passing through it is a dream come True. The sound and echo reminded me of my childhood fantasies.


![20260405_090049(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/23u5y2DggRxYpXXgZAYAGB1MLPT2FbK6MwqkM51X4XpAmbqURJzB3ceKNCJbWDHehyKZB.jpg)

The tunnel significantly reduces the journey time by about 2 hours and reduces the distance by 30 km, making the journey less stressful and faster. It went on nicely and ultimately ended up as one of the best road trip i ever had. This is my entry to this week [Weekend engagement](https://peakd.com/hive-168869/@galenkp/weekend-engagement-topics-week-305) topic 1.







**In good faith - Peace!!**



![1000037470.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/Eo8M1obna2cYnnMAc2ZC3wWMW9ZqZHvk9StEga6aY2cTsKmweW7zFBDm7D13YHVoC5N.png)

title.title: Is It Normal?
title.body:
haiku, the universe kept on presenting me with more of them. Often I am in the garden when they come to me. Was it a toad that told me? 


![text15.png](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmWXynVma7pYo3MCivJ5Cb6Nfae2uMGNt11YGxqysBGqBW/text15.png)

*is it normal
to think 
that toads can speak?*


*is it normal
to **not** want to be 
a trailblazer?*

*is it normal
to fret
after the choice is made?*


*is it normal
to rush rush rush
every step of the way?*



*is it normal
to step on **none** of the toes
in any room?*

*is it normal
to feel naked
without your phone?*

*is it normal
to consider the absurd
to be normal?*



*is it normal
to stand quietly
and breathe?*

Dani cruzó los brazos y les lanzó una mirada con brillo en los ojos. —Hablando de grande ¿alguna vez pensaron en competir en el concurso de bandas de la escuela? Este año tenemos que hacerlo. Además, tenemos a Lucas y creo que podemos llegar lejos. Lucas se levantó un poco, nervioso agarrando su tambor muy fuerte. —Si trabajamos como ahora, yo, creo que podemos ganar todo, además daré lo mejor, solo tenemos que ensayar duro y coordinar nuestras ideas. Stewie —Exacto, cada golpe, cada nota, cada silencio todo cuenta, para así poder estar listo. Esta vez no sólo será tocar; será demostrar lo que somos capaces de hacer juntos. >The band kept playing with their new member, and when the final beat came, silence fell over the studio for a second; everyone looked at each other with smiles. Lucas, still breathing heavily, rested his drumsticks on the drum and sighed with relief. “That was incredible,” he said. “I’ve never felt anything like that playing with someone else.” # >Stewie dropped his drumsticks onto the keyboard. “That’s just the beginning, and you’ll see—you’ll get the hang of it.” Dani crossed her arms and gave them a look with a sparkle in her eyes. “Speaking of big things, have you ever thought about competing in the school band contest? I’ll give it my all—we just have to practice hard and coordinate our ideas.” Stewie: “Exactly. Every beat, every note, every silence—it all counts, so we can be ready. This time it won’t just be about playing; it’ll be about showing what we’re capable of doing together.” ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPNcXyRm5NprXnHCiAPV1TJbbT4qiu5GCkYgHRVHdbWqZ/image.png) [Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/tambor-maracatu-instrumento-musical-1038063/) Dani dio un paso adelante—Entonces, ¡está decidido! Pero cuidado, chicos, si creen que esto será fácil, están muy equivocados, ya que habrá más horas, nuevas canciones. Lucas comentó. —Perfecto. Me gusta la idea de desafiarme a mí mismo y apoyar la Banda. Stewie levantó sus baquetas. ¡Que empiece la práctica! Y con eso, el primer golpe del nuevo desafío fue muy fuerte, mezclando la energía de cuatro corazones dispuestos a transformar su música en algo que nadie podría ignorar. El concurso ya no era un sueño lejano; estaba justo ahí, esperando por ellos. >Dani stepped forward. “So, it’s settled! We’re going to practice for the competition. If we want to win, we need intensity, creativity, and coordination.” Michelle smiled and began playing the keyboard, as if she were already rehearsing. “Then let the practice begin,” she said. “But watch out, guys—if you think this is going to be easy, you’re sorely mistaken, because there will be longer hours and new songs.” Lucas commented. “Perfect. I like the idea of challenging myself and supporting the band.” # >Stewie raised his drumsticks. Let the practice begin! And with that, the first beat of the new challenge rang out loud and clear, blending the energy of four hearts ready to transform their music into something no one could ignore. The competition was no longer a distant dream; it was right there, waiting for them. ![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP6wQEWJcRUmhXa88q2nuM9fg28BqbAkrjwamX7wV7MTU/image.png) [Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/bajista-guitarrista-guitarra-m%c3%basica-5505695/)

title.title: v4call.com
title.body:
v4call.com went from zero to 0.1 on 420 eve 19/04/2026. using the Hive blockchain as a phonebook. V4Call stands for Value for Call. Getting your own node running for testing https://www.completenoobs.com/noobs/V4CALL federation - maybe coming soon, still working that out.

## Why v4call Exists

I don't want strangers ringing my phone. I don't want cold callers, spam, or someone asking if I'm happy with my telephone provider. If someone I don't know wants to talk to me, they should pay for the privilege. If they value my time, they'll pay. If not, my phone doesn't ring. Simple.

I want a **ring fee** — a payment just to make my phone ring. I want a **connect fee** — a payment when I pick up. And I want a **per-hour rate** — so every minute of my time is compensated. If they hang up early, the unused credit goes back to them automatically.

But I don't want to charge everyone the same. I want **custom rules for different people:**

- **Family** — no restrictions, no fees, call any time
- **Friends** — free calls during the day (8am–11pm), but if they ring me after 11pm there's a small fee to make my phone ring — because it better be important
- **Work** — free during office hours (9am–5pm), after that I set my own rate for out-of-hours calls
- **Everyone else** — cold callers, randoms, unknowns — they pay my default rate. One price during the day, a higher price at night

I also want the same system for **text messages**. Spam texts cost the sender nothing and waste my time. If a stranger wants to message me, they can pay a small fee. If it's someone I know, it's free.

I don't want a public phone. I want a **private, personal phone** where the people I know can reach me freely, and everyone else pays to connect.

That's why v4call was built. The main idea behind v4call:

Good morning **Hivers**. This Sunday morning I would like to share with you more of my **photos** and I hope you like them 🤗. Trees have always been an example of **resilience**, constant **strength** and **growth**. There is a therapy called *Tree-therapy* where you hug trees to relieve stress and it really works. There are also interesting theories about the origin and future of trees, those that straighten up no matter the adversities around them. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUoP2wwHaWgSEhHz9WhVjrKXKXLqN3gEspdeKqFae23f9/1776592589779.jpg) What better than to accompany a **Sunday** with a sweet liqueur of **Eggnog**. You really don't have to wait for Christmas to be able to **enjoy** it with **family** and friends 😁. For my tastes, I like it loaded with alcohol jjjj it is the best recommended therapy when you have a stressful day jjj. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXb4wci1fLwndnnuBrg4NVW5j4iwSGjCaS7yAVRd6Co15/1776592650223.jpg) Walking for a while through the **forest** I find this curious bird **feather**. J does the grocery shopping so I don't really know how much everything costs these days, I do remember sitting down with him one time when he was redoing the house budget (which comprises of the bills and rates and groceries) and he was looking very confused, it was a while back when we first realised how annoyingly pricey things were getting as he was saying how the grocery bill had gone up substantially but he hadn't bought anything terribly different from what he usually gets.

My favourite fruits are mangos and I am a spoilt brat who grew up eating them pretty much straight from the tree so the shop ones rarely taste quite right (but they are mostly good most of the time and that's better than no mangos).  Fortunately we have a mango tree and friends who have multiple mango trees so we don't have to buy too many mangos.

Haven't really noticed a decline in quality in other fruits and vegetables but I probably don't have very high standards for a lot of things.
