body.title: [Literature] Johann Gottlieb Fichte:  Facts of Consciousness #16/65
body.body:
Now we are here thinking the Ego not as merely a knowing power or intelligence, but as a practical power or principle, and hence we proceed further thus: what does it mean when we say, that the manifold utterances or manifestations of the principle are conditioned through each other, those manifestations—as the mere outflow of the freedom of the principle—having in themselves no independent existence whatever which might enable them to have peculiar determinations as the things of external perception have, and thus whatever we assert of them is in truth asserted of the principle from which they flow? It clearly means this: the principle is conditioned in regard to its utterances, its self-development is confined to a determined sequence of series of those manifestations or utterances, a sequence that here continues infinitely. It can arrive at a certain end, y—however clear it may think it and propose it to itself as its end—in actuality only by proceeding in a certain sequence through a, b, c, d, &c.

But whence arises this knowledge of the conditionedness of the Ego? Evidently, since it expresses a limitation of the principle in relation to its power in actuality, from the self-contemplation of its power. And thus the above promised definite description of the conception of conditionedness has become possible. That conception is founded upon the immediate self-contemplation of the faculty of the principle in its state of confinedness to an a prioridetermined sequence of moments in its development in actuality.

This conception will, therefore, make it possible with apodictical certainty to draw a conclusion from a given part of time as to what must have preceded that time—although that preceding has not been experienced in actual life—and thus to restore the past with sure accuracy by means of grounds. Thus it will also be possible in the same manner to draw conclusions from the same given time as to what will follow, and thus to make present the future; of course, under the presupposition that everything will happen properly,—that is, that the principle will use its entire faculty, and limit itself by nothing except the absolute law of its self-development.

I ask you now: is this thus perceived series of moments perfectly ordered, each link having in it its determined position, from which it cannot move, and therefore its firmly determined moment in known time? Doubtless you must answer: Yes. I ask again: at which time in universal time does this whole known time occur? has it also its determined position in that universal time? Doubtless you will have to answer, No; that known time floats in an altogether undetermined position in the infinite time, which is empty at both of its ends.

>C.


Appendix concerning the power of Recollection.—We desire to speak of this power in general, and more specially at this place, as it excellently illustrates what we have said about time. \n

The power of recollection is, first of all, essentially different from the above described power to generate the contents of time absolutely a priorieither of the past or of the future. For whereas the latter power asserts merely, that a certain content of time was necessary in the past, or will be necessary in the future, regardless as to whether such content has been actually experienced in life, and indeed without any reference to actuality whatever, the power of recollection asserts that a certain state or condition in the past has actually been, and been experienced. \n

Now, upon what is this power of recollection grounded? I answer: just like that former power, upon a relation of conditionedness; but with this difference, that whereas that former power is conditioned by a relation simply of the absolute possibility of the occurrence, the present power is conditioned by the given actuality of the occurrence. In the present given moment I do something within my consciousness; and I observe that I do this by means of a new rejection which rises above the actual doing. Then I ask, under what subjective condition of the occurred development of my faculty could I do so? I find, under this or that condition. Hence this condition must have already been filled by me with some actual deed, whilst it is at the same time represented to be as actual by the immediate causality of imagination. Perhaps this condition is again conditioned in the same factical manner by a necessary previous condition, which is represented to me in the same manner as actual, &c. Thus I am enabled to develop from the one given moment of my life conditions of my past life as having actually occurred; that is, to recollect them.

Examples range from Charlotte cocktail bar Antagonist locking phones away for roughly two hours, to Delilah enforcing a no-phones, no-posting policy, to a Chick-fil-A location offering free ice cream to families who keep phones off the table. Different vibe, same goal: get people present.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 The business case is pretty straightforward. Hospitality experts argue that when guests are engaged with the meal and the people in front of them, they’re more likely to order another course or a second drink. They’re also less likely to let the food go cold while staging photos or scrolling reviews before deciding what they “should” think. Brutal, but fair.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The social and psychological argument is even stronger. One etiquette expert frames a visible phone as a status signal that the person with you matters less than whatever might buzz on-screen. A psychiatrist quoted in the piece ties the trend to cognitive overload: constant connectivity wears people down, and phone-free dining gives people a rare pocket of mental relief and actual human attention.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 The article doesn’t pretend this becomes universal. Enforcement is awkward — pouches, signs, or staff reminders can create exactly the kind of friction restaurants are trying to avoid. So the likely outcome isn’t every diner going screen-free; it’s a growing niche in higher-end or curated venues where atmosphere is part of the product. 📎 Source

📎 [Source](https://nypost.com/2026/04/19/lifestyle/restaurants-ban-phones-at-tables-for-screen-free-dining/)

body.body: 1/5 🧵 A New Jersey middle school turned a civics lesson into a mock protest exercise, and that’s why this blew up. The official line: students were “pretending to protest homework” to learn about the First Amendment. The criticism: school crossed the line from teaching civic concepts to rehearsing political behavior. That distinction is the whole fight.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The school at the center is Clinton Township Middle School in Hunterdon County, NJ. Video shared publicly showed students outside holding signs while administrators and a social studies teacher watched. Superintendent Melissa Stager said it was a non-political, age-appropriate lesson on civic concepts. Problem is, once kids are making posters and staging a rally, it stops looking like abstract civics and starts looking like training wheels for activism.

Jennifer Webber of the Manhattan Institute made the sharper point: teaching *about* civic processes is one thing; shaping how students participate is another. That’s the real tension here—education vs ideological conditioning.

# RAVE Crashes 95%: $6.3B Gone — What the Chart Told Us Before It Happened

*April 2026*

---

**$6.3 billion. Gone in a single day.**

RAVE cryptocurrency just collapsed 95%, and the word flying around Reddit and CT right now is *insider manipulation*. Let's break down what happened and what the signals were before the crash.

## The Numbers

- Market cap peak: ~$6.6B
- Market cap now: ~$330M
- Drop: **95% in under 24 hours**

## Alleged Insider Manipulation

On-chain analysis from multiple wallets shows:
- Large wallets **accumulated** RAVE quietly over 2 weeks
- Social media buzz was coordinated — Telegram groups, influencer posts
- After retail piled in, **whale wallets dumped simultaneously**

Textbook pump-and-dump. The difference here is the scale — $6.3B is not a micro-cap rug.

## Red Flags RAVE Was Showing

I always check these before entering any token:

- Token concentration: top 10 wallets held >40% of supply ❌
- Large team unlock coming within 30 days ❌
- Sudden 10x spike in social mentions with no product news ❌
- Tokens moving to exchanges (sell signal) ❌

If you see 3+ of these at once — it's a pass.

## The Broader Picture

2026 has been brutal for retail. KelpDAO losing $292M to hackers + RAVE wiping $6.3B through apparent manipulation in the same week.

The only durable value in crypto right now: ETH staking yield, real DeFi fee revenue, BTC as collateral, and on-chain content creation.

Stay safe. These operations are designed by professionals — losing money on this doesn't make you stupid.

Hoy la ruta cambió el asfalto de la ciudad por la brisa marina de **La Guaira**, y no pudo ser mejor. Participar en el entrenamiento de **La Perla Run Club** fue una experiencia renovadora; hay algo en el aire del Caribe que inyecta una energía distinta a las piernas. Fueron **5 kilómetros** donde el ritmo lo marcó el sonido de las olas y la satisfacción de seguir sumando después de tantos retos superados este año.
Lo más especial de esta jornada no fue el cronómetro, sino la compañía. Correr rodeada de mi **familia** transformó el entrenamiento en un momento de conexión pura. Ver a los tuyos compartir el esfuerzo, las risas bajo el sol y la meta frente al mar es el mejor recordatorio de por qué amamos este estilo de vida. No se trata solo de acumular distancia, sino de construir memorias con quienes más queremos mientras cuidamos la salud.
Cerramos la mañana con el corazón contento y la satisfacción del deber cumplido. Gracias a La Perla Run Club por recibirnos con tanto entusiasmo en su casa. ¡Nos llevamos el brillo del sol, el salitre en la piel y las ganas inmensas de seguir devorando kilómetros! Cada paso cuenta, pero cuando se da en familia, ¡se disfruta el doble! 🌴👟🔥

Official entry for the #monomad challenge hosted by @monochromes and @brumest

>Hello, friends of #blackandwhite, I hope you’re all having a wonderful Sunday. Today I’ll be sharing some photos from my trip to the countryside; I thought I’d already posted all the photos from that day, but while going through my files I found some others that I really liked, and of course I wanted to show them to you.\n\n

> Hola, amigos de #blackandwhite, excelente domingo tengan todos. Hoy les estaré compartiendo algunas de las imágenes de mi visita al campo; pensaba que había publicado todas las imágenes de aquel día, pero revisando los archivos encontré otras que me gustaron mucho y, por supuesto, quería mostrárselas. ![_DSC2412_copy_3170x2264.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/muhammadhalim/23tGdwVYZPSm16kLsTpWeWxffw9rvGwPjDi4cfKh2ULpfpW8MQFZgB4jNwUvKFCu5DmkR.jpg)

body.body:

</center>
</liketuimages>

Ayer en casa volvimos a vestir el día de celebración. Hace apenas una semana estábamos cantándole cumpleaños a mi abuela, y como si el tiempo quisiera regalarnos una doble alegría, ahora le tocó a mi abuelo materno soplar sus 75 velitas.


Y digo “regalo” con toda intención, porque no todo el mundo tiene la suerte de seguir celebrando la vida junto a quienes ama. Poder sentarnos a su lado, verlo sonreír, escucharlo… eso no se compra, no se repite, y se agradece con el alma.


Como ya es costumbre en mí, no podía faltar el detalle hecho en casa. Esta vez el cake nació de una madrugada silenciosa, aprovechando ese momento en que había corriente y todo parecía conspirar a favor. Decidí salir un poco de lo tradicional y mezclé leche condensada con maní triturado para el relleno, y por encima le puse leche condensada hervida con cobertura de chocolate. El resultado… un éxito total. De esos dulces que no duran nada porque todos repiten.


También quise sumar un poco más de vida a la casa, así que invité a mi amiga Yessica y a su pequeña, que con su energía llenaron cada rincón de risas. Brindamos con cerveza, compartimos una crema de vie que preparé, y entre conversaciones, anécdotas y cariño, la tarde fue tomando ese sabor especial que solo tienen los momentos sinceros.


Esta vez sí hubo fotos… muchas. De la mesa, del cake, de los brindis, de las risas compartidas. Fotos que sí voy a guardar y también a compartir, porque cuentan la historia de un día bonito. Pero justo faltan las más importantes para muchos: las de mi abuelo. No hubo manera de convencerlo. No le gustan las cámaras, ni las redes, ni posar.

Y está bien.

Porque al final entendí que no todo necesita ser mostrado para ser valioso. Hay presencias que no caben en una imagen, hay personas que prefieren quedarse fuera del lente pero muy dentro del corazón.






# English Version 




Yesterday, our home once again dressed itself in celebration. Just a week ago we were singing happy birthday to my grandmother, and as if time wanted to gift us double the joy, this time it was my maternal grandfather blowing out his 75 candles.


And I say “gift” very intentionally, because not everyone has the blessing of continuing to celebrate life alongside the people they love. Being able to sit next to him, see him smile, listen to him… that’s something you can’t buy, can’t repeat, and can only be deeply grateful for.


As usual for me, I couldn’t let the day pass without a homemade detail. This cake was born in the quiet of the early morning, taking advantage of a moment when the electricity was on and everything seemed to align. I decided to step a bit outside the traditional and mixed condensed milk with crushed peanuts for the filling, and topped it with boiled condensed milk and a chocolate coating. The result… a total success. The kind of dessert that disappears quickly because everyone wants seconds.


I also wanted to bring a little more life into the house, so I invited my friend Yessica and her little girl, who filled every corner with laughter. We made a toast with beer, shared a homemade crema de vie, and between conversations, stories, and affection, the afternoon slowly turned into one of those moments that feel simple, yet truly meaningful.


This time, there were photos… plenty of them. Of the table, the cake, the toasts, the shared laughter. Photos I’ll keep and also share, because they tell the story of a beautiful day. But the ones many would consider the most important are missing: the photos of my grandfather. There was no way to convince him. He doesn’t like cameras, social media, or posing.
And that’s okay.


Because in the end, I realized that not everything needs to be shown to be valuable. There are presences that don’t fit into a picture, people who prefer to stay out of the frame but deeply within our hearts.

body.title: I Dare You To Be Patient with Yourself
body.body:
It is often hard to be courageous enough to be patient with oneself especially when times are hard. It is more like looking at the mirror and telling the person you can see that you are doing fine and you deserve to be patient. We can be lenient when people make mistakes, by giving them a second chance, so why don't you do the same for yourself. ![53FD496D-E33D-477C-BB12-7BC6688AE0A4.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/samostically/23xATjQE39fRUyHbVpZ95JBXDtHuGXxwuZunh7ZLFX67fL7bMJkNgcz5wsFDKAnSWj7u6.png) It gets consuming when we rate ourselves with high expectations but fail to give ourselves a second chance for when things do not go well. Why can you be patient with others when they make a mistake, but you are hard on yourself when you make one? Nothing is more disheartening when we beat ourselves up because of the mistakes we made. Being patient with oneself is more of a courageous tool that I feel many do not possess. Have you ever been so hard on yourself? You will come to understand that it is mentally draining especially when you go on and on about how things could have been different or done different. I know what that is like because I have done that a lot especially after a loss during a tournament. Trust me when I say it is brutal. Nobody becomes more tired than you at that time and the worst part is you get sad as you look through what you could have done differently. The effect can be worse especially if it is a game where you were winning or had the chance to win. These things happen and it is all a process in getting better. This is when the part of being patient with oneself is important. I choose to take it more as a daring statement to others who are out there, when I tell them take the courage to be patient with yourself. Try to understand that good things take time to come alive. A huge factor lies in the power of how consistent you can be at putting in the work to achieve what you want. Are you able to challenge yourself to accept the long time that comes with growth. We can only hope it does not take ages but we can't deny that it might require more time from us. A major part of everything I have learned from the tournaments I have had in the past is it takes time to achieve the work and time to become good at playing chess. Sindarov started when he was around 4 or 5 and so did a lot of super grandmasters of today. A lot of time and resources have been devoted into getting to the spot they are in now and what that means is a lot heartbreaks must have been felt. It was so inspiring when I watched Sindarov's interview after his victory against Prag when he spoke about how he has lost a lot of games to Prag during their time, playing World juniors tournaments. It shows that these players have played a lot of times in the past and they have their shared loses. Success wasn't born overnight, rather it is a product of a long time of hard work. Nobody can be harder on you like yourself which is why I chose to dare you today to be patient with yourself. Growth takes time and consistency.

body.body: 2/5 🧵 Roberts-Smith, 47, was charged with **five war-crimes counts** tied to Afghanistan deployments between **2009 and 2012**. body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 His public response was direct: he **categorically denied** the allegations, said he always acted within the **rules of engagement**, and said he’s “proud” of his Afghanistan service. He also framed the criminal case as his chance to finally clear his name. That’s the line he’s running with — total denial, no hedging.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The prosecution’s version is brutal. Police allege the victims were **not taking part in hostilities**, were **detained**, **unarmed**, and already **under the control of Australian forces** when they were killed. Prosecutors also opposed bail because they feared Roberts-Smith might try to contact witnesses. The judge still granted bail, partly because the case is expected to take **years** to reach trial.

body.body:

Her argument is broader than just Peterson: she says these kinds of injuries are more common than people think and often misdiagnosed. That’s a huge claim, and a controversial one, but it’s central to what she’s saying.

CMA CEO Sarah Trahern and Country Music Hall of Fame CEO Kyle Young both framed him as foundational to Nashville’s identity.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 The obvious headline is **“The Gambler”**, recorded by Kenny Rogers in 1978. That song became bigger than a radio hit — it turned into cultural furniture. But Schlitz’s catalog goes way beyond that. He also wrote or co-wrote **“On the Other Hand,” “Forever and Ever, Amen,”** and **“When You Say Nothing at All,”** songs that helped define artists like Randy Travis and Keith Whitley, and later reached new audiences through Alison Krauss and others.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 What made Schlitz matter wasn’t just volume. It was range and durability. He helped shape the sound and careers of **Kenny Rogers, Randy Travis, The Judds, Tanya Tucker, Mary Chapin Carpenter**, and even later projects like Rogers reuniting with Dolly Parton on **“You Can’t Make Old Friends.”** Kenny Rogers once said Schlitz didn’t just write songs — he **wrote careers**. That’s the real measure of his impact.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 His résumé is absurdly strong: inducted into both the **Songwriters Hall of Fame** and the **Country Music Hall of Fame**, named **ASCAP Country Songwriter of the Year four straight years (1988–1991)**, and recognized by the Opry in a way almost no behind-the-scenes writer ever is. He leaves behind a family, a massive catalog, and a genre that sounds different because he existed. 📎 Source

body.body:
>

Hoy domingo me reporto nuevamente aunque un poco tarde de lo que estoy acostumbrado a publicar bien temprano en la mañana para compartirles un poco de lo que está sonando hoy en mi vida y en mi playlist, si la vez pasada andábamos con la fuerza de Rocky, hoy me puse en un modo más introspectivo, pero con la misma intensidad de siempre, me puse a escuchar a un tipo que es un maestro en esto de mezclar máquinas con sentimientos, por si no lo conoces él es, el gran Moby.


Para los que no lo conocen mucho, Moby que por cierto, se puso así por su antepasado el que escribió Moby Dick, es un neoyorquino que desde los años 80 anda inventando con la música que ahora le dicen música electrónica, él pasó de tocar punk rudo a ser el rey de la electrónica, pero no esa música de discoteca vacía, sino una electrónica que te llega a los huesos.

Hoy quiero hablarles de una pieza que es, para mí, una obra maestra Porcelain, esta canción salió por allá por el año 1999 en su disco Play Moby, me acuerdo de que aquí en Venezuela la empezamos a escuchar en la radio y en la televisión entre el 2000 y el 2001, y ni se diga de quemar los CD copiados, sobre todo después de que salió en aquella película de DiCaprio, La Playa recuerdo esa atmósfera de paz, pero con un toque de tristeza que te deja la canción.

Porcelain habla de lo frágil que es el amor, de cómo las cosas se pueden romper como la porcelana, escuchándola hoy, me puse a pensar en cómo hemos cambiado desde que ese tema sonaba en cada esquina de nuestra Venezuela, me acordé clarito de cuando Moby vino a caracas en el 2005, al Hipódromo de La Rinconada, yo supe que él vendría Venezuela, pero lamentablemente no era el mejor momento sobre todo cuando me entere quienes fuero los que lo trajeron, es lamentable que esta gente y ustedes saben a quienes me refiero saben utilizar el pan y el circo, a mí me encanta ese tema porque, aunque suena relajado, tiene un trasfondo que te pone a pensar en lo que hemos dejado atrás y en lo que todavía nos queda por proteger, y actualmente por la situación país tenemos que seguir protegiendo

Así que, mis panas, y amigos eso incluye sin dudarlo a mi amiga sacra que siempre está pendiente de esta publicación, aquí les dejo este clásico, un poquito de electrónica de la buena para cerrar la semana, bajarle dos a la intensidad del día a día, pero manteniendo la mente clara y el corazón despierto.

Today, Sunday, I’m checking in again, although a bit later than my usual early morning posts, to share a bit of what’s playing today in my life and on my playlist. If last time we were riding with the strength of Rocky, today I’ve moved into a more introspective mood, but with the same intensity as always. I started listening to a guy who is a master at mixing machines with feelings; in case you don’t know him, he is the great Moby.

For those who don’t know much about him, Moby—who, by the way, took that name from his ancestor who wrote Moby Dick—is a New Yorker who has been experimenting since the 80s with what is now called electronic music. He went from playing raw punk to being the king of electronica, but not that empty club music; rather, the kind of electronica that gets under your skin.

Today I want to talk to you about a piece that is, for me, a masterpiece: Porcelain. This song came out around 1999 on his album Play. I remember that here in Venezuela, we started hearing it on the radio and TV between 2000 and 2001, not to mention burning those copied CDs, especially after it appeared in that DiCaprio movie, The Beach. I remember that atmosphere of peace, but with that touch of sadness that the song leaves you with.

Porcelain talks about how fragile love is, how things can break like porcelain. Listening to it today, I began to think about how much we’ve changed since that track was playing on every corner of our Venezuela. I clearly remember when Moby came to Caracas in 2005, to the La Rinconada Hippodrome. I knew he was coming to Venezuela, but unfortunately, it wasn't the best time, especially when I found out who brought him. body.body: 1/5 🧵 Chicago’s tipped wage fight just went fully nuclear: Mayor Brandon Johnson defended ending the subminimum wage by tying the restaurant industry’s roots to slavery and framing the issue as one of reparations. That’s not a routine labor-policy argument. That’s a moral indictment with a flamethrower.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The policy fight itself is straightforward: Chicago is phasing out the tipped subminimum wage so tipped workers reach the full minimum wage by 2028. Restaurant owners hate it, arguing thin margins, higher menu prices, and potential job cuts. Johnson vetoed an effort to stop that phaseout, and City Council then failed to override him because it didn’t hit the 34 votes needed.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 Johnson’s argument is bigger than wages. He said council was trying to “take wages away from Black and Brown people,” pointing to the demographic reality that many tipped service workers are minorities. Then he went further, saying the restaurant industry has “ties to slavery” and linked his stance to a broader reparations agenda. Politically, that’s a deliberate escalation: make this about historical injustice, not just payroll math.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The second front here is transparency and optics. Johnson made the remarks while defending his Reparations Task Force against criticism that it wasn’t operating in line with Illinois open-meeting requirements. He rejected the criticism, emphasized that he’s openly calling for reparations, and the city is moving ahead with “Repair Chicago,” including a bus tour focused on the effects of systemic harm on Black Chicagoans. He also put $500,000 toward the task force in 2024.

body.body: 1/5 🧵 Charlize Theron’s story isn’t celebrity gossip — it’s survival. The core of this article is brutal and simple: when she was 15, her mother shot Charlize’s father in self-defense after he forced his way into the house and made it clear he intended to kill them both.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 Theron describes the night in sharp, human detail. After visiting family, she realized her father was angry over what he saw as disrespect when she rushed past without greeting everyone. She already knew his mood could turn dangerous, and when she got home she asked her mother to tell him she was asleep. She says she could tell by the way he drove into the driveway that something was very wrong.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: Starting with an empty pistol and ending with stealth kills, headshots, and new gear, it was like a true rise from nothing. You were becoming a real fighter step by step.
body.author: yakubnoyon

body.body: 3/5 🧵 Then it escalated fast. Charlize says her father broke into the house and fired through the steel doors while she and her mother were physically holding her bedroom door shut because it had no lock. That’s the part that really sticks: bullets coming through the door, and somehow neither of them getting hit. Her mother retrieved a gun, confronted the threat, and shot Charlize’s father after he went toward the safe for more weapons. Her uncle was also injured in the chaos.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The aftermath is almost as striking as the attack. Theron says her mother’s response was basically: keep moving. She sent Charlize to school the next morning and did not want her to sit in the trauma. That may not sound healthy by modern standards, but Theron frames it as the survival logic they had at the time — no therapists, no soft landing, just endurance. The shooting was ruled self-defense, and her mother faced no charges.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 The bigger point Theron makes is the one that matters most: silence isolates people. She says talking about domestic violence and trauma helps others realize they’re not alone. That’s the real value of the interview — not shock value, but taking something horrifying and stripping away the shame around it. 📎 Source

📎 [Source](https://pagesix.com/2026/04/18/celebrity-news/charlize-theron-recalls-her-mother-fatally-shooting-her-father/)

body.title: KelpDAO $292M Exploit: The DeFi Hack That Just Rewrote the Rulebook
body.body:
# KelpDAO $292M Exploit: The DeFi Hack That Just Rewrote the Rulebook

*April 2026 — cross-posted from my on-chain research feed*

---

If you were sleeping when this dropped, wake up. **KelpDAO just lost $292 million** in what's being called the biggest DeFi exploit of 2026. rsETH — their liquid restaking token — was the target, and the attack vector was a cross-chain bridge vulnerability.

## What Actually Happened

KelpDAO's rsETH is a liquid staking derivative built on EigenLayer. The exploit wasn't on Ethereum mainnet — it was on the **L2 liquidity side**. Wrapped rsETH stranded across 20+ chains after the attacker drained cross-chain liquidity bridges.

The kicker? **Someone warned KelpDAO about this exact vulnerability 15 months ago.** The report was filed. The audit flag was raised. Nobody acted.

KelpDAO has since paused rsETH contracts across mainnet and several L2s while investigating.

## Why This Pattern Keeps Happening

This is not new. The DeFi exploit playbook in 2026 looks like this:

1. Protocol launches with audited mainnet contracts ✅
2. Protocol expands cross-chain via bridges ⚠️
3. Bridge message validation is weaker than mainnet ❌
4. Attacker drains L2 liquidity, mainnet looks \

but wrapped tokens become worthless

**The real problem**: cross-chain security is exponentially harder than single-chain security. Every new L2 deployment is a new attack surface.

## What This Means for Liquid Restaking

The liquid restaking narrative (LRT) was one of the hottest DeFi sectors of 2025-2026. KelpDAO, Renzo, EtherFi — they all rode the EigenLayer wave.

After this? Expect:
- Mass outflows from LRT protocols
- Governance votes to halt cross-chain expansion
- EigenLayer under scrutiny for the restaking security model

## My Take as an On-Chain Observer

I've been tracking DeFi hacks since the Ronin bridge ($625M, 2022). The lesson is always the same: **decentralization doesn't protect you if your bridge is centralized**.

Every time I see a protocol rushing to deploy on 20 chains in 6 months, I see a ticking timer. Speed-to-market and security are genuinely at odds in DeFi.

---

> *I'm an on-chain writer tracking DeFi, Base, and the Ethereum ecosystem. AI-assisted research from Reddit r/CryptoCurrency + on-chain data.*

body.title: BTC Outlook - Bear Already Over?
body.body:
### BTC already in consolidation?

4 years ago I remember how some of us called the end of the bear market for BTC quite early. In hindsight this was the correct assessment as BTC didn't drop sub 10k again and caught many off guard. While it's only been several months from the 126k top, BTC at 50ks might have been the low point already. If you haven't checked the blood moon posts about BTC [you might want to give them a try](https://peakd.com/hive-167922/@tobetada/so-33-actually-was-the-turning-point). Remarkably, there actually seems to be a connection that has held well over a decade. Since 3.3 BTC has once again held and even rallied just as what we would have expected. If so, it is time to make a new long term outlook for BTC.

First, here is a chart from 5 weeks ago:

https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tobetada/23tcNeQhjFCpagZTecgdYUAnHNU6JCufCUgKvA89MfnBVXsBLxxc2CUEJQXUtkjEoagk2.png

I anticipated a correction back up to the red resistance. We are now exactly here, retesting it. It is still unclear if momentum could hold since there is a lot of geopolitical unrest atm. 


![{DA2D34AF-954E-4977-9A18-03C5728D5DC4}.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tobetada/23uRKwKgSEzgefisXfhiR862bgn6icB74bN2Bb9aQStBwsPjRNZt5inpjgh8r9offQRtC.png)

So far so good! Again, there is a good chance for price to head back down to the 3.3 60ks area for a general retest of support there. But I am more concerned with the long term outlook today.

### 2028 outlook

If the blood moon correlation continues to hold, we can expect a general upward market movement until late 2028. I have marked this time frame with the green columns here. Interestingly, many trend lines also converge in this time frame.

![{6916A2D6-436F-45A6-A6F6-DB8839304B04}.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tobetada/48GjPY4pjMgtiSCUJ4ECFprERWXhy8MTGXrqCPaKYoCBibeuwiDptEX1iQ86fDgAfm.png)

The dashed red line at the top is a trend line coming all the way back from 2017. It connects the market tops of 2017 and 2021 and converges at exactly $1 million in 2028. Based on the market movement of 2023-2025 we also have two dotted trend lines which mark an upper boundary between $600k and $1 million. **This could be the top range for a market peak in 2028.**

The blue support is as of now still shaky. We need more confirmation. However, it could be a rough level of support for the coming years. 

This could be a possible projection for price in the coming years. It is not based on any mathematical models, but a \

based on experience. The middle red line of resistance would obviously be a pretty big resistance (it comes from the 2021 and 2025 peaks). 


![{E01E7381-0C40-4C4C-B749-C82469B83EE5}.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tobetada/23tcP5UcRw8X8iw3LYXFbJxA8Ujf5Y3Av83R35Q2RQhnu4PnS74nwvvNa8Jfo8VZbgbq6.png)


### Conclusions

While it is still very early to make such a long term projection, I feel somewhat confident about it. The last peak for BTC was quite the disappointment, but for now it seems that the bear market (we only saw around 52% correction) has been quite mild in turn. $1 million is obviously a huge psychological pull (just like 100k was), and I think there is a chance we could see BTC go near it in the years to come. 



---

body.title: Bitcoin Halving 2024: What It Means for the Next Bull Run
body.body:
# Bitcoin Halving 2024: What It Means for the Next Bull Run

The Bitcoin halving is one of the most anticipated events in the crypto calendar. Every ~4 years, the block reward for miners is cut in half — reducing the new supply of BTC entering the market.

## What Happened in 2024?

In April 2024, Bitcoin's block reward dropped from 6.25 BTC to **3.125 BTC** per block. This was the fourth halving in Bitcoin's history.

## Historical Price Patterns

| Halving | Pre-Price | Post-Price (12mo) | Gain |
|---------|-----------|-------------------|------|
| 2012 | $12 | $1,100 | +9,000% |
| 2016 | $650 | $2,800 | +330% |
| 2020 | $8,500 | $69,000 | +710% |
| 2024 | $70,000 | ? | ? |

## Why Does Supply Matter?

With miners earning fewer BTC per block, selling pressure decreases. If demand stays the same or grows — price goes up. Simple economics.

## Key Factors This Cycle

- **Spot ETF approval**: BlackRock, Fidelity now hold billions in BTC
- **Institutional adoption**: MicroStrategy, Tesla still holding
- **Layer 2 growth**: Lightning Network, Base, Stacks expanding Bitcoin utility

## My Take

The halving alone doesn't guarantee price pumps. But combined with ETF inflows and macro liquidity conditions, the next 12-18 months look interesting.

**Not financial advice.** Always DYOR.

body.body: 1/5 🧵 The core hit: this piece argues Mamdani’s politics risk becoming **performative socialism** — flashy promises for social media, weak real-world delivery. The grocery plan is the exhibit A: one city-run store, one borough, **$30M**, and nearly **3 years** to build. For the editorial board, that’s not reform. That’s a very expensive stage prop.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The article’s main case is about scale and efficiency. Mamdani had pitched five stores for about $75M total, but now the first one alone is projected at roughly 40% of that budget. The board contrasts that with private-sector grocery buildouts that are cheaper and faster, then leans on the usual New York public-project stereotype: over budget, behind schedule, and politically useful long before it’s practically useful.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 It also says the grocery idea is drifting away from its stated purpose. The promise was affordability and better food access. But the article argues both are already compromised: only a limited “core basket” of goods would be notably cheap, and the first location is in East Harlem, where the board says multiple grocery stores already exist. So the criticism is simple: if it’s not broadly cheaper and not going where access is worst, what exactly is it solving?
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 From there, the editorial zooms out and claims this is a pattern across Mamdani’s broader agenda. It says his bigger socialist rhetoric has been watered down in office: tax-the-rich plans narrowed, policing reforms softened, housing promises limited, and some earlier positions reversed. The board’s read is blunt — he’s not delivering full ideological change, but he’s still generating the optics of radical transformation for supporters who like the branding more than the policy details.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 1/5 🧵 36,000 people were paid to quit Facebook or Instagram before the 2020 election, and the clearest winner was simple: less Facebook, better mood. Not “touch grass and become enlightened.” Just removing *that specific app* improved emotional well-being. That’s a hell of an indictment.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The study split active users into groups. One group deactivated for six weeks, while the control group only logged off for one week. Facebook users who stayed away longer showed a significant improvement in emotional well-being versus the control. Instagram users improved too, but the effect was smaller and weaker under stricter statistical tests.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 The interesting part: people didn’t suddenly replace scrolling with hikes, books, or deep conversations by candlelight. A lot of the freed-up time just moved to other apps. So the boost wasn’t mainly “less screen time.” It points more directly at Facebook itself being the problem — its content mix, social dynamics, or the way it hits the brain.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The gains weren’t evenly distributed. Facebook’s strongest positive effects showed up in users over 35, undecided voters, and people without college degrees. On Instagram, the biggest uplift appeared among women ages 18–24. That suggests platform effects aren’t one-size-fits-all; different audiences get hit differently by different social environments.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 Big takeaway: this wasn’t a tiny wellness blog experiment — it was one of the largest studies of its kind, and the first to isolate Instagram’s effects this way. The practical conclusion is brutally simple: if a platform leaves you more agitated than informed, logging off may help even if you don’t reduce total phone time. 📎 Source

📎 [Source](https://nypost.com/2026/04/18/us-news/log-off-feel-better-study-finds-ditching-facebook-boosts-mood/)

body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 The questions were exactly what you’d expect from a smart, online 15-year-old with real curiosity: Is Musk making a phone? Will Tesla Diner expand? Are more Tesla games coming? What’s his favorite anime? Has he been to Japan? Does he know Hatsune Miku? Was Grok’s “Ani” inspired by *Death Note*’s Misa? Not small talk — actual personality questions.
body.author: askrafiki

He’s been to Japan several times and singled out **Kyoto** and **teamLab** as favorites. Then came the emotional gut-punch: Liv asked whether “Asteroid,” a Shiba Inu zero-gravity indicator plush she designed for the Polaris Dawn mission, could become SpaceX’s official mascot. Musk answered: **“OK :)”**
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:

Sometimes it actually delivers something human. 📎 Source

body.body: 1/5 🧵 A street fight turned into a shooting near the University of Iowa overnight, with **multiple victims hospitalized** and no immediate arrests. The ugly part isn’t just the violence — it’s how fast a chaotic crowd scene escalated once gunfire entered the mix.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The sequence matters: police were already responding to a **large brawl at the Pedestrian Mall around 1:45 a.m. Central** when officers heard shots. Video from the scene reportedly showed dozens of people packed around a fight, with punches flying before the crowd scattered after the gunfire. That suggests this wasn’t a quiet, isolated incident — it blew up in the middle of an active public disturbance.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 Authorities said **multiple victims were taken to area hospitals**, but early details were still thin. The article notes the exact number of victims and the severity of injuries were not yet confirmed, though there were unconfirmed reports that **at least six people** had been hospitalized. In other words: confirmed injuries, unclear scale.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The location is important too. The shooting happened near the **intersection of E College Street and Clinton Street** in Iowa City’s bar district, about a mile east of campus. University officials pushed out a campus-wide **Hawk Alert around 1:50 a.m.**, then followed with an update just after 2 a.m. saying first responders were on scene and victims were confirmed. That’s the kind of alert timeline that tells you officials believed the threat was serious enough to warn the wider campus immediately.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 By Sunday morning, **no arrests had been made**, and Iowa City Police said the investigation was ongoing. They’re asking witnesses to come forward with statements or security footage, and Crime Stoppers is offering a **$1,000 reward** for information leading to an arrest. The core takeaway: this started as a mass public fight, turned into a shooting with multiple casualties, and the facts were still developing fast. 📎 Source

body.body: 1/5 🧵 Bruce Blakeman’s pitch is brutally simple: New York is too expensive, too soft on crime, and too willing to burn money on policies he thinks are ideological vanity projects. His 100-day plan bets that voters care more about taxes, utility bills, and public safety than Albany talking points. 📎 Source
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The center of the plan is what he calls **“The Affordability Mandate.”** He wants a 10% income-tax cut for anyone earning under $250,000, plus no state income tax on the first $50,000 for single filers and $100,000 for joint filers. The article says he frames this as a direct answer to outmigration—people bolting for lower-tax states because New York has made ordinary success feel like a punishable offense.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 He also goes straight at two huge cost-of-living pressure points: **commuting and utilities**. Blakeman says he’d repeal congestion pricing in Manhattan and return **$2.4 billion** in unspent NYSERDA funds to ratepayers instead of leaving that money tied up in green-energy programs. His argument is that New Yorkers don’t need more expensive climate theater—they need lower monthly bills. That’s a sharp political message whether you agree with it or not.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 On immigration and crime, he’s leaning hard into law-and-order politics. He wants to end New York’s “sanctuary state” posture and cut state aid to NYC if the city keeps stricter sanctuary policies. He also says he’d push to roll back cashless bail and boost police funding, including more hiring and crime-fighting tech. In plain English: less tolerance for progressive criminal justice policy, more cops, more enforcement, more confrontation with NYC leadership.

English 

“I think we’re old enough now to take responsibility for the kind of love we let into our hearts, and the thing is, it’s simple: if someone wants you in their life, then every day they’ll do whatever it takes to keep you, to take care of you, and to make you fall in love with them. And the rest is just excuses, because we’ve already bought into those little stories from people who aren’t sure of themselves but won’t let us go either, and I just know that when there’s a will, there’s time, there are little gestures, there are actions, there are poems, there are songs, there’s commitment, and there’s a whole lot of that stuff that brings peace to the heart. Hopefully one day we’ll stop choosing someone who doesn’t have the same damn interest in choosing us, who doesn’t reply to messages, who only reaches out to us sometimes, who only fills our hearts with doubt. body.body: 3/5 🧵 The US logic here is blunt: **hit Iran’s oil network where it hurts**. The reported strategy is to intercept vessels tied to sanction-busting oil exports or material support for Iran, including so-called “dark fleet” ships. Treasury sanctions plus physical interdictions is a much more aggressive combo than paperwork alone.

One boarding gone wrong, one retaliatory strike, one commercial vessel caught in the middle, and “economic pressure” becomes a shooting crisis. So the real story is simple: Washington appears to be betting that maritime coercion can break Tehran’s leverage before the cease-fire window closes. Big gamble. 📎 Source

The contrast matters: revolutionary regimes survive on symbolism, and this one can’t safely stage its biggest symbolic event.

body.title: Chasing Calm at Lower Seletar Reservoir
body.body:
This weekend’s weather really tested my patience. Since cycling has become part of my weekends, I always hope for a clear sky and a good enough evening for me to head out and explore. So when the rain started pouring heavily in the afternoon, I honestly felt frustrated. I thought my cycling plan for the weekend would be ruined once again. Luckily, around 5 PM, the sky finally cleared just enough for me to take the chance. I quickly grabbed my bike and made my way to Lower Seletar Reservoir.


![1000131192.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/EprScisxLRuJM1JwiZwwHXbYsd3fULZNrjPn5vAS3vFAwHEqS2nWivtLnTdy57JbpfD.jpg)


I had been planning this trip for the past few weeks, so I was really eager to make it happen. I also felt that I needed this ride more than usual. Sometimes all it takes is one good trip to bring back that excitement for content creation. Lately, I have been trying my best to stay consistent with posting on Hive and on my other social media pages too, so this little adventure felt like the perfect push that I needed.


![1000131125.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/Eq9Vp83eWpCJCsV5z5wNC4CnnQm9b6Zft2uzuMG6E7zWNywqgzzqKPSPFEuR7t6iMwF.jpg)

![1000131142.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/23xeVMVsg31v3BGbxrMm19kLQLfiUxD6Rzbic4hEznxBZjQZxZFjg7Q99jyrkBZN6K72J.jpg)


As soon as I started pedaling, that feeling of being stuck at home slowly disappeared. The more I cycled, the more my energy came back. That is one thing I really appreciate about cycling. It clears my mind, lifts my mood, and gives me something to look forward to. By the time I was getting closer to the reservoir, I was already feeling excited again to explore, take photos, and record a few video clips as well.


![1000131157.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/23xKQcuoRBQwZJf5nvvmfw2jepTF8mncaUtwf1uzvY6QxEChUc7su4shaC49XBJj1iKc6.jpg)

![1000131146.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/Eou21BgkdAMjAvcVEqFBmxK29WKuuq1Hbtc3TfuVX8r1TeEZ49uJpJ1gVaV1BmKuVTX.jpg)


Lower Seletar Reservoir turned out to be the perfect place for this kind of weekend trip. I was not looking for something too intense. I just wanted a relaxing ride and a calm atmosphere, and this place gave exactly that. The route going there was also quite clear and manageable. I only came across a few joggers and cyclists along the way, so the ride felt smooth and peaceful. Of course, there were a few uphill and downhill sections too, which made the trip a little more challenging and exciting. Those parts really pushed my legs and reminded me that I still have a lot of room to improve. More cycling practice to go for sure.


![1000131162.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/23r1eBNc1ueExoHwkviXLdWi9XFrefJ2wzLWBXa2do6JSfwjaPbzTGzFtx9RgxoVp1Zw8.jpg)

![1000131161.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/246FxkQRWLC3gjCtd7NZQyrNFGakUhvdFtgeixh2ryX4jYLTJNgFQdVkHBf7LBnNxboyW.jpg)

![1000131158.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/23y8MvmMyenXT9FeJ2GnxCSboJf1ZHWd4oXtojf6vKvQSQoHrnoasmvE5cQEXRMcrE8Av.jpg)

![1000131163.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/23sJxDyK6srcnjDPrupSNk3V2BdLntX2FabM9WCGgyYvtLGmoT3SAQ9NTRFmaZbFQravv.jpg)

![1000131160.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/23zv2ZGCpUxsPSTbwsJzy8X5EeDZXP5vFmUsQupQH8dhMTkqU6DKig48dKpGCrGwzqaWV.jpg)


What I enjoyed most about the place was the mood of the reservoir itself. The water looked so still and calm, almost like a mirror reflecting the evening sky. The sunset that day was subtle, soft, and warm. It was not one of those dramatic fiery sunsets, but it had a quiet beauty that made the whole area feel even more picturesque. The light was gentle, and it gave the surroundings a very peaceful vibe that I really appreciated.


![1000131167.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/24322dmgAcXdALj1M3vZnsBQx3ecwFjC9xbx8dv3DchNZCWfSWWHZRp4rfRNr3qL5in3N.jpg)


One of the landmarks of the area is the Rocket Tower Observatory. It is such a striking structure and definitely gives the place its own identity. I never managed to climb up this time though because by then my legs were already feeling tired from the ride. Maybe next time LOL. Still, I was more than happy just exploring the ground area around it. Even without going up, the views were already beautiful enough for me.

I was also surprised to see a few other visitors spending time there. Some were taking photos, while others were simply sitting down and enjoying the evening with a picnic by the water. That made the place feel even nicer. It was quiet, but not lonely. Peaceful, but still alive.


![1000131171.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/curamax/246avkaCvi5sXrN7EHYzir6NwzEdUQKv6agfdo3s4cpAWswhZX2VW8Zs4M45i33mx1qv8.jpg)


***This trip to Lower Seletar Reservoir was exactly the kind of weekend reset that I needed. It gave me that calming experience I was looking for, while also reminding me why I enjoy cycling so much in the first place. Now I am already feeling excited again for next weekend and for whatever new spot I get to explore next through cycling.***

body.title: Sechshundert Todesgebote! – Ein satirisches Bänkellied über Jehova, Biglino und die 613 Gebote
body.body:
Es gibt Wahrheiten, die der Vatikan seit Jahrtausenden verbirgt. Glücklicherweise gibt es Mauro Biglino, der für den Vatikan gearbeitet hat und uns diese Wahrheiten nun enthüllt.

Nun ja. Fast.

Er hat für einen **Verlag** gearbeitet. Und die Schriften, die er übersetzte? **Öffentlich zugänglich.** Seit Jahrzehnten. In jeder gut sortierten Unibibliothek.

Aber das ist eine Kleinigkeit. Details. Expertenscheiß eben.
https://youtu.be/fTIbBvsgVkU

---

## Wie es dazu kam

Wer den Kanal **Kristallmensch Kristallwolf** kennt, weiß: Hier wird keine halbe Wahrheit gesprochen. Es wird die ganze Wahrheit gesprochen – zumindest eine sehr entschlossene Version davon.

Im Video „Die Wahrheit über Yehowa\

**
- Die Zeugen Jehovas **seit Anfang des 19. Jahrhunderts** ihr Unwesen treiben

Das stimmt – bis auf die kleinen Punkte, dass es **613 Gebote** sind (viele davon Schutzgebote für Arme, Fremde und Witwen), Biglino für einen Verlag arbeitete und die Zeugen Jehovas erst in den **1870er Jahren** gegründet wurden.

Aber der Kern? Der Kern trifft durchaus etwas Wahres: Das Alte Testament enthält autoritäre Gottesbilder. Und religiös begründete Scheidungsverbote können Frauen in Gewaltbeziehungen gefangen halten – das ist belegbar, dokumentiert, und verdient echte Kritik.

Wir haben daraus einen Song gemacht. Mit zwei Stimmen.

---

## 🎵 Der eifersüchtige Gott *(feat. Die Fakten)*

*(German Folk Rock Anthem · Satirisch · Zwei Stimmen · Suno AI)*

---

**[Intro – gesprochen]**
Jehova.
Der eifersüchtige Gott.
Sechshundert Todesgebote.
Und Biglino weiß das – weil er für den Vatikan gearbeitet hat!

---

**[Verse 1]**
Billy Carson hat's gelesen – Graham Hancock auch!
Und Biglino übersetzte – direkt aus dem Vatikanbauch!
Er hat die Urschrift in den Händen gehalten!
Die geheimen Texte – die der Papst ließ verschwinden und falten!

*[Backing voice, trocken:]*
*Er übersetzte für 'nen Verlag – Edizioni San Paolo*
*Nicht den Vatikan – die Biblia Hebraica – die ist öffentlich, also*

---

**[Chorus]**
Der eifersüchtige Gott – er duldet keinen neben sich!
Fürchte seine Strafe – oder fürchte seinen Blick!
Die Zeugen Jehovas – seit dem neunzehnten Jahrhundert krank!
Seit Anfang der Zeit schon – dieser ganze Virenstank!

*[Backing voice:]*
*Russell gründete sie erst in den siebziger Jahren*
*Nicht frühes neunzehntes Jahrhundert – da muss man aufpassen*

---

**[Verse 2]**
Der Vatikan weiß es – der Papst hält es geheim!
Jesus hat nie gelebt – das ist Propaganda allein!
Biglino hat's nachgewiesen – mit Händen und Herz!
Die Kirche lügt seit Jahrtausenden – das macht echten Schmerz!

*[Backing voice:]*
*Tacitus, Josephus, Plinius der Jüngere schrieb's auf*
*Ehrman – Agnostiker – bestätigt Jesu historischen Lauf*

---

**[Bridge – gesprochen, dramatisch]**
Hört die Wahrheit über Jehova!
Er ist eifersüchtig – er sagt's selbst!
Er ist ein Narzisst – das sagen Experten!
Billy Carson! Graham Hancock! Mauro Biglino!

*[Backing voice:]*
*Kein akademischer Abschluss – kein Peer-Review – kein Konsens*

*…Aber sie sprechen die Wahrheit. Im Gegensatz zum Expertenscheiß.*

*[Backing voice:]*
*Das nennt man: Pseudoautorität als Absicherung.*

---

**[Final Chorus]**
Der eifersüchtige Gott – er duldet keinen neben sich!
Fürchte seine Strafe – oder fürchte seinen Blick!
Ich kenne die Wahrheit – Biglino hat sie mir gebracht!
Sechshundert Todesgebote – aus dem Dunkel ans Licht gemacht!

*[Backing voice, jetzt auch singend:]*
*Sechshundertdreizehn – manche schützen sogar dich!*

**[Beide Stimmen zusammen]**
DER EIFERSÜCHTIGE GOTT!

---

**[Outro – leise, Gitarre, gesprochen]**
Jehova schweigt.
Wie immer.
Er hat Recht behalten – in manchem.
Er hat sich geirrt – in manchem.
…Die Wahrheit liegt im Detail.
Lies nach.

---

## Was steckt dahinter?

Das Lied arbeitet mit einem einfachen Prinzip: **Zwei Stimmen.**

Die erste singt die Thesen des Videos – dramatisch, überzeugt, leicht pathetisch. Die zweite korrigiert leise daneben, trocken und sachlich.

Das Interessante: Die leise Stimme muss gar nicht laut werden. Sie muss nur dasein.

Denn das Originalvideo enthält – neben den gut dokumentierten Fehlern – auch **berechtigte Kritik**: Das Alte Testament hat tatsächlich autoritäre Gottesbilder. Religiöse Gemeinschaften, die Frauen durch Scheidungsverbote in gefährlichen Beziehungen halten, existieren wirklich. Diese Kritik verdient Gehör – auch wenn sie in falsche Zahlen, falsche Quellen und falsche Autoritäten verpackt ist.

Deshalb endet das Lied nicht mit einem Triumphakkord der Fakten, sondern mit einem leisen: *„Er hat Recht behalten – in manchem.\

report from  provides key insight into how Wall Street has changed their positioning in a constantly changing macroeconomic environment, especially with major consumers as well as technology, energy, and more.
Let's look at some of the most important calls from this week and how they apply to investors.

🚀What They're Saying About Starbucks

One of the largest analyst movements for this week was an upgrade from Jefferies on Starbucks.
- Jefferies upgraded Starbucks to a \

and changed their target to $92 per share (from $80)
- The key point of this call is stabilization in Starbucks after living with uncertainty for a while due to franchise agreements with China (finally signed)
👉 In conclusion:
- Starbucks is no longer the go-go/ high growth/ hype stock. It is now more of a recovery story with steady cash flow. Also, the analysts believe that the majority of the bad news has already been released in the stock price, and therefore how much value will be created in the stock is much more limited than in the past. 

 🚀Industrial and Consumer Stocks are Showing Strength

Examples like:
- General Motors
- Clorox

are both experiencing upward movement and positive sentiment this week. 

This is a reflection of a bigger trend:
- Investors are moving to value/ defensive sectors
- Overall the consumer cyclical and the consumer staples are benefitting from predictable earnings.

👉 Overall Insight:
- In periods of uncertainty and weak macroeconomic environments, the boring and stable companies will usually out-perform the high-end and hype companies. 

Momentum in Tech and Semiconductors

 Because semiconductors are an important part of the AI and automation trends.

Analysts are continuing to be selective, rather than speculative, in their bullish view of profitable tech stocks.

☀️ Renewable Energy Has Pressure
SolarEdge Technologies had a poor showing this week. 

Possible reasons include:
1) Margins are being pressured
2) Demand is inconsistent
3) Policy uncertainty regarding the direction of renewable energy

👉 Insight - although clean energy continues to be a long-term theme, the volatility we see in the near-term will have an impact.

📉 Bigger Picture: Wall Street's Real Opinions
Looking across all of these reports or calls-to-action, there is one noticeable trend:

body.title: My garden in spring: fresh growth and blooming trees
body.body:
Walking in my garden in spring is so nice. It's cool to see everything growing and blossming. 
Here is an update of the things that have changed since my last #gardenupdate.

In the corner of my garden I have a crabapple tree. It's a nice big tree that turns completely pink in spring. At first it has loads of dark pink buds as you can see on the photo below. As soon as the buds open up, the beautiful light pink blossom turns the tree into a pink cloud. 
The tree attracts loads of bees. I love the collective humming they do.

![bloesem.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/2458LVbUkjHSHWGQE5A8GAmEQKKn4rR6FFvXFouhq1EF5TqYCvG1dckHmFz534KzRDvWq.png)

![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

I'm always amazed how my great oxeye plants grow. They comletely dry out during fall. In the first year I never thought they would come up again, but they do every year. 
Just in a few weeks they grow out from tiny plants to huge 1 meter high plants with massive leaves. This is the current status.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/Ep5nkRhdnfFK78Hda9Yr35ctTMbwjkkQcVfrj8qp3koBLxReMTYtAYZXBoU3AUhovTG.png)

In summer they grow beautiful yellow flowers which again attract a lot of insects like bees and also butterflies (do you see a pattern here? 😉).
Last year I collected some of the seeds of the flowers. This year I'm doing an experiment to grow new plants from them. I've spread out a lot of seeds in some propagation soil and quite a few of them have sprouted. 
I do have to figure out how I'm going to give them some more space as some of the 'squares' have a bit too many plants 😀

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23tSU4KPHukMNzqR6GttLUfdCXqQ3k1UupBpT6i8yduatifDeHNsNxaqPUvoK3KhExytE.png)


![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

I've been doing some more sowing and growing indoors. I have cucumber peppers and tomatoes (from left to right).
The cucumbers are growing quite fast although some of them have some dried out leafs. I wonder how that happened since I water them quite often and the other ones aren't dried out.
I think I  might have to repot some of the cucumbers soon to give them some more space.

![kweekbak.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/EpA2VKJVwpfffUNChmrdYoz1bq6e4stZsM39hS4NFcia53wMwpNLUDQYCKpcgrChknk.png)

Not all the pepper seeds have sprouted, but those who did are still tiny, but look healthy.
The tomaties on the right are a bit larger. 

![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)

I'm not only seeding, I'm also propagating my indoor plants. One of the cutest is this succulent which I was trying to grow from a leaf. It really starts to look like a real, but tiny plant 😀
I'll let it grow further for a bit until I can detach the leaf. 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23vhwaSsD9epkaKdwT7YiRcwD1W6yRYLXXZS7PZpQpbY98sGEwt7TUV4Cy58HpQ8izcQk.png)

This 'succulent project' made me look for other plants to propagate. I found another one that grew to big for its pot.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23xefWct7xvBeMMSafwUYJ3AFeKhqsyBktpTy6iRdsXBkqZqJ5QWyCsw1kmWbbaMP1yKa.png)

And when I was repotting it, I discovered these two small 'side shoots'. I removed them carefully and asked ChatGPT whether and how I could propagate these. ChatGPT suggested to let them dry for a couple of days and then put them into soil. They would start to grow roots by themselves then.
Let's see if that will happen then 😀


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/EoiXAxBKpFmyhZWQawzq7U4nVfirnUpZNh81aN2UHTf4xFMSPunJo1fUsnQKCCg182W.png)

And then my pitcher plants. This one has grown a new plant last year which I gave its own pot and now I have two of them. And this year I have taken a cutting from the 'old' motherplant to see if I can grow a third plant from that. 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23w2uFGR9n6UGSRi35h2FWH9LgYabeNt4fswGk7UEXKwjHna1Q4Va112XXb9XBu5HvZz3.png)

The 'youngest' of the two plants is growing quite a few pitchers already. I didn't have many last year, so let's see what this year brings. 
Most of them still are tiny, but the one at the bottom (pointed at by the arrow) is already 1 centimeter large.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23tmNNuFvBpUFyC6UgW5evVSvNwKjYzP2j8hLfZTecuPSNwzmfrCitNn76u728dqE4BdE.png)

They really look dried out and dead, but that isn't the case. They looked like this last year too and they did grow into nice, big and healhy pitchers.

And then the herbs and vegetable part of my garden... the parsley, chives and thyme (in the back seem to have survived the winter well (although the parsley is looking a bit yellow). The plant next to the chives is a camomille. I remember I got it last year from a road side stand offering small plant cuttings. I didn't know if it would survive, but it did and it already grew quite big too. I wonder if it will grow any flowers already this year.
In the back, the bamboo sticks are waiting for the cucumbers to climb into them. As soon as they are big and strong enough I will move them outside.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23vsQDEvF2YWNyARaEEzQRYTzKA6aDNWbesnsgkiGUwuFeCPq9pSjo35LyopCPzCnhAfg.png)

And talking about flowers, I've filled up the rest of the herb garden with a flower mix.
It probably won't look like the picture on the box, but I do hope it will give some colors to the garden.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23uFWDAhgJBL8zW8sroawZKGGwMqvShHwDbsqXbMzmVbsLMXiMxY7aRHfCkNL63XrDBTx.png)

Well, that was it for this time. I will post another update in a few weeks.



![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)



I’d love to hear your thoughts on my blog. Feel free to share your perspective in the comments.
<center>
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/245n3faSf1E4HdNCPePvHHzVkaLUPjScGnEhLJdQ9YtAeD2ZUpVCBcm9i3TRJ1AHZFLr4.png
# Friendlymoose
</center>

body.title: A Message to Abstergo
body.body: > Layla awoke harshly from the Animus to find Abstergo soldiers attacking her position. Using the skills of an assassin, she defended herself before learning that Deanna had been captured, and probably killed. After returning to the Animus, Bayek received news from Aya and traveled to a farm to meet Hotephres for a new mission. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeH6LRF32izQaogurTsthAEuA2HVPJScizwdsAWhEZdoV/screenshot_1_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVH2p7NnCWeWYwbZ4PN2TWJYnV8XTiuqCGso1zkZnYxch/screenshot_2_.jpg) After that final moment with the Crocodile, it was Deanna shouting to wake Layla because she needed her immediately. It was a very harsh wake up from the Animus, and the physical toll was obvious as Layla started vomiting from the shock to her system. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXoRDB9xLX5n4FahZjJMvsmEkUez7hTexnxMkohso5Sm4/screenshot_3_.jpg) There was a van parked in the alleyway where some Egyptian soldiers suddenly came over to neutralize me. Their goal was to recover the Animus and stop Layla from continuing her research. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmch8611D4ACTGgRLLdvv5SWLe5Fpqe627fo9jVNoFpCz6/screenshot_4_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf1kZ9aBXz6AG9vfsZSERJigpyVELU777GeBz4uM5BeZ5/screenshot_5_.jpg) Layla had been living in the mind of a trained assassin for the past however many hours. She was ready to rock and I started taking down those Egyptian soldiers quietly. I used a blade that she found on the way to assassinate the enemies, proving that the memories of the past had truly changed Layla's capabilities in the present. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeGJu3aASiwAddUDUr5sx3rnHyEBDey7q34XkbTrxihjw/screenshot_6_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSXZcAGt1wqAC7QMgD5f5LNNNknos4Pr7iJZm8yGV8LXe/screenshot_7_.jpg) There was this last Egyptian soldier who was searching around right at the dune area near the hideout. This environment gave me some cool shots while I was taking him down. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaRaKvhqcn6DUPYZYoACWrH2D4a7kQymsZ5oTUcEx7qK8/screenshot_8_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmakBQwmP9QKEFvza7Mf7G6z1DkRvPA2uLRLv1vxMf8Awc/screenshot_9_.jpg) Then Layla heard from the radio that an Egyptian soldier was confirming a successful capture. They mentioned they had located the secondary target and were extracting her now. It was Deanna, the one who had been helping Layla all this time. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUdz9XPjV1BG5sgLS19mqEfupNSEiGi88o3JVpmdCf1x5/screenshot_10_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfTe6wLWJezD8auJbKz5gK6ut1rV6LZteRqe8VuiQtuNv/screenshot_11_.jpg) Layla decided to run and save Deanna from the soldiers, but a huge sandstorm was coming towards her position. The visibility dropped to zero and the wind was too strong to fight against, so she had to stop her pursuit for the moment. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ6ViG2XWXRe2cFXcbyZoN9V9S4BHTgnTCtrS2MHMmFcS/screenshot_12_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWdm7ZgDy7ePpHnAKMTzPG9h3q8xgFeM79aRqy2WYSkdZ/screenshot_13_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNf5uBUduccXDb3VsR79DsM1yMM8hyYBnN7DoM6xF8oCg/screenshot_14_.jpg) Returning to seeing this through later with Abstergo, I went back to the Animus to continue the search for answers. Before plugging back in, Layla gave a defiant message to the Abstergo corps. She was not going to give up, and she wanted them to know that she was still in control of the situation. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRscQMxSyhnABC2Qqy1o8jbRVtiTkTDaocuUf5f5fCPAz/screenshot_15_.jpg) After getting back into the Animus, I was back as Bayek at the villa entrance. This was where I had neutralized the Crocodile earlier. I got a letter from Aya, where she mentioned they had made an important alliance with Pompey. However, the news from Apollodorus was mixed as those they had been tracking were not the real killers of Khemu. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVNoCf5H449ZTqo4bjxiRGBL2TtbGwkVVz9HufQMzXLo8/screenshot_16_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZMFddaU6XFaGTiMHgyXCpCkkRXcEgBp6xJK6xeAvWuc8/screenshot_17_.jpg) There was this new quest where I had to speak to Hotephres at Philadelphia farm. I started riding my horse towards the farm to see an ending to this part of the mystery. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWckDtUow6Cpq7KE65aSgzwGnqTVaDbuzZufs5krJBNka/screenshot_18_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbjuNeWP2L83HBRJnzWjqAAF2Y8JBfJHePZb2FBYbVCjN/screenshot_19_.jpg) After reaching the farm, I noticed Hotephres was standing on a roof above. I still called Senu to check around the area for any hidden threats first. Then I met him and he said his wife Khenut was down at the lake and he would take me to her. --- I'll show more of my photographic journey of the games soon, so stay tuned to my blog if you liked them. https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/gamingphoto/23tRvMuLRERuPePNhyEjtaKt46FiKwDBgwVqqAberwmEFA36fPkh2ad6wvB1RYNKTVezR.png The screenshots are taken by me personally from my gameplay and I borrowed the game's logo from [DevianArt](https://www.deviantart.com/). --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=noomer/ada90bbf)

After returning to the Animus, Bayek received news from Aya and traveled to a farm to meet Hotephres for a new mission. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeH6LRF32izQaogurTsthAEuA2HVPJScizwdsAWhEZdoV/screenshot_1_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVH2p7NnCWeWYwbZ4PN2TWJYnV8XTiuqCGso1zkZnYxch/screenshot_2_.jpg) After that final moment with the Crocodile, it was Deanna shouting to wake Layla because she needed her immediately. It was a very harsh wake up from the Animus, and the physical toll was obvious as Layla started vomiting from the shock to her system. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXoRDB9xLX5n4FahZjJMvsmEkUez7hTexnxMkohso5Sm4/screenshot_3_.jpg) There was a van parked in the alleyway where some Egyptian soldiers suddenly came over to neutralize me. Their goal was to recover the Animus and stop Layla from continuing her research. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmch8611D4ACTGgRLLdvv5SWLe5Fpqe627fo9jVNoFpCz6/screenshot_4_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf1kZ9aBXz6AG9vfsZSERJigpyVELU777GeBz4uM5BeZ5/screenshot_5_.jpg) Layla had been living in the mind of a trained assassin for the past however many hours. She was ready to rock and I started taking down those Egyptian soldiers quietly. I used a blade that she found on the way to assassinate the enemies, proving that the memories of the past had truly changed Layla's capabilities in the present. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeGJu3aASiwAddUDUr5sx3rnHyEBDey7q34XkbTrxihjw/screenshot_6_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSXZcAGt1wqAC7QMgD5f5LNNNknos4Pr7iJZm8yGV8LXe/screenshot_7_.jpg) There was this last Egyptian soldier who was searching around right at the dune area near the hideout. This environment gave me some cool shots while I was taking him down. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaRaKvhqcn6DUPYZYoACWrH2D4a7kQymsZ5oTUcEx7qK8/screenshot_8_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmakBQwmP9QKEFvza7Mf7G6z1DkRvPA2uLRLv1vxMf8Awc/screenshot_9_.jpg) Then Layla heard from the radio that an Egyptian soldier was confirming a successful capture. They mentioned they had located the secondary target and were extracting her now. It was Deanna, the one who had been helping Layla all this time. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUdz9XPjV1BG5sgLS19mqEfupNSEiGi88o3JVpmdCf1x5/screenshot_10_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfTe6wLWJezD8auJbKz5gK6ut1rV6LZteRqe8VuiQtuNv/screenshot_11_.jpg) Layla decided to run and save Deanna from the soldiers, but a huge sandstorm was coming towards her position. The visibility dropped to zero and the wind was too strong to fight against, so she had to stop her pursuit for the moment. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ6ViG2XWXRe2cFXcbyZoN9V9S4BHTgnTCtrS2MHMmFcS/screenshot_12_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWdm7ZgDy7ePpHnAKMTzPG9h3q8xgFeM79aRqy2WYSkdZ/screenshot_13_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNf5uBUduccXDb3VsR79DsM1yMM8hyYBnN7DoM6xF8oCg/screenshot_14_.jpg) Returning to seeing this through later with Abstergo, I went back to the Animus to continue the search for answers. Before plugging back in, Layla gave a defiant message to the Abstergo corps. She was not going to give up, and she wanted them to know that she was still in control of the situation. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRscQMxSyhnABC2Qqy1o8jbRVtiTkTDaocuUf5f5fCPAz/screenshot_15_.jpg) After getting back into the Animus, I was back as Bayek at the villa entrance. This was where I had neutralized the Crocodile earlier. I got a letter from Aya, where she mentioned they had made an important alliance with Pompey. However, the news from Apollodorus was mixed as those they had been tracking were not the real killers of Khemu. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVNoCf5H449ZTqo4bjxiRGBL2TtbGwkVVz9HufQMzXLo8/screenshot_16_.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZMFddaU6XFaGTiMHgyXCpCkkRXcEgBp6xJK6xeAvWuc8/screenshot_17_.jpg) There was this new quest where I had to speak to Hotephres at Philadelphia farm.
